'''Ryan James McGowan''' (born 15 August 1989) is an Australian [[association football|soccer]] player who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|Livingst}} club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].

He has previously played for [[Para Hills Knights]], [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], [[Shandong Luneng Taishan F.C.|Shandong Luneng Taishan]], [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], [[Henan Jianye F.C.|Henan Jianye]], [[Guizhou Zhicheng]], [[Al-Sharjah]], [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]], [[Sydney FC]], [[Kuwait SC]] and [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]], with loan spells at [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]], [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] and [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].

McGowan has represented Australia at [[Australia national under-17 football team|under-17]], [[Australia national under-20 football team|under-20]], [[Australia men's national under-23 soccer team|under-23]] and at [[Australia men's national soccer team|senior]] levels. McGowan has been officially designated as Socceroo #546 (2012).

==Club career==
===Heart of Midlothian===
McGowan began his career at [[Para Hills Knights]]<ref name="Hearts family">{{cite web | url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/ryan-mcgowan-hearts_2241487_40931 | title=Hearts Profile | publisher=[[Heart of Midlothian F.C.]] | access-date=3 September 2011 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927175226/http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/ryan-mcgowan-hearts_2241487_40931 | archive-date=27 September 2011 }}</ref> and was part of the [[South Australian Sports Institute Football Program|South Australian Sports Institute]],<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.tribalfootball.com/articles/mcgowan-makes-debut-hearts-romp-victory-1062381 | title=McGowan makes debut as Hearts romp to victory | publisher=Tribal Football | work=tribalfootball.com | date=22 August 2010 | access-date=20 August 2012}}</ref> before moving to [[Scottish Premier League]] club [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] in 2006 and was promoted to the first-team in 2008.<ref name = "Hearts family"/> He was the captain of Hearts' under 19 squad<ref name = "Hearts family"/> before making his SPL debut as substitute on 13 May that year in the final league match of the 2007–08 season against [[Gretna F.C.|Gretna]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20080513/gretna-1-hearts-0_2241469_43413 | title=Gretna vs Hearts | publisher=[[Heart of Midlothian F.C.]] | date=13 May 2008 | access-date=3 September 2011 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120924143040/http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20080513/gretna-1-hearts-0_2241469_43413 | archive-date=24 September 2012 }}</ref> Shortly after he signed a five-year contract with the club.<ref name = "Hearts family"/>

After just the one first team appearance he was sent out on loan to Ayr United in October 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tribalfootball.com/hearts-youngster-mcgowan-joins-ayr-united-loan-380801 |title=Hearts youngster McGowan joins Ayr United on loan |publisher=tribalfootball.com|access-date=14 November 2009}}</ref> His debut for Ayr came on 14 October, when he scored one of the goals in a 2–2 draw at home to [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/scot_div_1/8304497.stm | title=Ayr recovered from two goals down to snatch a point against title favourites Dundee | work=[[BBC Sport]] | date=14 October 2009 | access-date=2 February 2014}}</ref> In January 2010, the loan was extended until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20100101/loan-deals-extended_2241384_1919771 | title=Loan deals extended | publisher=[[Heart of Midlothian F.C.]] | date=1 January 2011 | access-date=3 September 2011 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120924143335/http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20100101/loan-deals-extended_2241384_1919771 | archive-date=24 September 2012 }}</ref> In total, he made 30 appearances in all competitions, scoring one goal for Ayr.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.ayrunitedfc.co.uk/player_detail.asp?int_player_id=205 | title=Ayr United Profile | publisher=[[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] | access-date=3 September 2011 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110929191924/http://www.ayrunitedfc.co.uk/player_detail.asp?int_player_id=205 | archive-date=29 September 2011 }}</ref>

On his return under new manager [[Jim Jefferies (footballer)|Jim Jefferies]] he played as a substitute against Hamilton on 21 August 2010,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/8929859.stm | title=Hamilton 0 – 4 Hearts | publisher=[[BBC]] | work=BBC Sport | date=21 August 2010 | access-date=5 January 2012}}</ref> and against Celtic in September.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/8986073.stm | title=Celtic 3 – 0 Hearts | publisher=[[BBC]] | work=BBC Sport | date=11 September 2010 | access-date=5 January 2012}}</ref> On 15 February 2011, he joined First Division team [[Partick Thistle]] on a three-month loan deal<ref>{{cite web | url=http://local.stv.tv/edinburgh/sport/6776-hearts-youngster-ryan-move-sto-firhill/ | archive-url=https://archive.today/20120715151343/http://local.stv.tv/edinburgh/sport/6776-hearts-youngster-ryan-move-sto-firhill/ | url-status=dead | archive-date=15 July 2012 | title=Hearts youngster Ryan moves to Firhill | publisher=Scottish television | date=15 February 2011 | access-date=3 September 2011 }}</ref> and made his debut the same night.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_div_1/9397631.stm | title=Cowdenbeath 1–1 Partick Thistle | publisher=BBC | work=BBC Sport | date=15 February 2011 | access-date=3 September 2011}}</ref> In all he made eight appearances before returning to Hearts at the start of April.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://sport.scotsman.com/top-stories/Football-news-in-brief-Ryan.6743979.jp | title=Ryan McGowan returns to Hearts from Partick | publisher=Scotsman Publication | work=The Scotsman | date=1 April 2011 | access-date=3 September 2011}}</ref> After returning from his loan at Partick, McGowan made six more appearances for Hearts that season,<ref>{{Soccerbase season|46726|2010|access-date=5 January 2012}}</ref> with his first start for Hearts coming on 7 May 2011 against [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]]<ref>{{cite web | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/9476492.stm | title=Rangers 4 – 0 Hearts | publisher=[[BBC]] | work=BBC Sport | date=7 May 2011 | access-date=5 January 2012}}</ref>

On 23 July 2011, he started the 2011–12 season with a Sky Sports 'Man of the Match' performance against [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] at Ibrox.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.skysports.com/football/match_facts/0,19762,11065_3407112,00.html | title=Rangers 1 – 1 Hearts | publisher=BSkyB | date=23 July 2011 | access-date=3 September 2011}}</ref> He began to establish himself as a member of the first team and played in the Europa League qualifiers against [[Paksi SE|Paks]]<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14289918 | title=Paksi 1 - 1 Hearts | publisher=BBC | work=BBC Sport | date=28 July 2011 | access-date=3 September 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14321318 | title=Hearts 4 – 1 Paks (agg 5 – 2) | publisher=BBC | work=BBC Sport | date=3 August 2011 | access-date=3 September 2011}}</ref> and in the second leg against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham]] at [[White Hart Lane]], where Hearts drew 0–0 (losing 5–0 on aggregate).<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14569541 | title=Tottenham 0 – 0 Hearts (agg 5 – 0) | publisher=BBC | work=BBC Sport | date=25 August 2011 | access-date=3 September 2011}}</ref> McGowan scored his first goal for Hearts in an [[Edinburgh derby]] on 2 January.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16330946 | title=Hibernian 1 – 3 Hearts | publisher=[[BBC]] | work=BBC Sport | date=2 January 2012 | access-date=3 January 2012}}</ref> Later in the same game he [[headbutt]]ed [[Ivan Sproule]] in the stomach, which the referee viewed and took no action, however the SFA compliance officer opened an investigation.<ref name = "hibs goal">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16402030|title=Scottish FA to look at incident involving Ryan McGowan of Hearts|work=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=3 January 2012|access-date=3 January 2012}}</ref> The compliance officer offered a two match ban.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16402030 | title=Ryan McGowan faces two-match suspension | publisher=[[BBC]] | work=BBC Sport | date=5 January 2012 | access-date=5 January 2012}}</ref> Hearts denied it was violent conduct but accepted the ban offered.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20120106/ryan-receives-two-match-ban_2241384_2568756 | title=Ryan receives two match ban | publisher=[[Heart of Midlothian F.C.]] | date=6 January 2012 | access-date=6 January 2012 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120108050954/http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20120106/ryan-receives-two-match-ban_2241384_2568756 | archive-date=8 January 2012 }}</ref> The 2011–12 [[Scottish Premier League|SPL]] season was a good one for McGowan, scoring 3 goals – including one in the [[2012 Scottish Cup Final]] victory against [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibs]] – and winning the Hearts Young Player of the Year award.<ref name="Hearts FC">{{cite news|url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20120407/young-player-of-the-year-votes-are-in_2241384_2727151|title=Young Player of the Year votes are in|work=Hearts FC|date=7 April 2012|access-date=7 April 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120410005656/http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20120407/young-player-of-the-year-votes-are-in_2241384_2727151|archive-date=10 April 2012}}</ref>

Ahead of the last day of summer transfer window, [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] made a bid for Hearts duo McGowan and [[David Templeton]] worth combined £1.3m valuation for the duo but the move rejected.<ref>{{cite news|title=Rangers fail in bid for Hearts pair Ryan McGowan and David Templeton|url=http://sport.stv.tv/football/clubs/rangers/188003-rangers-fail-in-bid-for-hearts-pair-ryan-mcgowan-and-david-templeton/|publisher=Sports STV|date=30 August 2012|access-date=11 September 2012|archive-date=5 February 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160205130344/http://sport.stv.tv/football/clubs/rangers/188003-rangers-fail-in-bid-for-hearts-pair-ryan-mcgowan-and-david-templeton/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Templeton went on to join Rangers but McGowan stayed, explaining that he needs to keep his international career status alive.<ref>{{cite news|title=Hearts star Ryan McGowan reveals why he snubbed move to Rangers|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/hearts-star-snubbed-rangers-1318475|work=Daily Record|location=Glasgow|access-date=11 September 2012}}</ref> On 2 January 2013, it was announced that [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] had accepted a bid of around £400,000 from Chinese side [[Shandong Luneng Taishan F.C.|Shandong Luneng Taishan]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20849001 | title=Hearts' Ryan McGowan to discuss Shandong Luneng Taisha move | publisher=[[BBC]] | work=BBC Sport | date=2 January 2013 | access-date=2 January 2013}}</ref> In all, McGowan made 73 appearances for the club.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/ryan-mcgowan/13038/ | title=Soccerway Stats | publisher=Soccerway | access-date=3 September 2011}}</ref>

===Shandong Luneng Taishan===
On 7 January 2013, McGowan signed a two-year contract with [[Chinese Super League]] side [[Shandong Luneng Taishan F.C.|Shandong Luneng Taishan]].<ref name="Hearts hero">{{cite web | url=http://www.scotsman.com/edinburgh-evening-news/football/top-stories/two-year-chinese-contract-for-hearts-hero-ryan-mcgowan-1-2721624 | title=Two-year Chinese contract for Hearts hero Ryan McGowan | publisher=[[Edinburgh Evening News]] | work=The Scotsman | date=7 January 2013 | access-date=7 January 2013}}</ref> He made his Chinese Super League debut for Shandong Luneng Taishan on 9 March 2013 against Dalian Aerbin.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2013/03/09/china-pr/csl/shandong-luneng/dalian-aerbin-fc/1453296/ |title=Shandong Luneng Vs. Dalian Aerbin 1 – 0 |work=Soccerway |publisher=Perform Group |access-date=8 April 2016}}</ref> In his last match for Shandong, he scored the winning goal in the injury time against [[Jiangsu Guoxin-Sainty F.C.|Jiangsu Sainty]] in the second leg of [[2014 Chinese FA Cup]] final.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsports.com.au/football/ryan-mcgowan-scores-95th-minute-goal-to-win-the-chinese-fa-cup-for-shandong-luneng/story-e6frf423-1227132048958?nk=2276b3b69ce874dc51f5ea14ff1ab1de|title=Ryan McGowan scores 95th minute goal to win the Chinese FA Cup for Shandong Luneng|website=Fox Sports|date=23 November 2014|access-date=30 January 2015}}</ref> However, Shandong Luneng decided not to extend his contract at the end of 2014 season.

===Dundee United===
On 23 January 2015, McGowan moved back to Scotland, signing an 18-month contract with [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref>{{cite web|title=AUSTRALIAN INTERNATIONALIST SIGNS ON|url=http://dufc.co/news/australian-internationalist-signs/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150123182403/http://dufc.co/news/australian-internationalist-signs/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=23 January 2015|website=dufc.co|publisher=[[Dundee United F.C.]]|access-date=23 January 2015|date=23 January 2015}}</ref> He made his debut on 31 January 2015, as Dundee United beat Aberdeen 2–1 in the semi-final of the [[Scottish League Cup]] at [[Hampden Park]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dundee United 2-1 Aberdeen|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30963450|work=BBC Sport|last=Wilson|first=Richard|date=31 January 2015|access-date=1 February 2015}}</ref>

===Henan Jianye===
McGowan returned to China on 21 January 2016 after he was transferred from Dundee United to [[Henan Jianye F.C.|Henan Jianye]]. The transfer fee was reported to be approximately £350,000.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Fowler|first1=Craig|title=Ryan McGowan leaves Dundee United for China return|url=http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/latest/ryan-mcgowan-leaves-dundee-united-for-china-return-1-4007366|access-date=21 January 2016|work=Edinburgh Evening News|date=21 January 2016|archive-date=10 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160310025957/http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/latest/ryan-mcgowan-leaves-dundee-united-for-china-return-1-4007366|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his debut by scoring an own goal as [[Shanghai SIPG F.C.|Shanghai SIPG]] beat Henan Jianye 5–0. On 27 January 2017, McGowan was released by Henan Jianye.<ref>{{cite news|script-title=zh:麦克格文宣布离开建业：难忘梦幻一年 想念你们|url=http://sports.sina.com.cn/china/j/2017-01-27/doc-ifxzyxmt1410586.shtml|access-date=27 January 2017|work=sina.com.cn|date=27 January 2017|language=zh}}</ref>

===Guizhou Hengfeng Zhicheng===
One month after leaving Henan Jianye, McGowan joined newly promoted [[Chinese Super League]] club [[Guizhou Hengfeng Zhicheng F.C.|Guizhou Hengfeng Zhicheng]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.fourfourtwo.com.au/news/mcgowan-finds-new-home-452399|title=McGowan finds new home|first=Ben|last=Somerford|newspaper=[[FourFourTwo]]|date=24 February 2017|access-date=23 February 2017|archive-date=21 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170421080725/http://www.fourfourtwo.com.au/news/mcgowan-finds-new-home-452399|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 3 March 2017, he made his debut for Guizhou in a 1–1 home draw against [[Liaoning F.C.|Liaoning FC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.sina.com.cn/china/j/2017-03-03/doc-ifycaafm5033884.shtml|script-title=zh:中超-石笑天染红耶拉维奇点杀 贵州主场1-1辽足|publisher=sports.sina.com|date=2017-03-03|access-date=2017-03-05|language=zh}}</ref>

===Al-Sharjah===
On 21 August 2017, McGowan joined [[UAE Arabian Gulf League]] side [[Al-Sharjah SCC|Al-Sharjah]].<ref>{{cite web|title=UAE club sign the wrong McGowan brother|url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com.au/news/uae-club-sign-the-wrong-mcgowan-brother-471308|publisher=Fourfourtwo|access-date=9 October 2017}}</ref>

===Bradford City===
On 26 January 2018, Ryan joined [[EFL League One]] side [[Bradford City]] from Al-Sharjah for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11745/11221502/bradford-city-set-to-sign-ryan-mcgowan-from-al-sharjah|title=Bradford City set to sign Ryan McGowan from Al-Sharjah|website=Sky Sports}}</ref>

In January 2019 he was linked with a departure from the club, and a return to Scottish football with [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/sport/17395370.bradford-city-mcgowan-linked-with-return-to-scotland/|title=Dundee eye Bantams defender McGowan|website=Bradford Telegraph and Argus|date=30 January 2019 }}</ref> Later that month he moved on loan to Dundee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bradfordcityfc.co.uk/news/2019/january/mcgowan-in-dundee-loan-switch/|title=McGOWAN IN DUNDEE LOAN SWITCH|website=bradfordcityfc.co.uk|date=31 January 2019|access-date=31 January 2019}}</ref>

In May 2019, following Bradford City's relegation to League Two, it was announced that he would leave the club upon the expiry of his contract on 30 June 2019, one of 11 players to be released.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/sport/17623655.bradford-city-announce-retained-list/|title=Bradford City announce retained list|date=7 May 2019|access-date=7 May 2019|author=Simon Parker|publisher=Telegraph & Argus}}</ref>

===Sydney FC===
On 3 July 2019, McGowan signed a two-year contract with [[A-League]] club [[Sydney FC]], while his brother [[Dylan McGowan|Dylan]] earlier joining their derby rivals [[Western Sydney Wanderers FC|Western Sydney Wanderers]].<ref name="McPartlin">{{cite news|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/latest-hearts-news/ryan-mcgowan-joins-sydney-will-face-brother-and-fellow-ex-hearts-player-dylan-mcgowan-in-city-derby-1-4958352|title=Ryan McGowan joins Sydney, will face brother and fellow ex-Hearts player Dylan McGowan in city derby|first=Patrick|last=McPartlin|newspaper=[[Edinburgh Evening News]]|date=3 July 2019}}</ref>

On 3 July 2021, Sydney FC announced that McGowan was leaving the club, having agreed to terms with an overseas club.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sydneyfc.com/news/ryan-mcgowan-departs-overseas-contract|title=Ryan McGowan departs for overseas contract|website=[[Sydney FC]]|date=4 July 2021}}</ref>

===Kuwait SC===
On 7 July 2021, McGowan signed with [[Kuwait Premier League]] club [[Kuwait SC]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.socceroos.com.au/news/aussies-abroad-ryan-mcgowan-moves-kuwait-sc|title=Aussies Abroad: Ryan McGowan seals move to Kuwait SC|website=socceroos.com|date=7 July 2021}}</ref>

===St Johnstone===
McGowan returned to Scottish football in July 2022, signing for [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62271546 |title=Ryan McGowan: St Johnstone sign former Australia and former Hearts defender |website=BBC Sport |date=22 July 2022 |accessdate=23 July 2022}}</ref> He would score his first goal for the ''Saintees'' on 24 May 2023, a last-minute equaliser against [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=County need final-day win after 95th-minute goal |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65618150 |access-date=2023-05-25}}</ref> After two seasons with the ''Saintees'', the club confirmed on 3 July 2024 that McGowan had left the club after the expiry of his contract.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Our thanks to Ryan McGowan and Daniel Phillips |url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/ |access-date=2024-07-03 |website=St Johnstone Football Club |language=en}}</ref>

===Livingston===
In July 2024, McGowan signed for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Welcome to Livingston, Ryan McGowan! |url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/welcome-ryan-mcgowan5/ |date=2024-07-05 |website=Livingston Football Club |language=en}}</ref> McGowan made his competitive debut for the ''Lions'' on 13 July in a victory over [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Forfar Athletic vs Livingston: League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/crgk63zn81xt |access-date=2024-07-13 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 8 February 2025, McGowan scored his first goal for Livi in a [[Scottish Cup]] fifth round victory over [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Livingston vs Cove Rangers: Scottish Cup report, reaction & stats |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/clynz6gj1dxt |access-date=2025-02-08 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 30 March 2025, McGowan won the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] with Livingston, playing the full game in a five-goal hammering over [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Queen's Park vs Livingston: SPFL Trust Trophy final stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cz03vzdrgmpt |access-date=2025-03-30 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Livingston lift SPFL Trust Trophy {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/livingston-lift-spfl-trust-trophy |access-date=2025-03-30 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref> In April 2025, McGowan was one of four ''Lions'' named as part of the [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year#Championship 10|2024–25 PFA Scotland Championship Team of the Year]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Black |first=Dave |date=2025-04-25 |title=PFA Championship Team of the Year 2025 |url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/pfa-championship-team-of-the-year-2025/#:~:text=A%20huge%20well%20done%20to,Championship%20Team%20of%20the%20Year. |access-date=2025-05-03 |website=Livingston FC |language=en-GB}}</ref> In total, McGowan played every minute in all 53 games of the season, and finished off in style by winning the [[2024–25 Scottish Premiership#Premiership play-offs|Scottish Premiership play-offs]] to return the ''Lions'' to the [[Scottish Premiership]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ross County 2-4 Livingston (3-5 agg): Scottish Premiership play-off final second leg - radio & text, BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cpd41v9p65xt |access-date=2025-05-26 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Ryan McGowan.jpg|thumb|right|McGowan with [[Australia men's national under-23 soccer team|Olyroos]] in 2011]]
McGowan was part of the [[Australia national under-20 football team|Australia]] team that [[AFC Youth Championship 2008 qualification#Group G|qualified]] for the [[AFC Youth Championship 2008]] in November 2007.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.footballaustralia.com.au/MensU20/default.aspx?s=aus_u20men_newsfeatures_news_item&id=20232 |title=Qantas Young Socceroos downed by Korea Republic |publisher=Footballaustralia.com.au |date=15 November 2007 |access-date=14 November 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121011105304/http://www.footballaustralia.com.au/MensU20/default.aspx?s=aus_u20men_newsfeatures_news_item&id=20232 |archive-date=11 October 2012 }}</ref> McGowan was selected for the [[2009 FIFA U-20 World Cup]] in [[Egypt]]; his brother and teammate [[Dylan McGowan]], was not selected.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://au.fourfourtwo.com/news/112051,young-socceroos-under-20-world-cup-squad-revealed.aspx |title=Young Socceroos U20 World Cup Squad Revealed |publisher=Au.fourfourtwo.com |date=8 September 2009 |access-date=14 November 2009 |archive-date=30 September 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120930141959/http://au.fourfourtwo.com/news/112051,young-socceroos-under-20-world-cup-squad-revealed.aspx |url-status=dead }}</ref>

McGowan started in the first match for the [[Young Socceroos]] in the [[2009 FIFA U-20 World Cup]], and received a yellow and a straight red against the [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]] for a studs up challenge which resulted in a penalty.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2009/09/27/world/world-youth-championship/czech-republic-u20/australia-youth/873271/ | title=CZECH REPUBLIC U20 VS. AUSTRALIA U20 2 – 1 | publisher=Soccerway | date=27 September 2009 | access-date=3 September 2011}}</ref>

He received his first call-up to the [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia]] senior squad in August 2012, when he was selected for the friendly match against [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]],<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/hearts-defender-ryan-mcgowan-called-up-1235256 | title=Socceroos call-up Jambos ace McGowan for Scotland clash | work=Daily Record|location=Glasgow | date=8 August 2012 | access-date=20 August 2012}}</ref> making his debut as a late substitute replacing [[Sasa Ognenovski]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19243564 | title=Scotland 3–1 | publisher=[[BBC]] | work=BBC Sport | date=15 August 2012 | access-date=20 August 2012}}</ref> McGowan was booed by some sections of the home support due to his Hearts connections,<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scotsman.com/sport/mcgowan-and-black-refuse-to-let-boo-boys-spoil-debuts-1-2470243 | title=McGowan and Black refuse to let boo boys spoil debuts | work=[[The Scotsman]] | date=16 August 2012 | access-date=20 August 2012}}</ref> with the game being played at [[Easter Road]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://news.smh.com.au/breaking-news-sport/mcgowan-inches-closer-to-socceroo-debut-20120814-245ub.html | title=McGowan inches closer to Socceroo debut | work=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] | date=14 August 2012 | access-date=20 August 2012}}</ref>

He was named in Australia's [[2014 FIFA World Cup]] squad and provided the assist to [[Tim Cahill]]'s goal in Australia's 3–2 loss to the [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.socceroos.com.au/news/3-days-go-ryan-mcgowans-fifa-world-cup-story|title=3 days to go: Ryan McGowan's FIFA World Cup story | Socceroos|date=11 June 2018|website=www.socceroos.com.au}}</ref>

==Family and personal life==

His parents emigrated to Australia in 1980, and McGowan was born in [[Adelaide]]<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.ozfootball.net/ark/Players/M/MCA.html#McGowanRyan | title=OzFootball profile | publisher=Australian Player Database | access-date=5 January 2012}}</ref> into a [[Scottish people|Scottish]] family from [[Glasgow]].<ref name = "Hearts family"/> His brother [[Dylan McGowan|Dylan]]<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/spl/interview-ryan-and-dylan-mcgowan-on-their-heartfelt-brotherly-love-1-2694446 | title=Ryan and Dylan McGowan on their heartfelt brotherly love | work=[[The Scotsman]] | date=16 December 2012 | access-date=7 January 2013}}</ref> currently plays for [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]].<ref name="McPartlin"/>

'''Graham Carey''' (born 20 May 1989) is an Irish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who last played for {{Scottish football updater|Livingst}} side [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]]. He plays as a left sided [[attacking midfielder]].

Carey joined [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in 2005 from Shelbourne's youth team and made his Celtic debut in 2009 against Rapid Vienna in the UEFA Europa League, He has played six times for the [[Republic of Ireland national under-21 football team|Republic of Ireland Under 21 team]], having been capped at all International levels from under 15. During his time at Celtic Carey had loan spells with [[Bohemian F.C.|Bohemians]] in the [[League of Ireland]],<ref>[http://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/league-of-ireland/bohemians-hopes-suffer--big-setback--as-carey-loan-deal-ruled-out-1820367.html Bohemians' hopes suffer big setback as Carey loan deal ruled out] Irish Independent, 14 July 2009</ref> [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]]<ref name=Capture>{{cite news |url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11781_5909303,00.html |title=Buddies capture Carey |date=1 February 2010 |access-date=1 February 2010 |publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref><ref name=Andorra1>[http://www.fai.ie/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=2585/ Ireland beat Andorra 3–0 to restore their UEFA qualifying ambitions] FAI, 3 November 2007</ref> and [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]] in [[Football League One|League One]] in England. He then signed for St Mirren permanently and in 2013, moved to [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] where he spent two seasons. After spending four seasons with [[Plymouth Argyle F.C.|Plymouth Argyle]], scoring 49 goals in 200 appearances, he moved to [[First Professional Football League (Bulgaria)|Bulgarian top flight]] club [[PFC CSKA Sofia|CSKA Sofia]] in 2019 for 3 seasons and won the [[Bulgarian Cup]] with them. Carey then returned to Scotland in 2022 with [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] and amassed 117 appearances and 12 goals in 3 seasons with the [[Perth, Scotland|Perth]] side before their relegation. 

In 2010, ex [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] and then [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] manager [[Craig Brown (footballer born 1940)|Craig Brown]], stated Carey "looks a real talent" and said he "is the kind of player fans like to watch".<ref name="heraldscotland.com">[http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/spl/falkirk/craig-brown-gives-his-verdict-on-which-of-the-relegation-candidates-can-steady-the-ship-1.1020996/ Craig Brown gives his verdict on which of the relegation candidates can steady the ship] Herald Scotland, 14 April 2010</ref>

==Club career==

===Celtic===
In 2005, Carey signed for [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] from [[Shelbourne F.C.|Shelbourne]]'s youth set up. He made his senior Celtic debut as a substitute against [[SK Rapid Wien|Rapid Vienna]] in the [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] on 17 December 2009, a match which Celtic drew 3–3.<ref>[http://www.itv.com/sport/football/news/uefacup/matchreports/report-rapid-vienna-v-celtic-728928153.html Rapid Vienna v Celtic] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605093842/http://www.itv.com/sport/football/news/uefacup/matchreports/report-rapid-vienna-v-celtic-728928153.html |date=5 June 2011 }} ITV Sport, 17 December 2009</ref> He was regularly named as a substitute for Celtic in the [[2009–10 Scottish Premier League|2009–10 SPL season]] before being loaned out to [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] in February 2010, and English [[Football League One|League One]] team [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]] in August 2010.

Carey was a regular for the [[Celtic F.C. Reserve and Youth squads|youth team and reserves]] during his time in Glasgow and worked under [[Willie McStay (footballer born 1961)|Willie McStay]], [[Danny McGrain]] and [[Neil Lennon]].<ref>[http://www.celticfc.net/news/stories/news_211209155807.aspx Lennon's Bhoys run riot against Chelsea]{{dead link|date=January 2011}} Celtic FC, 21 December 2009</ref> He later said he was disappointed to have never made it into the first team during his time at Celtic.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/football/you-can-always-go-back-but-you-cant-go-back-all-the-way.23828552 |title=Carey: I was disappointed I didn't break into Celtic's first team, but it's behind me now |publisher=The Scotland Herald |access-date=3 April 2014 |date=29 March 2014}}</ref>

====Bohemians (loan)====
In a bid to get more first team experience for Carey, Celtic boss [[Gordon Strachan]] loaned him out to [[League of Ireland]] Champions [[Bohemian F.C.|Bohemians]] in February 2009. He played his first league match against [[Derry City F.C.|Derry City]] on 13 March and scored his first league goal against [[St. Patrick's Athletic F.C.|St. Patrick's Athletic]] on 11 April.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120223092417/http://www.herald.ie/sport/soccer/fenlon-bemoans-cold-shoulder-from-trap-1651076.html Carey goes on loan to Bohemians] Herald.ie, 24 February 2009</ref> Carey was deemed an instant hit and was described as the star of the show having impressed during the local derby against [[St. Patrick's Athletic F.C.|St. Patrick's Athletic]].<ref name=Instant>[http://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/new-bhoy-carey-an-instant-hit-at-bohs-1708389.html New Bhoy Carey an Instant hit at Bohs] Irish Independent, 15 April 2009</ref>

Bohemians manager [[Pat Fenlon]] was keen to extend Carey's loan deal which expired in July until the end of the season. The talented winger was also due to be out of contract at Celtic in July and was aiming to secure a place in new manager [[Tony Mowbray]]'s team due to impressive performances with Bohemians and the Republic of Ireland under 21s.<ref name=Instant />

Carey was due to play on the left wing in Bohemians' [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] qualifiers against the [[Austrian Football Bundesliga|Austria]] Champions [[FC Red Bull Salzburg|Red Bull Salzburg]], but the loan deal could not be extended in time. He made 20 appearances and scored five goals in all competitions for Bohemians and capped his loan period by winning a League of Ireland Medal.<ref name=Heary /><ref>[http://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/league-of-ireland/euro-blow-for-bohs-as-heary-and-carey-to-miss-salzburg-tie-1831774.html Euro Blow for Bohs as Heary and Carey miss Salzburg tie] Irish Independent, 21 July 2009</ref>

====St Mirren (loan)====
Carey joined [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on loan on 1 February 2010, until the summer of 2010.<ref name=Capture/><ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120801070652/http://www.herald.ie/sport/soccer/bhoys-deal-is-carey-reward-1763170.html|title=Bhoys' deal is Carey reward}} Evening Herald, 5 June 2009</ref><ref>[http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/2010/03/09/st-mirren-star-graham-carey-taking-inspiration-from-ex-celt-jim-o-brien-s-success-at-motherwell-86908-22096772/ St Mirren star Graham Carey taking inspiration from ex-Celt Jim O'Brien's success at Motherwell] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110609175057/http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/2010/03/09/st-mirren-star-graham-carey-taking-inspiration-from-ex-celt-jim-o-brien-s-success-at-motherwell-86908-22096772/ |date=9 June 2011 }} Daily Record, 9 March 2010</ref> He made his debut against [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on 10 February in the [[Scottish Premier League|SPL]]. He came on as a 60th-minute substitute and curled in a free kick which led to the equalising goal for [[Michael Higdon]]. He was described as having "impressed" on his debut.<ref>[http://www.saintmirren.premiumtv.co.uk/articles/20100210/st-mirren-1-st-johnstone-1_2233575_49577 St Mirren 1 St Johnstone 1]{{dead link|date=June 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} St Mirren FC, 10 February 2010</ref> ''Saints'' manager [[Gus McPherson]] said in his post match interview "Graham Carey had some good delivery from the wider area. He's only been with us for a week and we hope he'll be a good addition for us."<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120304002313/http://www.saintmirren.premiumtv.co.uk/articles/20100210/post-match-interviews-v-st-johnstone_2233570_1962206|title=Post Match Interviews v St Johnstone}} St Mirren FC, 10 February 2010</ref>

Carey scored his first goal for St Mirren on 6 March 2010, when he scored from a free kick against [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].<ref>[http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/2010/03/07/rangers-3-st-mirren-1-86908-22091762 Rangers 3 St Mirren 1] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110609195526/http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/2010/03/07/rangers-3-st-mirren-1-86908-22091762/ |date=9 June 2011 }} Daily Record, 7 March 2010</ref> After the match, he said he copied [[Cristiano Ronaldo]]'s free kick technique.<ref>{{cite news |title=I copied Cristiano Ronaldo technique to bag opener at Ibrox, says St Mirren loan star Graham Carey |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/i-copied-cristiano-ronaldo-technique-to-bag-1052439 |publisher=Daily Record |date=7 March 2010 |access-date=14 June 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150708150606/http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/i-copied-cristiano-ronaldo-technique-to-bag-1052439 |archive-date=8 July 2015 }}</ref> A few weeks later, Carey started against Rangers, in the [[2010 Scottish League Cup Final|Scottish League Cup Final]], but the match ended in a 1–0 loss for St Mirren.<ref>{{cite news |title=St Mirren 0 – 1 Rangers |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/scot_cups/8576203.stm |work=BBC Sport |date=21 March 2010 |access-date=14 June 2013 |first=Andy |last=Campbell}}</ref>

Carey scored a 35-yard free kick against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] in the SPL on 3 April, and was commended by the St Mirren manager [[Gus MacPherson]] who said "It was a wonder strike from Graham. When he picks up the ball there's excitement as the crowd sense something may happen. He's always more than capable with his excellent delivery from set-pieces."<ref>[http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/2010/04/04/st-mirren-1-hearts-1-86908-22161282/ St Mirren 1 Hearts 1] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100407204204/http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/2010/04/04/st-mirren-1-hearts-1-86908-22161282/ |date=7 April 2010 }} Sunday Mail, 4 April 2010</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/s/st_mirren/8602184.stm |title=St Mirrens MacPherson hails Graham Carey |work=BBC Sport |date=3 April 2010}}</ref> On 24 April 2010, Carey helped set up the winning goal for [[Andy Dorman]] as St Mirren beat [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] 1–0 and after being substituted, received a standing ovation from the St Mirren fans.<ref>[http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/2010/04/25/st-mirren-1-kilmarnock-0-86908-22210737/ St Mirren 1 Kilmarnock 0] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110609185414/http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/2010/04/25/st-mirren-1-kilmarnock-0-86908-22210737/ |date=9 June 2011 }} Daily Record, 25 April 2010</ref>

Carey won the [[List of Scottish Premier League monthly award winners|SPL Young Player of the Month award]] for April 2010 and St Mirren manager Gus MacPherson added that he was keen to keep him at the club.<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20120304002334/http://www.saintmirren.tv/articles/20100430/gus-pre-match-talk_2233570_2040194/0%2C%2C10295%2C00.html Gus Pre Match Talk]}} St Mirren FC, 30 April 2010</ref> His successful loan spell at St Mirren attracted interest from [[Premier League]] clubs [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]], [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolves]] and [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]] as well as [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] in the [[Football League Championship|Championship]]. He was offered a two-year contract extension by Celtic.<ref>[http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/celtic/2010/05/30/graham-carey-i-d-rather-become-first-team-star-at-celtic-than-make-move-to-english-premier-league-86908-22296775/ Graham Carey: I'd rather become first-team star at Celtic than make move to English Premier League] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100602203911/http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/celtic/2010/05/30/graham-carey-i-d-rather-become-first-team-star-at-celtic-than-make-move-to-english-premier-league-86908-22296775/ |date=2 June 2010 }} Daily Record, 30 May 2010</ref>

====Huddersfield Town (loan)====
On 14 July 2010, Carey signed on loan for [[Football League One|League One]] outfit [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]] until January 2011. Huddersfield boss [[Lee Clark (footballer)|Lee Clark]] said "Graham will bring brilliant versatility to the squad – he can play anywhere up the left side of the pitch.... He has a terrific left foot and he looks as elegant as you would expect from a quality left-footed player".<ref name="Terriers land Bhoys youngster">{{cite news |title=Terriers land Bhoys youngster |url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,12875_6259579,00.html |publisher=Sky Sports |date=14 July 2010}}</ref> Carey made an immediate impact with Huddersfield scoring a low left footed drive from 20 yards against [[Bury F.C.|Bury]] in a pre-season friendly on 19 July 2010.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.examiner.co.uk/huddersfield-town-fc/huddersfield-town-fc-match-reports/2010/07/19/celtic-starlet-helps-huddersfielld-town-draw-with-bury-86081-26879338/ |title=Huddersfield Examiner Celtic starlet helps Huddersfield Town draw with Bury |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120927231439/http://www.examiner.co.uk/huddersfield-town-fc/huddersfield-town-fc-match-reports/2010/07/19/celtic-starlet-helps-huddersfielld-town-draw-with-bury-86081-26879338/ |archivedate=27 September 2012 |work=Huddersfield Daily Examiner |date=19 July 2010}}</ref>

He made his first appearance for the Terriers as a substitute in a 1–0 win against [[Carlisle United F.C.|Carlisle United]] at [[Brunton Park]] in the [[2010–11 Football League Cup|League Cup]]. He made his first League One start in the 4–2 loss against [[Peterborough United F.C.|Peterborough United]] at [[London Road Stadium]]. Carey while playing as a left back, provided an assist to [[Jordan Rhodes]] from a well worked corner and scored a 25-yard free kick to make the score 2–0 to the Terriers.<ref>[http://www.skysports.com/football/match_report/0,19764,11065_3285944,00.html Posh peg back Town in thriller] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100822081702/http://www.skysports.com/football/match_report/0%2C19764%2C11065_3285944%2C00.html |date=22 August 2010 }} Sky Sports, 21 August 2010</ref> On 28 August 2010, he started for Huddersfield against [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]], on the left side of midfield and was awarded Man of the Match for his efforts, including setting up two goals during the match.<ref>{{cite news |title=Huddersfield 3 – 1 Charlton |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_2/8922364.stm |work=BBC Sport |date=28 August 2010 |access-date=14 June 2013}}</ref>

Huddersfield manager [[Lee Clark (footballer)|Lee Clark]] wanted to keep Carey after his loan deal expired in January 2011,<ref>[http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11095_6649460,00.html Clark seeks Carey extension] Sky Sports, 10 January 2011</ref> but despite talks of extending the deal to the end of the season, terms were not agreed, and he returned to Celtic.<ref>{{cite news |title=Carey returns to Hoops |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11719/6660840/ |publisher=Sky Sports |date=13 January 2011 |access-date=14 June 2013}}</ref><ref name=RetCelt>[http://www.htafc.com/page/NewsDetail/0,,10312~2264945,00.html Graham Carey returns to Celtic] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110115044307/http://www.htafc.com/page/NewsDetail/0%2C%2C10312~2264945%2C00.html |date=15 January 2011 }} Huddersfield Town, 13 January 2011</ref> He made 23 starts and three substitute appearances for the [[Yorkshire]] club, scoring two goals.<ref name=RetCelt/>

===Ross County===
After leaving St Mirren, Carey went on trial with [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]<ref>{{cite news |title=McNamara closes in on young English duo |url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/football/mcnamara-closes-in-on-young-english-duo.21466483 |publisher=Herald Scotland |date=2 July 2013 |access-date=31 July 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Transfer news: Graham Carey hoping to land Dundee United contract |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11794/8829016/transfer-news-graham-carey-hoping-to-land-dundee-united-contract |publisher=Sky Sports |date=18 July 2013 |access-date=31 July 2013}}</ref> After three weeks at the club, Carey's trial at Dundee United came to an end after the club were indecisive with their interests signing him.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dundee Utd: Nadir Ciftci closer to deal but Graham Carey misses out |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23425507 |work=BBC Sport |date=23 July 2013 |access-date=31 July 2013}}</ref>

[[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]]<ref>{{cite news |title=Celtic 2 – 1 Ross County |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23474794 |work=BBC Sport |date=3 August 2013 |access-date=12 August 2013}}</ref> In the next game, Carey scored his first goal for the club, scoring with a deflected shot from outside the area, in a 3–1 loss against [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Steven Lawless double helps Partick secure 3–1 win at Ross County |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/aug/10/ross-county-partick-thistle-scottish-premiership |work=The Guardian |date=10 August |title=Ross County assistant Neale Cooper admits he'll have to go into hiding if Staggies win Highland derby against Inverness CT |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/ross-county-assistant-neale-cooper-2529034 |publisher=Daily Record |date=25 October 2014 |access-date=3 July 2015}}</ref>

Ahead of the 2014–15 season, Carey signed a new contract with Ross County on 7 August 2014, just three days before the season started.<ref>{{cite news |title=Carey returns to Ross County] |url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/carey-returns-to-ross-county/ |publisher=SPFL |date=7 August 2014 |access-date=3 July 2015 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304000014/http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/carey-returns-to-ross-county/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Under the new management of [[Jim McIntyre (footballer)|Jim McIntyre]] following the sacking of [[Derek Adams]] after five defeats, Carey played in an unfamiliar role as a left-back.<ref>{{cite news |title=New high-tempo football has Ross County buzzing, says Graham Carey |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/new-high-tempo-football-ross-county-4291528 |publisher=Daily Record |date=20 September 2014 |access-date=3 July 2015}}</ref> He scored his first goal of the season in a 2–2 draw against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on 25 October 2014.<ref>{{cite news |title=St Mirren 2 – 2 Ross County |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29670320 |work=BBC Sport |date=25 October 2014 |access-date=3 July 2015}}</ref> Two weeks later on 8 November 2014, Carey scored his second goal of the season, in a 3–0 win over [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Kilmarnock 0 – 3 Ross County |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29860205 |work=BBC Sport |date=8 November 2014 |access-date=3 July 2015}}</ref>

At the end of the [[2014–15 in Scottish football|2014–15 season]], Carey was released by the "Staggies".<ref>{{cite news |title=Ross County to release 14 players at end of season |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32820578 |work=BBC Sport |date=20 May 2015 |access-date=3 July 2015}}</ref>

===Plymouth Argyle===
On 2 July 2015, Carey signed for [[Football League Two]] club [[Plymouth Argyle F.C.|Plymouth Argyle]] on a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.pafc.co.uk/news/article/take-good-carey-yourself-2524062.aspx |title=Take Good Carey Yourself |publisher=Plymouth Argyle F.C |date=2 July 2015 |access-date=2 July 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150703165444/http://www.pafc.co.uk/news/article/take-good-carey-yourself-2524062.aspx |archive-date=3 July 2015 |url-status=live}}</ref> Carey scored on his debut in a 2–0 win at [[AFC Wimbledon]] on the first day of the season. His scoring run continued with four goals in his first five league games for the club.

Carey enjoyed an excellent first season at [[Plymouth Argyle F.C.|Plymouth]], scoring 12 goals in 46 games and winning the club's Player of the Year award.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/graham-carey-crowned-league-fans-player-year-6/story-29314718-detail/story.html |title=Graham Carey crowned League Two fans' player of the year with more than 7,000 votes |work=Plymouth Herald |date=7 May 2016 |access-date=2 July 2016 }}{{Dead link|date=May 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
Carey was also included into the English League Two Team of the Season for the 2016–17 season, along with teammates [[Sonny Bradley]] and [[Luke McCormick (footballer, born 1983)|Luke McCormick]], after 15 goals and 15 assists in all competitions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/10807996/efl-teams-of-the-season-announced-for-the-sky-bet-championship-league-one-and-league-two|title=EFL teams of the season announced for the Sky Bet Championship, League One and League Two|website=Sky Sports}}</ref>

On 29 June 2017, despite interest from other clubs and speculation that he could move on after his contract expired, Carey signed a new contract at Argyle keeping him at the club where he gained cult status amongst the supporters.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/graham-carey-signs-new-plymouth-argyle-contract/story-30415652-detail/story.html |title=Graham Carey signs new Plymouth Argyle contract |date=29 June 2017 |access-date=29 June 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170629111710/http://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/graham-carey-signs-new-plymouth-argyle-contract/story-30415652-detail/story.html |archive-date=29 June 2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

His 2017–18 season saw Carey transfer his excellent League Two form into League One, particularly during the second half of the season. From the 4–1 victory against [[Oldham Athletic Football Club|Oldham Athletic]] until the defeat to [[Northampton Town Football Club|Northampton]], Carey operated as an inside forward alongside [[Ruben Lameiras]] to great effect. Between them they created more than half of Argyle's goal scoring chances and were directly involved in 26 of the team's 35 goals during that time.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://argyle.life/analysis/turning-the-ship-around-7/ |title=Turning the Ship Around – Part 7: The Creative Void |publisher=Argyle Life |date=9 November 2018 |access-date=24 December 2018}}</ref>

Carey struggled during the first half of the 2018–19 season, with his goal return falling dramatically, however despite the collapse in goals Carey remained an Argyle fan favourite and his drop in form and his inferior performances stemmed largely from a tactical switch by manager [[Derek Adams]], which saw the Irishman operate from wider, deeper positions.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://argyle.life/analysis/is-graham-carey-having-a-bad-season/ |title=Myth busting: Is Graham Carey having a bad season? |publisher=Argyle Life |date=21 December 2018 |access-date=24 December 2018}}</ref>

He was offered a new contract by Plymouth Argyle at the end of the 2018–19 season,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48193378|title=Jamie Ness: Plymouth Argyle release midfielder and offer deals to 12|date=7 May 2019|access-date=8 May 2019|work=BBC Sport}}</ref> but left the club after his contract expired.

In all competitions Carey made 200 appearances, scored 49 goals and assisted a further 58 goals in his time at the club.<ref>{{cite web|title=Graham Carey {{!}} Football Stats {{!}} CSKA Sofia {{!}} Age 32 {{!}} Soccer Base|url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=52219|access-date=23 July 2021|website=www.soccerbase.com}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{cite web|last=Dollery|first=Paul|title=The man providing additional Irish interest in the Europa League from an unlikely source|url=https://www.the42.ie/graham-carey-europa-league-2020-21-5240118-Oct2020/|access-date=23 July 2021|website=The42 |date=22 October 2020 }}</ref>

===CSKA Sofia===
Carey joined Bulgarian club [[PFC CSKA Sofia|CSKA Sofia]] on a free transfer after signing a two-year deal on 11 June 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://cska.bg/index.php?main_page=document_general_info&products_id=8137|title=Ирландецът Греъм Кери подписа с ЦСКА|publisher=cska.bg|date=11 June 2019|language=bg}}</ref> He made his official debut on 9 July 2019, in the 4–0 home win over [[Montenegro|Montenegrin]] club [[OFK Titograd|Titograd]] in a [[2019–20 UEFA Europa League|UEFA Europa League qualifying round]] match.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://topsport.bg/europa-league/tsska-pobedi-titograd-s-4-0-v-mach-ot-parviya-kvalifikatsionen-krag-na-liga-evropa.html|title=ЦСКА победи Титоград с 4:0 в мач от първия квалификационен кръг на Лига Европа|author=Dimitrov, Ivaylo|publisher=topsport.bg|date=9 July 2019|access-date=18 April 2020|language=bg}}</ref> Carey found the net for the first time on 14 December 2019, in the 4–0 victory over [[FC Dunav Ruse|Dunav Ruse]] in a [[Bulgarian First League|league]] game.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2019/12/14/bulgaria/a-pfg/pfc-cska-sofia/dunav-2010-ruse/3032842/|title=CSKA Sofia vs. Dunav Ruse 4:0|publisher=soccerway.com|date=14 December 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}}</ref>

On 19 May 2021, Carey was part of the starting line up as CSKA Sofia beat [[FC Arda Kardzhali|Arda Kardzhali]] 1–0 to win the [[2020–21 Bulgarian Cup]]. The result secured CSKA Sofia's place in the second qualifying round of [[2021–22 UEFA Europa Conference League#Second qualifying round|2021–22 UEFA Europa Conference League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Арда надви Славия и се класира за исторически първи финал за Купата (видео+галерия)|url=https://sportal.bg/news-2021041314390650852|access-date=23 July 2021|website=Sportal.bg|language=bg}}</ref>

On 27 May 2021, Carey signed a new contract with CSKA Sofia; the length of the contract was not disclosed.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dubliner Graham Carey signs new contract with CSKA Sofia|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/dubliner-graham-carey-signs-new-contract-with-cska-sofia-40476520.html|access-date=23 July 2021|website=independent |date=27 May 2021 }}</ref>

On 16 September 2021, Carey scored CSKA Sofia's first ever goal in the [[2021–22 UEFA Europa Conference League|2021–22 UEFA Conference League]] group stage against [[A.S. Roma|Roma]] in the [[Stadio Olimpico]], lashing the ball into the top left corner.<ref name="CareyScorerinMatchvsRoma2021">{{cite web | title=Roma-CSKA-Sofia {{!}} UEFA Europa Conference League| author=| website=[[UEFA]]| url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaconferenceleague/match/2033270--roma-vs-cska-sofia/| date=16 September 2021|access-date=17 September 2021}}</ref> Roma went on to win the opening group game 5–1.<ref name="CareyScorerinMatchvsRoma2021"/>

=== St Johnstone ===
On 1 July 2022, Carey returned to Scottish football after signing for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web |last=Nicolson |first=Eric |title=Graham Carey: St Johnstone confirm 4th summer signing on a 2-year deal |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/3446928/graham-carey-st-johnstone-confirm-4th-summer-signing-on-a-2-year-deal/ |access-date=1 July 2022 |work=The Courier|date=1 July 2022|publisher=DC Thomson}}</ref>

=== Livingston === 
He signed for [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] in 2025, but left the club in May 2026 following the expiration of his contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=Squad Update – Retained & Released List|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/squad-update-retained-released-list/|website=livingstonfc.co.uk|date=19 May 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Carey has represented the Republic of Ireland at youth, [[Republic of Ireland national under-17 football team|under-17]] and [[Republic of Ireland national football team|under-19 level]].<ref name=Andorra1 /> He has six [[Republic of Ireland national under-21 football team|Under-21]] caps.<ref name=4Changes>[http://www.fai.ie/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=101207:four-changes-to-u21-squad&catid=3:under-21&Itemid=11 Four changes to U21 squad] FAI, 7 September 2010</ref> His debut for the Under-21s came under [[Don Givens]] in February 2009 at [[Turners Cross (stadium)|Turners Cross]] against [[Germany national under-21 football team|Germany]].<ref>[http://www.extratime.ie/newsdesk/articles/1270/ Rep. of Ireland 1 – 1 Germany] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120318021000/http://www.extratime.ie/newsdesk/articles/1270/ |date=18 March 2012 }} ExtraTime.ie, 10 February 2009</ref> He scored his first goal at that level away to [[Georgia national under-21 football team|Georgia]] with an impressive 18-yard left footed strike after a clever one two with [[Cillian Sheridan]].<ref>[http://www.fai.ie/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=100524:under-21s-held-by-georgia&catid=3:under-21&Itemid=11 Under 21s Held by Georgia] FAI, 14 November 2009</ref>

==Style of play==
Carey's preferred and most effective position is playing as a No 10 behind the striker, allowing him the freedom to move around the field and get on the ball. He can also play on the left or right side of midfield. He is very direct in his play and attacks defenders at every opportunity, while being a set-piece specialist his crossing has been described as "unbelievable".<ref name=Heary>[http://www.loi.ie/index.php/clubs/premier-division/bohemian-fc/latest-news/657-heary-hails-careys-contribution Heary Hails Carey contribution] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111006173421/http://www.loi.ie/index.php/clubs/premier-division/bohemian-fc/latest-news/657-heary-hails-careys-contribution |date=6 October 2011 }} League of Ireland, May 2009</ref> While at [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]], Carey was used as a left back and as a wing back on the left side.<ref>[http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/spl/rangers/rangers-3-st-mirren-1-jig-shows-all-the-right-moves-1.1011575 Rangers 3 St Mirren 1] Herald Scotland, 6 March 2010</ref>

Carey is also noted for his accurate set piece and crossing delivery as well as his long range shooting, particularly with his left foot. His former [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] teammate, and former [[Scotland national football team|Scotland international]], [[Gary Teale]] said "You will go a long way to come across a better left foot than Graham's. In a tight game, if you are giving someone like that an opportunity, then that can be the difference."<ref name="auto"/>

'''Steven May''' (born 3 November 1992) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays for {{Scottish football updater|Livingst}} side [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].  May has previously played in the Scottish leagues for [[St Johnstone]] (two spells), [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]], [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] and [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]], and in the English leagues for [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] and [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]]. He has been capped once internationally by [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]].

==Club career==

===St Johnstone===

====Early career====
May began playing football aged ten and started his career as a member of St Johnstone's youth squad.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/matchdaydetail.php?param=239 | title=Saints ease to last game win | publisher=[[St Johnstone F.C.]] | date=11 May 2009 | access-date=10 December 2011 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131230234305/http://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/matchdaydetail.php?param=239 | archive-date=30 December 2013 | df=dmy-all }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=When I get down I think about my old Saints pal who's now selling ice cream for a living, says Stevie May|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/down-think-old-saints-pal-3172000|publisher=Daily Record|date=22 February 2014|access-date=18 June 2014}}</ref> Aged 16, May made his first team debut on 11 May 2009 as a substitute against [[Airdrie United F.C.|Airdrie United]] in the [[Scottish First Division]] scoring his first senior goal.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_div_1/8043425.stm | title=Airdrie United 0–4 St Johnstone | publisher=BBC Sport | date=11 May 2009 | access-date=10 December 2011}}</ref> May later recalled on his debut, quoting: "[[Derek McInnes]] gave me my first taste of first team football. He gave my SPL debut at 16. He believed in me. He taught me how important it was to keep possession when I had the ball and make the opposition work to get it back."<ref>{{cite news|title=St Johnstone striker Stevie May reveals how he will never forget those who helped him on his way to stardom|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/st-johnstone-striker-stevie-reveals-3063201|publisher=Daily Record|date=26 January 2014|access-date=18 June 2014}}</ref> In 2009, he signed a new contract that tied him to the club until 2012.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/player.php?param=51 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100226070328/http://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/player.php?param=51 | url-status=dead | archive-date=26 February 2010 | title=Stevie May St Johnstone Profile | publisher=[[St Johnstone F.C.]] | access-date=10 December 2011 | df=dmy-all }}</ref>

May had to wait another season for his next appearance, coming on as a substitute on 13 November 2010 against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] in the [[Scottish Premier League]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/9182187.stm | title=St Johnstone 0 – 2 Hearts | publisher=BBC Sport | date=13 November 2010 | access-date=10 December 2011}}</ref> With his first start coming on 26 January 2011 against [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/scot_prem/9372940.stm | title=St Johnstone 1 – 0 Motherwell | publisher=BBC Sport | date=26 January 2011 | access-date=10 December 2011}}</ref> He scored two goals on 1 February 2011 in their 2–0 win over [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/9383805.stm | title=St Johnstone 2 – 0 Hamilton | publisher=BBC Sport | date=1 February 2011 | access-date=10 December 2011}}</ref> In all he made 22 appearances that season scoring twice.

====Alloa (loan)====
May's only appearance of the 2011–12 season for St Johnstone came as a substitute on the opening day of the season against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] at [[Pittodrie]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/14241745.stm | title=Aberdeen 0 – 0 St Johnstone | publisher=BBC Sport | date=23 July 2011 | access-date=10 December 2011}}</ref> With appearances limited he was loaned to [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]] until the end of January.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.alloaathletic.co.uk/BlogView.aspx?pageid=2&ItemID=626&mid=2 | title=Manager adds to squad | publisher=[[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]] | date=7 December 2011 | access-date=10 December 2011}}</ref> He made his league debut for Alloa on 10 December against [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]],<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16122529 | title=Alloa Athletic 1–0 Queen's Park | publisher=BBC Sport | date=10 December 2011 | access-date=10 December 2011}}</ref> going on to score his first goals on 2 January 2012, netting a hat-trick for The Wasps in a 3–1 win against [[East Stirlingshire F.C.|East Stirlingshire]].<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16375146 |publisher=BBC Sport | title=East Stirlingshire 1–3 Alloa Ath | date=2 January 2012}}</ref> After one month at the club, May had his loan spell with Alloa extended until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=May stays with Alloa|url=https://www.alloaadvertiser.com/sport/alloaathletic/articles/2012/01/26/422720-may-stays-with-alloa/|publisher=Alloa Advertiser|date=26 January 2012|access-date=18 June 2014}}</ref> May was awarded the [[Scottish Football League monthly awards|SFL Player of the Month]], Young Player of the Month and Irn-Bru Ginger Boot awards for January; the first time that one player has won all three player awards in a month.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/news/article/irn-bru-sfl-phenomenal-awards---january-2012/|title=Irn Bru SFL Phenomenal Awards – January 2012|publisher=Scottish Football League|date=17 February 2012|access-date=21 February 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120505123042/http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/news/article/irn-bru-sfl-phenomenal-awards---january-2012/|archive-date=5 May 2012|df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref name=Scotsman120212>{{cite news|url=http://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/sfl-division-three/steven_may_shows_he_s_got_style_and_substance_1_2112895|date=12 February 2012|access-date=1 March 2012|title=Steven May shows he's got style and substance|publisher=Johnston Press|work=Scotland on Sunday}}</ref> He scored four goals in the 8–1 victory against [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]] that clinched the Third Division championship.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17641962|title=Alloa Athletic v Elgin City|publisher=BBC Sport|date=7 April 2012|access-date=7 April 2012}}</ref> At the end of the season, May won the Irn-Bru SFL Phenomenal Third Division Player of the Season.<ref>{{cite news|title=IRN-BRU SFL End of Season Awards 2011/12|url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/irn-bru-sfl-end-of-season-awards-201112/|publisher=SFFL Official Website|date=25 May 2012|access-date=17 June 2014}}</ref> May signed a new one-year contract with St Johnstone.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/18461577|title=Stevie May signs new contract with St Johnstone|publisher=BBC Sport|date=15 June 2012|access-date=16 June 2012}}</ref>

====2013–14 season====
[[File:Scottish Cup Final2 28.jpg|thumb|left|200px|May playing for [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] in the [[2014 Scottish Cup Final|Scottish Cup Final]] against [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].]]

In the summer of 2013, May was the subject of several bids from [[Peterborough United F.C.|Peterborough United]] of the [[Football League One|English League One]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Transfer news: Peterborough still interested in St Johnstone's Stevie May|url=https://www1.skysports.com/football/news/16213/8870110/transfer-news-peterborough-still-interested-in-st-johnstones-stevie-may|publisher=Sky Sports|date=14 August 2013|access-date=17 June 2014}}</ref> though May insisted he was happy at the club.<ref>{{cite news|title=Stevie May happy to be playing and scoring with St Johnstone|url=https://www1.skysports.com/football/news/16213/8917321/stevie-may-happy-to-be-playing-and-scoring-with-st-johnstone|publisher=Sky Sports|date=13 September 2013|access-date=17 June 2014}}</ref> Immediately after being linked with Peterborough, May was offered and signed a further contract extension by St Johnstone.<ref>{{cite news|title=Stevie May: St Johnstone to offer new deal to Peterborough target|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23795137|publisher=BBC Sport|date=22 August 2013|access-date=17 June 2014}}</ref> May believed his performance in his two loan spells would allow him to make a breakthrough at the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/newsitemsdetail.php?param=2546 |title=STEVIE READY TO SHOW WHAT HE CAN DO AT SPL LEVEL |publisher=Perth St Johnstone |access-date=17 June 2014 |date=3 June 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140617224036/http://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/newsitemsdetail.php?param=2546 |archive-date=17 June 2014 |url-status=unfit }}</ref>

May started the 2013–14 season very well. Awarded a starting place, he scored the equaliser against [[Europa League]] opponents, [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]], in a famous 2–1 aggregate win.<ref>{{cite news|title=St Johnstone 1–1 Rosenborg (agg 2–1)|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23352990|publisher=BBC Sport|date=25 July 2013|access-date=17 June 2014}}</ref> He went on to score the winner against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Scottish Premiership: Stevie May's goal enough for St Johnstone|url=https://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/299089/report|publisher=Sky Sports|date=4 August 2013|access-date=17 June 2014}}</ref> and goals against [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]]<ref>{{cite news|title=St Johnstone 4–0 Ross County|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23644634|publisher=BBC Sport|date=17 August 2013|access-date=17 June 2014}}</ref> and [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibs]].<ref>{{cite news|title=St Johnstone 1–2 Hibernian |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23999508|publisher=BBC Sport|date=14 September 2013|access-date=17 June 2014}}</ref> He scored 4 goals in his first 9 games of the season leading to a call-up for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland U21]] team. New St Johnstone manager [[Tommy Wright (Northern Ireland footballer)|Tommy Wright]] described him as "heading for the top".<ref>{{cite news|title=Football – Mature May 'heading for the top'|url=https://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/news/football-mature-may-heading-top-073258507--sow.html |publisher=Yahoo! Eurosport|date=20 September 2013|access-date=17 June 2014}}</ref>

A rich vein of form followed. In a match against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] on 5 October, May provided a triple assist and scored, as St Johnstone won 4–0.<ref>{{cite news|title=St Johnstone 4–0 Inverness Caledonian Thistle|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/24349649|publisher=BBC Sport|date=5 October 2013|access-date=17 June 2014}}</ref> He then scored four goals in three matches against [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]], Hearts and [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]]. Thanks to this form, May extended his contract at St Johnstone until 2015.<ref>{{cite news|title=St Johnstone: Stevie May signs one-year contract extension|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/24653360|publisher=BBC Sport|date=24 October 2013|access-date=17 June 2014}}</ref> May won the Scottish Professional Football League player of the month award of October.<ref>{{cite news|title=St Johnstone: Stevie May and Tommy Wright win October awards|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/24943063|publisher=BBC Sport|date=14 November 2013|access-date=17 June 2014}}</ref> May
scored his first hat-trick of the season, in a 3–0 win over [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref>{{cite news|title=St Johnstone 3–0 Dundee United|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25482658|publisher=BBC Sport|date=29 December 2013|access-date=17 June 2014}}</ref> Three weeks after that, May scored another hat-trick, on 18 January, in a 3–3 draw against Hearts.<ref>{{cite news|title=St Johnstone 3–3 Heart of Midlothian|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25693251|publisher=BBC Sport|date=18 January 2014|access-date=17 June 2014}}</ref>

Premier Division|1991–92 season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=St Johnstone's Stevie May has Paul Wright's record in his
