===Sheffield Wednesday===
[[File:Stevie May 092014.jpg|200px|thumb|May playing for [[Sheffield Wednesday]] in 2014]]
May joined [[Football League Championship]] side [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] on 9 August 2014, signing a four-year deal.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28711389 | title=Sheffield Wednesday sign striker Stevie May from St Johnstone |work=BBC Sport | access-date=9 August 2014|date=9 August 2014}}</ref><ref name="swfcofficial">{{cite web|url=http://www.swfc.co.uk/news/article/strike-ace-stevie-may-joins-sheffield-wednesday-1815082.aspx |title=Strike ace Stevie May joins Sheffield Wednesday |access-date=9 August 2014 |date=9 August 2014 |publisher=Sheffield Wednesday |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140809235527/http://www.swfc.co.uk/news/article/strike-ace-stevie-may-joins-sheffield-wednesday-1815082.aspx |archive-date=9 August 2014 |url-status=unfit }}</ref> Upon the move, Manager [[Stuart Gray (footballer, born 1960)|Stuart Gray]] believed that May had expectations to become a success at the club<ref>{{cite news|title=Championship: Sheffield Wednesday boss Stuart Gray says Stevie May should not feel pressure|url=https://www1.skysports.com/football/news/12040/9417773/championship-sheffield-wednesday-boss-stuart-gray-says-stevie-may-should-not-feel-pressure|publisher=Sky Sports|date=11 August 2014|access-date=8 March 2015}}</ref> and May, himself, felt it was the right decision to leave St Johnstone at the right time.<ref>{{cite news|title=Transfer news: Stevie May happy with timing of Sheffield Wednesday move|url=https://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11703/9455557/transfer-news-stevie-may-happy-with-timing-of-sheffield-wednesday-move|publisher=Sky Sports|date=4 September 2014|access-date=8 March 2015}}</ref>

May made his debut for the club on 16 August 2014, in a goalless draw against [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Sheffield Wednesday 0–0 Derby County|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28716630|publisher=BBC Sport|date=16 August 2014|access-date=8 March 2015}}</ref> His first goal came in an away fixture at [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] on 23 August, which Wednesday won 3–2.<ref>{{cite web|title=Middlesbrough 2–3 Sheffield Wednesday|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28815097|publisher=BBC Sport|date=23 August 2014|access-date=8 March 2015}}</ref> He scored his second goal for the club at [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] on 16 September, in a 2–0 win.<ref>{{cite web|title=Birmingham City 0–2 Sheffield Wednesday|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29120663 |publisher=BBC Sport|date=16 September 2014|access-date=8 March 2015}}</ref> Four days later, he continued a sequence of contributing vital goals, as he scored the only goal of the game against Reading.<ref>{{cite news|title=Sheffield Wednesday 1–0 Reading |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29186723|publisher=BBC Sport|date=20 September 2014|access-date=8 March 2015}}</ref> May helped the club end an 11-game winless run by scoring in a 2–1 win over [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] on 29 November.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sheffield Wednesday 2–1 Wigan Athletic |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30155829|publisher=BBC Sport|date=29 November 2014|access-date=8 March 2015}}</ref> May then had a goal drought that lasted twelve games and, as a result, he was often placed on the substitute bench.<ref>{{cite news|title=Sheffield Wednesday: Gray backs misfiring May to come good|url=http://www.sheffieldtelegraph.co.uk/sport/sheffield-wednesday/sheffield-wednesday-gray-backs-misfiring-may-to-come-good-1-7122147|work=Sheffield Telegraph|date=24 February 2015|access-date=8 March 2015}}</ref> This drought ended on 24 February 2015, when he scored in a 3–1 win against [[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Millwall 1–3 Sheffield Wednesday |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31498955|publisher=BBC Sport |date=24 February 2015|access-date=8 March 2015}}</ref>

===Preston North End===
May was transferred to [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] on 1 September 2015 for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34122084 |title=Stevie May and Eoin Doyle join Preston North End |publisher=BBC Sport |date=1 September 2015 |access-date=1 September 2015}}</ref> Whilst playing for [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston]] against [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] in November 2015, May suffered a knee ligament injury which ruled him out for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Preston North End striker Stevie May ruled out for season|url=https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/preston-north-end/injury-news/news/preston-striker-stevie-may-ruled-out-for-season_260417.html#$$o17ltf&&3CAF5L7NEeWB1AqPcXQCJw$$=Sport|publisher=Sports Mole|date=28 November 2015|access-date=19 January 2016}}</ref><ref name="eager24">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c3rx4dg2w2jo|author=Jonathan Sutherland|title=May back among goals and eager for more silverware|website=BBC Sport|date=8 November 2024|access-date=8 November 2024}}</ref> He made his first team return as a substitute against [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] on 11 February 2017.<ref>{{cite news
|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/38864155
|title=Preston 4–2 Brentford
|publisher=BBC Sport
|date=11 February 2017
|access-date=2 May 2017}}</ref> May scored his first goal for Preston in a 1–1 draw with [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]] on 29 April 2017.<ref>{{cite news
|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39675690
|title=Preston 1–1 Rotherham
|publisher=BBC Sport
|date=29 April 2017
|access-date=2 May 2017}}</ref>

===Aberdeen===
May joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] on a four-year deal in August 2017, for an undisclosed fee thought to be around £300,000, reuniting with former St Johnstone manager Derek McInnes.<ref>{{cite news
|url=https://www.pnefc.net/news/2017/august/stevie-may-joins-aberdeen-on-permanent-deal|title=Stevie May Joins Aberdeen on Permanent Deal|publisher=Preston North End FC|date=10 August 2017|access-date=10 August 2017}}</ref> Although initially given the squad number of 18, May later changed to 83, in honour of Aberdeen winning the [[UEFA Cup Winner's Cup]] in May 1983.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.afc.co.uk/mobile/news/9925.php|title=Welcome May 83|publisher=Aberdeen F.C.|date=11 August 2017|access-date=11 August 2017}}</ref> May scored his first goal for Aberdeen in a 2–1 victory over [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]]; coincidentally this was timed at the 11th minute of the game, creating a further reference to the club's European honours (11 May 83).<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40908207|title=Aberdeen 2–1 Dundee|publisher=BBC Sport|date=19 August 2017|access-date=19 August 2017}}</ref> He contributed to Aberdeen finishing runners-up in the [[2017–18 Scottish Premiership]], and was an unused substitute in the [[2018 Scottish League Cup Final]], lost to [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref>[https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/dec/02/celtic-aberdeen-scottish-league-cup-final-match-report Celtic claim Scottish League Cup after Ryan Christie strike denies Aberdeen], The Guardian, 2 December 2018</ref>

===St Johnstone (second spell)===
On 29 August 2019, May signed for St Johnstone for a second time, agreeing a two-year contract with the option of a further year.<ref>{{cite web|title=Stevie May returns to St Johnstone after leaving Aberdeen|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49517073|publisher=BBC Sport|date=29 August 2019|access-date=29 August 2019}}</ref> He scored his first goal since returning in a 2–2 draw away to Ross County in October 2019, also missing a penalty in the same match.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ross County 2–2 St Johnstone|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49861443|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Southwick|first=Andrew|date=5 October 2019|access-date=6 October 2019}}</ref>

On 26 April 2021, May signed a new two-year contract extension with St. Johnstone.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/stevie-may-signs-new-two-year-contract|title=Stevie May Signs New Two Year Contract|publisher=St Johnstone FC|date=26 April 2021|access-date=26 April 2021}}</ref>

===Livingston===
On 21 August 2024, May signed for [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/stevie-may-joins-the-lions-on-loan/|title=Stevie May joins the Lions on loan!|publisher=Livingston FC|date=21 August 2024}}</ref><ref name="eager24"/> He was part of the squad that won the [[2024–25 Scottish Challenge Cup|2024–25 Scottish Challenge]] cup scoring four goals in five appearances including a goal in the final as Livingston beat [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queens Park]] 5–0 at [[Falkirk Stadium]].<ref name=":0" />

==International career==
On 5 August 2013, May was called up for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland Under-21]] team.<ref>{{cite news|title=Scotland U21 call for St Johnstone striker Stevie May|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23578014|publisher=BBC Sport|date=5 August 2013|access-date=17 June 2014}}</ref> On 30 September 2014, May was called up to the senior [[Scotland national football team]] for [[UEFA Euro 2016 qualifying Group D|Euro 2016 Group D]] qualifying matches against [[Georgia national football team|Georgia]] and [[Poland national football team|Poland]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Ryan Gauld and Stevie May called up for Scotland|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/scotland/29427160|access-date=30 September 2014|publisher=BBC Sport|date=30 September 2014}}</ref> On 18 November 2014 he made his international debut, coming on as a substitute in the 67th minute in a friendly against [[England national football team|England]] at Celtic Park.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29999555|title=Scotland 1 – 3 England|date=18 November 2014 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=31 October 2017}}</ref>

'''Liam Polworth''' (born 12 October 1994) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Kilmarno}} club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]]. He has previously played for [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]], [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] and [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].

==Early and personal life==
Polworth was born in [[Inverness]].<ref name = "ICT"/> His father Iain also played for Inverness.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/inverness-caledonian-thistle/663092/liam-polworth-looks-seize-caley-thistle-opportunity/|title=Liam Polworth looks to seize Caley Thistle opportunity|date=12 August 2015|accessdate=25 October 2015|publisher=Press & Journal}}</ref>

==Club career==

=== Inverness Caledonian Thistle ===
Polworth made his senior debut for [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] in the [[Scottish Premier League]] on 11 May 2011, becoming the club's youngest ever player, at the age of 16 years, 211 days.<ref name = "ICT">{{cite web|url=http://ictfc.com/stats/player.php?id=192|title=Profile|accessdate=25 October 2015|publisher=Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150912044735/http://ictfc.com/stats/player.php?id=192|archive-date=12 September 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> Polworth was an unused substitute as Inverness won the [[2015 Scottish Cup Final]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32728510 |title=Inverness CT 2–1 Falkirk |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=30 May 2015 |access-date=4 June 2015 |first=Alasdair |last=Lamont}}</ref> Polworth established himself in the first team during the 2015–16 season, scoring five goals from a midfield position.<ref name = "contract"/> He signed a new three-year contract with Inverness in April 2016.<ref name = "contract"/>

On 24 March 2018, Polworth started the whole game in the [[2018 Scottish Challenge Cup final|Scottish Challenge Cup final]] against [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] and helped Inverness Caledonian Thistle win 1–0 to win a trophy.<ref name="Polworth Dumbarton 2018">{{cite web|title=Dumbarton 0–1 Inverness CT|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43445358|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Crawford|first=Kenny|date=24 March 2018|access-date=29 April 2018|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180329032040/http://www.bbc.com/sport/football/43445358|archive-date=29 March 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> 

For his performance in the 2018–19 season, Polworth, alongside [[Aaron Doran]], were named PFA Scotland Scottish Championship Team of the Year.<ref name="Polworth Scottish Championship Team of the Year">{{cite web|url=https://ictfc.com/aaron-doran-and-liam-polworth-named-in-championship-team-of-the-season/|title=Aaron Doran and Liam Polworth named in Championship Team of the Season|website=Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|date=5 May 2019|access-date=7 November 2025|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220925153454/https://ictfc.com/aaron-doran-and-liam-polworth-named-in-championship-team-of-the-season|archive-date=25 September 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Motherwell ===
On 17 April 2019, Polworth signed a pre-contract agreement with [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]], his first club after being at Inverness since the age of 8.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47969758|title=Motherwell: Liam Polworth agrees to sign from Inverness CT|date=17 April 2019|access-date=17 April 2019|language=en-GB}}</ref>

After rejecting a new contract in January 2021 and falling out with manager [[Graham Alexander]], Polworth was made to train with the youth team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/ex-motherwell-man-liam-polworth-24259703|title=Ex-Motherwell man Liam Polworth on training with youths after contract rejection|first=Euan|last=Robertson|date=6 June 2021|website=Daily Record}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/ross-county/3199291/ex-caley-jag-liam-polworth-on-being-made-to-train-with-kids-at-motherwell-as-he-confirms-ross-county-link/|title=Ex-Caley Jags midfielder Liam Polworth confirms Ross County link and speaks of training with teens at Motherwell|first=Paul|last=Chalk|date=4 June 2021 }}</ref>

On 24 May 2021, Motherwell announced that Polworth would be leaving the club at the end of the season when his contract expired.<ref>{{cite web |title=END OF 2020/21 SQUAD UPDATE |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2021/05/24/end-of-2020-21-squad-update/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=24 May 2021 |date=24 May 2021}}</ref>

===Kilmarnock===
He signed for [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on 23 June 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/inverness-caledonian-thistle/3258814/ex-caley-thistle-ace-liam-polworth-closes-in-on-move-to-championship-side-kilmarnock/|title=Ex-Caley Thistle ace Liam Polworth closes in on move to Championship side Kilmarnock|first=Paul|last=Chalk|date=23 June 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/tommys-delight-as-liam-polworth-joins-killie/|title=Tommy's delight as Liam Polworth joins Killie|date=23 June 2021}}</ref> On 28 February 2022, Polworth joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] on loan for the remainder of the 2021–22 season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Polworth_joins_on_loan&ID=13652 |title=Polworth joins on loan |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=28 February 2022 |accessdate=1 March 2022}}</ref>

==International career==
Polworth has represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-16 football team|under-16]] and [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17]] youth levels.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=2492&playerID=68244&squadID=17|title=Under-16 profile|accessdate=25 October 2015|publisher=Scottish Football Association}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=2492&playerID=68244&squadID=13|title=Under-17 profile|accessdate=25 October 2015|publisher=Scottish Football Association}}</ref> He made his debut appearance for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] team during the 2015–16 season.<ref name = "contract">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36164560 |title=Liam Polworth extends Inverness Caledonian Thistle stay until 2019 |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=28 April 2016 |accessdate=28 April 2016}}</ref>

'''Gary Sean Mackay-Steven''' (born 31 August 1990) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]]

Having not made the first team at English clubs [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] and [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]], he began his professional career with [[Airdrie United F.C.|Airdrie United]] in January 2011, spending half a season there before moving to top-flight team [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]. He remained with Dundee United until February 2015, when he was signed by [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] for £250,000. He joined [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] in 2017, and later moved to [[New York City FC]] when his contract expired in July 2019. Mackay-Steven returned to Scottish football in 2021 with [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].

Mackay-Steven has made two full international appearances for [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]].

==Club career==
===Early career===
Born in [[Thurso]], [[Caithness]], Mackay-Steven began his youth career with [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] before moving to English [[FA Premier League|Premier League]] side [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in 2007.<ref name="lpool">{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/r/ross_county/6419773.stm|title=Liverpool sign up Ross County kid|date=16 March 2007|access-date=18 July 2011|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> After spending two years in the reserve and youth sides, Mackay-Steven was released after an injury-plagued season.<ref name="airdrie"/> He trained with [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] before eventually returning to Scotland.<ref name="airdrie"/>

===Airdrie United===
On 11 January 2011, Mackay-Steven joined [[Scottish Football League Second Division|Scottish Second Division]] side [[Airdrie United F.C.|Airdrie United]].<ref name="airdrie">{{cite news|url=http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/news/article/airdrie-bring-in-former-liverpool-youth/|title=Airdrie bring in former Liverpool youth|date=11 July 2011|access-date=18 July 2011|publisher=Scottish Football League|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120814051443/http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/news/article/airdrie-bring-in-former-liverpool-youth/|archive-date=14 August 2012}}</ref> He made his debut a week later in the fourth round of the [[Scottish Cup]], starting against [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] at [[Cappielow Park]] and scoring the opening goal of a 2–2 draw from 25 yards out.<ref>{{cite news|title=Morton 2-2 Airdrie|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/9364352.stm|access-date=16 January 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=18 January 2011}}</ref> A week later, in the replay at the [[Excelsior Stadium]], Mackay-Steven scored again, albeit in a 5–2 defeat.<ref>{{cite news|title=Airdrie 2-5 Morton|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_cups/9372264.stm|access-date=16 January 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=25 January 2011}}</ref> He played 19 league matches in the remainder of the season, but did not score.

===Dundee United===
On 13 July 2011, Mackay-Steven signed a two-year deal with [[Scottish Premier League]] club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref name="utd">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14136831|title=Winger Gary MacKay-Steven joins Dundee United|date=13 July 2011|access-date=18 July 2011|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> He made his debut eight days later as an 80th-minute [[substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Johnny Russell (footballer)|Johnny Russell]] in a [[UEFA Europa League]] match against [[Śląsk Wrocław]], which his club won 3–2 but were nonetheless eliminated on the away goals rule.<ref>{{cite news|title=Dundee Utd 3-2 Slask Wroclaw|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14201969|access-date=2 March 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=21 July 2011}}</ref> On 24 July, he made his league debut for the club on the opening day of [[2011–12 Scottish Premier League|the season]], coming on for [[Barry Douglas (footballer)|Barry Douglas]] for the last 30 minutes of a 1–1 draw against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] at [[Tannadice Park]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dundee United 1-1 Kilmarnock|url=http://spfl.co.uk/premiership/fixture/3407113/|publisher=[[Scottish Professional Football League]]|access-date=2 March 2015|archive-date=2 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402114653/http://spfl.co.uk/premiership/fixture/3407113/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 29 August, Mackay-Steven scored his first goal for the club (and his first career league goal), netting in the 3–3 draw at [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref name="stjohnstone">{{cite news|url=http://www.thecourier.co.uk/Sport/Football/article/16823/st-johnstone-3-dundee-united-3-perth-men-count-cost-of-late-madness.html|title=St Johnstone 3 Dundee United 3: Perth men count cost of late madness|date=29 August 2011|access-date=30 August 2011|work=[[The Courier (Dundee)|The Courier]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121019175314/http://www.thecourier.co.uk/Sport/Football/article/16823/st-johnstone-3-dundee-united-3-perth-men-count-cost-of-late-madness.html|archive-date=19 October 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> By the end of the 2011–12 season, Mackay-Steven had established a regular starting place in the first team and become a huge fans' favourite thanks to his large role in helping turn around United's poor start to the season. Mackay-Steven signed an extended contract with the club in January 2012.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16550511|title=Dundee United's Gary Mackay-Steven extends contract until 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=13 January 2012|access-date=13 January 2012}}</ref>

[[Blackburn Rovers]] scouts were reported to have been watching Mackay-Steven on 24 August 2013, in Dundee United's 4–0 victory over [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]], a game in which he scored.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dundee United star Gary Mackay-Steven aims to show Scotland boss Gordon Strachan what he's missing|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/gary-mackay-steven-plans-demonstrate-gordon-2224176|publisher=Daily Record|date=26 August 2013|access-date=3 September 2013}}</ref> On 12 April 2014, he scored Dundee United's second goal in a 3–1 win against [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] in the [[2013–14 Scottish Cup|Scottish Cup]] semi–final at [[Ibrox Stadium|Ibrox]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Rangers 1-3 Dundee United|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26898652|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Wilson|first=Richard|date=12 April 2014|access-date=14 April 2014}}</ref> In [[2014 Scottish Cup final|the final]] on 17 May, he started in a 2–0 defeat to St Johnstone at [[Celtic Park]], being substituted for [[Ryan Gauld]] after 64 minutes.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Wilson|first1=Richard|title=St Johnstone 2-0 Dundee Utd|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27354162|access-date=8 September 2014|publisher=BBC Sport|date=17 May 2014}}</ref>

He scored twice as Dundee United won the [[Dundee derby]] 6–2 against [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on 1 January 2015.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Campbell|first1=Andy|title=Dundee Utd 6-2 Dundee|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30600732|access-date=7 January 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=1 January 2015}}</ref>

===Celtic===
[[File:20170701 SK Rapid Wien vs Celtic FC 1720.jpg|thumb|Mackay-Steven in action in a friendly against [[Rapid Vienna]] in July 2017]]
On 16 January 2015, Mackay-Steven signed a pre-contract agreement to join [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] at the end of the season on the expiry of his Dundee United contract.<ref name=Celtic>{{cite news|title=Celtic: Gary Mackay-Steven agrees summer switch|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30799180|access-date=16 January 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=16 January 2015}}</ref> In the January transfer window, he had been pursued by [[Nigel Clough]], manager of English [[Football League One|League One]] club [[Sheffield United]], who made three bids up to £100,000 while Dundee United wanted a minimum of £250,000.<ref name=Celtic/> On the transfer deadline day, 2 February, Celtic made an offer of £250,000 and the move was completed immediately, with his Dundee United teammate [[Stuart Armstrong]] joining in a separate deal at the same time.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Spence|first1=Jim|title=Stuart Armstrong & Gary Mackay-Steven join Celtic|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31088504|access-date=3 February 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=2 February 2015}}</ref> Five days later, the pair watched from the stands as Celtic won 2–0 at Dundee in the fifth round of the Scottish Cup.<ref>{{cite news|last1=McVake|first1=Roddie|title=Dundee 0-2 Celtic|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31071296|access-date=8 February 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=7 February 2015}}</ref>

Mackay-Steven made his debut on 11 February away to [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]], scoring after 37 seconds in a 3–0 victory.<ref>{{cite news|title=Partick Thistle 0-3 Celtic|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30600739|access-date=11 February 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=11 February 2015}}</ref> His first goal at [[Celtic Park]] came on 1 March as the third in a 4–0 win over [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]], with a shot from 20 yards.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Wilson|first1=Richard|title=Celtic 4-0 Aberdeen|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31572587|access-date=2 March 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=1 March 2015}}</ref> On 15 March Celtic won the [[2015 Scottish League Cup final|Scottish League Cup final]] against Dundee United, but Mackay-Steven was cup-tied, having already represented Dundee United in the tournament that season.<ref name=bbcfinal>{{cite news|title=Dundee Utd 0-2 Celtic|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31785677|access-date=15 March 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=14 March 2015|first=Richard|last=Wilson}}</ref>

===Aberdeen===
On 12 July 2017, Mackay-Steven signed a two-year contract with [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite news|title=Gary Mackay-Steven joins Aberdeen from Celtic on a two-year contract for an undisclosed fee|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40566901|access-date=12 July 2017|publisher=BBC Sport|date=12 July 2017}}</ref> He made his debut the following day in a UEFA Europa League second qualifying round first leg at home to [[NK Široki Brijeg]], starting in a 1–1 draw. In the second leg in Bosnia a week after, he scored to wrap up a 2–0 win and advancement.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Parks|first1=Gordon|title=Aberdeen ignore Siroki warnings of hell as Stewart and Mackay-Steven goals leave Dons in heaven – big match verdict|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/aberdeen-ignore-siroki-warnings-hell-10841806|access-date=28 August 2017|work=Daily Record|date=20 July 2017}}</ref>

Mackay-Steven scored his first league goal for Aberdeen on 14 October, the only one of a victory at [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Derek McInnes salutes Aberdeen star Gary Mackay-Steven after bagging winner against Hibs|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/aberdeen-gary-mackay-steven-mcinnes-11343257|access-date=17 December 2017|work=Daily Record|date=14 October 2017}}</ref> On 16 December, against the same opponents, he scored his first senior hat-trick in a 4–1 win.<ref>{{cite news|title=Aberdeen 4 – 1 Hibs: Mackay-Steven nets treble in thumping win|url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/competitions/premiership/aberdeen-4-1-hibs-mackay-steven-nets-treble-in-thumping-win-1-4641053|access-date=17 December 2017|work=The Scotsman|date=16 December 2017}}</ref> Mackay-Steven won the [[Scottish Cup]] Goal of the Fourth round award for his strike in the 4–1 win against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Gary Mackay-Steven wins William Hill Scottish Cup Goal of the Fourth Round award|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/watch/gary-mackay-steven-wins-william-hill-scottish-cup-goal-of-the-fourth-round-award/?rid=4452|access-date=4 March 2018|work=Scottish FA|date=8 February 2018}}</ref>

In the [[2018 Scottish League Cup final]] against former club Celtic on 2 December 2018, Mackay-Steven was stretchered from the field after being knocked unconscious by a clash of heads with [[Dedryck Boyata]] shortly before the end of the first half (Aberdeen lost 1–0).<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2018/12/02/ryan-christie-fires-celtic-victory-aberdeen-scottish-league/ |title =Ryan Christie fires Celtic to victory over Aberdeen in Scottish League Cup final|work=The Daily Telegraph|location=London|date=2 December 2018|access-date=2 October 2019|last1 =Forsyth|first1 =Roddy}}</ref> He was released from hospital after a few days<ref>[https://www.eveningexpress.co.uk/fp/aberdeen-fc/donsnews/mackay-steven-breaks-silence-to-thank-medical-staff-for-treatment-after-horror-betfred-cup-final-injury1/ Mackay-Steven breaks silence to thank medical staff for treatment after horror Betfred Cup final injury], Evening Express, 7 December 2018</ref> and returned to playing towards the end of January 2019.<ref>[https://www.afc.co.uk/video/rd-22-gary-mackay-steven-hamilton-accies-preview/ Rd 22: Gary Mackay-Steven: Hamilton Accies Preview] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221022221226/https://www.afc.co.uk/video/rd-22-gary-mackay-steven-hamilton-accies-preview/ |date=22 October 2022 }}, [[Aberdeen FC]], 22 January 2019</ref>

===New York City FC===
On 24 June 2019, Mackay-Steven joined [[Major League Soccer]] side [[New York City FC|New York City]] on a free transfer, effective from the start of the league's transfer window on 9 July.<ref>[https://www.nycfc.com/post/2019/06/24/new-york-city-fc-signs-gary-mackay-steven New York City FC Signs Gary Mackay-Steven], New York City FC, 24 June 2019</ref> He made his debut on 14 July during the [[Hudson River Derby]] away to the [[New York Red Bulls]] as an 84th-minute substitute for [[Valentín Castellanos]] in a 2–1 loss.<ref>{{cite web|title=New York Red Bulls 2, New York City FC 1 – 2019 MLS Match Recap|url=https://matchcenter.mlssoccer.com/matchcenter/2019-07-14-new-york-red-bulls-vs-new-york-city-fc/recap|publisher=MLSsoccer.com|last=Boehm|first=Charles|date=14 July 2019}}</ref> He scored his first goal on his 29th birthday on 31 August in a 3–1 win at [[Vancouver Whitecaps FC]], after replacing the injured [[Héber Araujo dos Santos|Héber]].<ref>{{cite news |title=NYCFC dispose of Whitecaps for 4th straight win |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/report?gameId=533068 |access-date=2 October 2019 |agency=Reuters|publisher=ESPN FC |date=1 September 2019}}</ref>

Following their 2020 season, Mackay-Steven departed the club after [[New York City F.C.|New York City]] opted to decline their contract option for Mackay-Steven.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nycfc.com/news/new-york-city-fc-announces-roster-moves-2021|title=New York City FC Announces Roster Moves For 2021|first=New York City|last=FC|website=New York City FC}}</ref>

===Heart of Midlothian===

On 8 January 2021, Mackay-Steven returned to Scotland to sign with [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] on a deal to run until the summer of 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|title=GMS joins Jambos {{!}} Heart of Midlothian Football Club|url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/article/gms-joins-jambos|access-date=2021-08-04|website=heartsfc.co.uk}}</ref>

Mackay-Steven only made six appearances for Hearts during the [[2022–23 Heart of Midlothian F.C. season|2022–23 season]], as he suffered a foot injury in December.<ref name = killie/> Hearts announced in May that Mackay-Steven would leave the club at the end of the season,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/article/trio-to-leave|title=Trio to leave|website=heartsfc.co.uk|date=25 May 2023|accessdate=25 May 2023}}</ref> although he was allowed the use of their facilities as he recovered from the foot injury.<ref name = killie/>

===Kilmarnock===
Mackay-Steven started training with [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] during October 2023,<ref name = killie>{{Cite news |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/23867191.gary-mackay-steven-kilmarnock-contract-chances-addressed/ |title=Gary Mackay-Steven Kilmarnock contract chances addressed |newspaper=The Herald |first=Ewan |last=Paton |date=19 October 2023 |accessdate=20 October 2023}}</ref> and he signed a short-term contract with the club in December.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cpdpe31nvx3o |title=Mackay-Steven joins Kilmarnock on short-term deal |publisher=BBC Sport |date=5 December 2023 |accessdate=5 December 2023}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle===
In March 2026, Mackay-Steven signed a short term deal with [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/gary-mackay-steven-signs-on-a-short-term-deal/|title=Gary Mackay-Steven signs on a short-term deal|website=Partick Thistle FC}}</ref> 

Mackay-Steven made his Thistle debut, coming off the bench in a 2–0 home win over [[Dunfermline Athletic]] in the Scottish Championship.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4glq195ppkt|title=Partick Thistle vs Dunfermline Athletic: Championship stats & head-to-head|first=Live|last=Text|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> 

MacKay-Steven signed a one year contract extension with Thistle in June 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/gary-mackay-steven-extends-firhill-stay/|title=Gary Mackay-Steven extends Firhill stay|website=Partick Thistle FC}}</ref>

MacKay-Steven scored his first and second goal for Thistle in a 6–0 home win over Brechin City in a [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage tie.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cn0vv0zzk78t|title=Partick Thistle vs Brechin City: Scottish League Cup score updates & stats|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|access-date=July 31, 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Mackay-Steven made his first international appearance for [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] on 15 November 2013, replacing [[Craig Conway (footballer)|Craig Conway]] for the last six minutes of a goalless friendly draw against the [[USMNT|United States]] at [[Hampden Park]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Lamont|first1=Alasdair|title=Scotland 0-0 USA|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/24862652|access-date=7 January 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=15 November 2013}}</ref>

He was recalled to the Scotland squad in October 2018, for a friendly against [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45850784 |title=Scotland: Charlie Mulgrew, John Souttar, Kieran Tierney and Robert Snodgrass withdraw from squad |first=Jane |last=Lewis |publisher=BBC Sport |date=13 October 2018 |access-date=15 October 2018}}</ref> He came on as a substitute in the 67th minute, and assisted [[Steven Naismith]] in scoring Scotland's only goal of the game.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45173871 |title=Scotland 1–3 Portugal |publisher=BBC Sport |date=14 October 2018 |access-date=15 October 2018 |first=Tom |last=English}}</ref>

==Personal life==
On 27 August 2017, Mackay-Steven was rescued from the [[River Kelvin]] in [[Glasgow]] after falling in. He was taken to [[Queen Elizabeth University Hospital]] where he was treated for [[hypothermia]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Footballer Gary Mackay-Steven is pulled from River Kelvin|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-glasgow-west-41071609|access-date=28 August 2017|publisher=BBC News|date=28 August 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Gary Mackay-Steven opens up over River Kelvin incident|url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/aberdeen/gary-mackay-steven-opens-up-over-river-kelvin-incident-1-4565173|date=20 September 2017|work=The Scotsman|access-date=24 June 2019}}</ref>

'''Cristian Alexis Montaño Castillo''' (born 11 December 1991) is a Colombian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays for {{Scottish football updater|Livingst}} club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]]. A versatile player, he can play at [[Defender (association football)|left-back]] or as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]], though his preferred position is as a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]]; he is known for his pace.

Born in [[Cali]], Colombia, he emigrated to London at a young age and joined the [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] [[West Ham United F.C. Reserves|Academy]]. He never played a first-team game for the club. He did play on [[Loan (sports)|loan]] at [[Notts County F.C.|Notts County]], [[Swindon Town F.C.|Swindon Town]], [[Dagenham & Redbridge F.C.|Dagenham & Redbridge]] and [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]]. He was signed by [[Oldham Athletic A.F.C.|Oldham Athletic]] in August 2012 but was sacked in December 2013 after being arrested for [[spot-fixing]] and [[rape]]. All charges were later dropped, and he returned to his hometown in Colombia to play for [[América de Cali]]. He returned to England and joined [[Bristol Rovers F.C.|Bristol Rovers]] in July 2015. He helped the club to win [[Promotion and relegation|promotion]] out of League Two in 2015–16 before he moved on to [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]] in June 2017. He stayed at [[Vale Park]] for four seasons, where he learned to play at left-back. He signed with Livingston in May 2021. The club were relegated from the [[Scottish Premiership]] in 2024, though managed to win the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] the following year before winning promotion via the play-offs in 2025.

== Early life ==
Born in [[Cali]], Colombia, Montaño moved to [[London]] as a child and holds the nationality of both Colombia and the United Kingdom.<ref name=U12>{{cite web|title=Cristian signs|url=http://www.whufc.com/articles/20100621/cristian-signs_2236884_2074131|publisher=West Ham United F.C.|access-date=6 August 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Youth – 2009/10|url=http://www.whufc.com/articles/20100601/youths-200910-squad_2236884_1368925|publisher=whufc.com|access-date=5 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120313034940/http://www.whufc.com/articles/20100601/youths-200910-squad_2236884_1368925|archive-date=13 March 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> He recalled that he "always heard gun shots growing up in Colombia", before moving to England at the age of ten to join his mother, who had emigrated four years previously.<ref>{{cite news|title=Cristian Montano shooting for the stars, after once dodging bullets|url=http://www.nottinghampost.com/cristian-montano-shooting-stars-dodging-bullets/story-15222960-detail/story.html|access-date=22 June 2017|work=Nottingham Post|date=14 February 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140727144719/http://www.nottinghampost.com/Cristian-Montano-shooting-stars-dodging-bullets/story-15222960-detail/story.html|archive-date=27 July 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Playing career==

===West Ham United===
Montaño joined [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] as an [[West Ham United F.C. Reserves|under-12 player]] before he signed his first professional [[Association football contracts|contract]] in June 2010.<ref>{{cite news |title=Young striker signs |url=https://www.guardian-series.co.uk/sport/westham/8230220.cristian-is-latest-graduate-from-hammers-academy/ |access-date=19 August 2020 |work=East London and West Essex Guardian Series |date=21 June 2010 |language=en}}</ref> In August 2011, he signed a one-month [[Loan (sports)|loan]] deal with [[EFL League One|League One]] side [[Notts County F.C.|Notts County]],<ref name="Nottsco1">{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14426609 | title=Notts County sign West Ham forward Cristian Montaño | publisher=BBC Sport | date=5 August 2011 | access-date=5 August 2011}}</ref> making his debut on 9 August in a [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] game against [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]], which Notts County lost on penalties after the game had finished 3–3.<ref name=Debut>{{cite news|title=Nott'm Forest 3 – 3 Notts County|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/league_cup/14368484.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=10 August 2011|date=9 August 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Montano makes league bow|url=http://www.whufc.com/articles/20110809/montano-makes-league-bow_2236884_2415336|publisher=West Ham United F.C.|access-date=10 August 2011}}</ref> He scored on his [[English Football League|league]] debut four days later in a 2–1 defeat to [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] at [[Meadow Lane]].<ref name=LeagueDebut>{{cite news|title=Notts County 1 – 2 Charlton| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14429694|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=14 August 2011|date=13 August 2011}}</ref> His loan with the "Magpies" was extended until 9 October,<ref name=Loan2>{{cite web|title=Cristian signs for longer|url=http://www.whufc.com/articles/20110905/cristian-signs-for-longer_2236884_2441314|publisher=West Ham United F.C.|access-date=5 September 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120119092521/http://www.whufc.com/articles/20110905/cristian-signs-for-longer_2236884_2441314|archive-date=19 January 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> after which he returned to West Ham. [[Manager (association football)|Manager]] [[Martin Allen]] said that "he's a fantastic player and what a lovely lad. He's humble, hard-working and dedicated".<ref>{{cite news|title=Notts boss Martin Allen closes in on Montano replacement|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/15242265|access-date=22 June 2017|publisher=BBC Sport|date=10 October 2011}}</ref>

Soon after leaving Notts County, Montaño signed a one-month loan deal with [[Swindon Town F.C.|Swindon Town]] of [[EFL League Two|League Two]].<ref name="Robins">{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/15289676 | title=Swindon Town sign West Ham forward Montano on loan | publisher=BBC Sport | date=13 October 2011 | access-date=13 October 2011}}</ref> He made his debut for the "Robins" on 15 October, scoring the second goal in a 2–0 away win against [[Accrington Stanley F.C.|Accrington Stanley]].<ref name="Robins2">{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/15225790 | title=Accrington 0–2 Swindon | publisher=BBC Sport | date=15 October 2011 | access-date=16 October 2011}}</ref> His loan was cut short in November and he returned to the [[Boleyn Ground]] having scored one goal in four appearances.<ref name=whuagain>{{cite news|title=West Ham's Cristian Montano in early Swindon Town exit|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/15646225|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=9 November 2011}}</ref> Swindon boss [[Paolo Di Canio]] said that "I don't know if he feels part of Swindon Town. He didn't prove this to me."<ref>{{cite news|title=Swindon manager Paolo Di Canio unsure on Montano stay|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/15589603.app|access-date=22 June 2017|publisher=BBC Sport|date=4 November 2011}}</ref> Days after leaving Swindon, Montaño signed a one-month loan deal with League Two rivals [[Dagenham & Redbridge F.C.|Dagenham & Redbridge]].<ref name=daggers>{{cite news|title=Dagenham & Redbridge sign Montano and Spillane|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/15781964|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=17 November 2011}}</ref> He scored on his debut for the "Daggers" in a 3–2 defeat to [[Southend United F.C.|Southend United]] at [[Victoria Road (Dagenham)|Victoria Road]] on 19 November.<ref name=Dagdebut>{{cite news|title=Dag & Red 2 – 3 Southend|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/15705020|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=20 November 2011}}</ref> Montaño's loan was twice extended as manager [[John Still (footballer)|John Still]] felt that "it gives us a player who has done very well for a little bit longer."<ref name="daggers extend loan">{{cite news|title=Dagenham & Redbridge keep West Ham striker Montano|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16265328|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=2 January 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=West Ham's Cristian Montano signs Dagenham & Redbridge extension|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16595845|access-date=22 June 2017|publisher=BBC Sport|date=17 January 2012}}</ref>

Montaño again joined Notts County on loan in February 2012.<ref>{{cite news|title=Notts County sign Cristian Montaño for a second loan spell|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/16950951|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=8 February 2012}}</ref> However, he played only four games in his second spell and the loan was not extended and 'dreamland'|url=http://www.thisisnottingham.co.uk/Notts-County-boss-Curle-dreamland/story-15496421-detail/story.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130527195830/http://www.thisisnottingham.co.uk/Notts-County-boss-Curle-dreamland/story-15496421-detail/story.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=27 May 2013|publisher=thisisnottingham.co.uk|access-date=12 March 2012}}</ref> On 16 March, Montaño returned to League Two when he joined [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]] on loan as a replacement for ex-loanee [[Lee Holmes]].<ref name="oufc">{{cite web | url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17397557 | title = Oxford United sign West Ham forward Cristian Montaño | publisher = BBC Sport | date= 16 March 2012 | access-date = 16 March 2012}}</ref> His first goal for the "U's" came on 7 April in a 2–1 away defeat to [[Northampton Town F.C.|Northampton Town]].<ref name="u's">{{cite news|title=Substitute Brett Williams scored an injury-time winner for Northampton against Oxford United in a lively League Two encounter.|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17558723|publisher=BBC Sport|date=7 April 2012|access-date=10 September 2020}}</ref> Manager [[Chris Wilder]] decided to extend the loan spell after in 39 appearances for four different clubs across five separate loan spells during the [[2011–12 West Ham United F.C. season|2011–12]] season.<ref name="2011/12"/>

===Oldham Athletic===
In August 2012, Montaño signed a two-year contract with [[Oldham Athletic A.F.C.|Oldham Athletic]], with the option of a third year, for an undisclosed fee (reported as being £50,000).<ref>{{cite web|title=Latics sign Montaño|url=http://www.oldhamathletic.co.uk/news/article/170812-montano-317817.aspx|publisher=Oldham Athletic A.F.C|access-date=17 August 2012}}</ref><ref name="herb"/> Manager [[Paul Dickov]] said that: "I gather he could have stayed at West Ham, but he was keen to move because of his wish to play football rather than being a squad player."<ref>{{cite news|title=Montano can be matchwinner|url=https://www.oldhamathletic.co.uk/news/2012/august/montano-can-be-matchwinner/|access-date=22 June 2017|work=oldhamathletic.co.uk|date=17 August 2012}}</ref> He scored two goals in 33 games in the [[2012–13 Oldham Athletic A.F.C. season|2012–13]] campaign after missing two months with a [[Strain (injury)|tore]] [[thigh]] muscle.<ref>{{cite news|title=Cristian Montano: Oldham Athletic winger out for two months|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20957248|access-date=22 June 2017|publisher=BBC Sport|date=9 January 2013}}</ref> He scored twice in 15 games in the first half of the [[2013–14 Oldham Athletic A.F.C. season|2013–14]] season.<ref name="2013–14"/>

He was sacked by the club in December 2013 on the grounds of gross misconduct relating to alleged [[spot-fixing]] in relation to the [[2013 English match fixing scandal]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Montaño sacked|url=http://www.oldhamathletic.co.uk/news/article/20131216statement-1238989.aspx|publisher=Oldham Athletic A.F.C|access-date=16 December 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20131216112327/http://www.oldhamathletic.co.uk/news/article/20131216statement-1238989.aspx|archive-date=16 December 2013}}</ref> He said he was preparing to head to Manchester to speak to manager [[Lee Johnson (footballer)|Lee Johnson]] when a club director rang to ask his location, the director then informed the police, who came to his location and arrested him, and the club announced that they had sacked Montaño whilst he was at the police station; he said "no-one from Oldham spoke to me about it. ... they were turning against me, I was left on my own".<ref>{{cite news|last1=Smith|first1=Ben|title=Cristian Montano: Ex-Oldham winger angry at double standards|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31002710|access-date=22 June 2017|publisher=BBC Sport|date=27 January 2015}}</ref> In November 2014, having been released from [[bail]] but with investigation still ongoing by the [[National Crime Agency]], Montaño announced his intention to sue Oldham Athletic for unlawful dismissal and loss of earnings; this would be the remaining £39,000 of his £1,500 a week wages and compensation of £76,500.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30126234 | title=Cristian Montano: Ex-Oldham star accused of spot-fixing to sue club | publisher=BBC Sport | date=24 November 2014 | access-date=24 November 2014}}</ref><ref name="herb">{{cite news|last1=Herbert|first1=Ian|title=More woe for Oldham as sacked player plans to sue for £100,000|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/news-and-comment/more-woe-for-oldham-as-sacked-player-plans-to-sue-for-100000-9981670.html|access-date=22 June 2017|work=The Independent|date=15 January 2015}}</ref> The spot-fixing charges were dropped in January 2015.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Chambers|first1=Matthew|title=Case against Montano withdrawn|url=https://www.oldham-chronicle.co.uk/news-features/10/oldham-athletic-news/89854/case-against-montano-withdrawn|publisher=Oldham Evening Chronicle|access-date=18 January 2015|date=15 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Football 'spot-fixing' case dropped|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-30815575|publisher=BBC News|access-date=18 January 2015|date=15 January 2015}}</ref>

{{Blockquote|"I had got no club. I thought my life was over, all I know is football. Then I saw all the abuse I was getting on [[Twitter]]. How much people were talking. People wishing bad on me, saying, 'I hope someone breaks your legs'. Other people were laughing at me and telling me I wouldn't get back into football and wishing the worst on me. Listening to what people were saying about me on social media led to me thinking about taking my own life."|Montaño was suicidal after facing possible financial ruin and the prospect of the criminal charges costing him his career, as well as turning friends and supporters against him.<ref name="suicide">{{cite news |last1=Ault |first1=Richard |title=Port Vale's Cristian Montano reveals how he 'thought his life was over' |url=https://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/sport/port-vales-cristian-montano-reveals-4292061 |access-date=6 July 2020 |work=Stoke Sentinel |date=6 July 2020}}</ref>}}

===América de Cali===
Following his dismissal by Oldham Athletic, Montaño returned to his hometown to play for [[América de Cali]] in the [[Categoría Primera B]]; he slept on a friend's couch and took a bus to the [[Training ground (association football)|training ground]].<ref name="suicide"/> He scored one goal in nine league games in the [[2014 Categoría Primera B season|2014]] season to help the "Scarlets" to a fifth-place finish and also made seven appearances in the [[Copa Colombia]]. He featured twice at the [[Estadio Olímpico Pascual Guerrero]] in the [[2015 Categoría Primera B season|2015]] season before returning to England after the criminal charges against him were dropped.<ref name="suicide"/>

===Bristol Rovers===

[[File:Cristian Montaño 30-04-2016 1.jpg|thumb|upright|Montaño playing for [[Bristol Rovers F.C.|Bristol Rovers]] in 2016]]

Montaño joined [[Bristol Rovers F.C.|Bristol Rovers]] in July 2015; manager [[Darrell Clarke]] stated that "he comes with quite a lot of baggage [but] I know that he is desperate for another opportunity to play league football and I'm a firm believer in giving everyone a second chance".<ref>{{cite news|title=Cristian Montano: Bristol Rovers give midfielder 'second chance'|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33370186|access-date=29 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=2 July 2015}}</ref> He scored two goals in 31 appearances as the "Gas" secured automatic [[Promotion and relegation|promotion]] out of League Two in [[2015–16 Bristol Rovers F.C. season|2015–16]]. He signed a contract extension of an undisclosed length in June 2016.<ref>{{cite news|title=Cristian Montano: Bristol Rovers forward agrees new contract|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36568510|access-date=22 June 2017|publisher=BBC Sport|date=18 June 2016}}</ref> He played 31 games in the [[2016–17 Bristol Rovers F.C. season|2016–17]] campaign before he was released in April 2017.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bristol Rovers: Five offered new deals but eight to leave, including Christian Montano|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39744945|access-date=22 June 2017|publisher=BBC Sport|date=28 April 2017}}</ref> Clarke said that "Montaño was a very tough decision, it was borderline really. But there has to be a freshness and a bigger freshness than we've had in the last couple of seasons".<ref>{{cite news|last1=Vittles|first1=Jack|title=Clarke on why Montano is leaving but Gaffney and Harrison are staying|url=https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/darrell-clarke-explains-thinking-bristol-40068|access-date=22 June 2017|work=Bristol Post|date=29 April 2017}}</ref>

Aspin]], who claimed it was a "soft" penalty.<ref>{{cite news|title=Neil Aspin: Port Vale boss says two red cards in FA Cup exit at Yeovil were 'kick in Under-21s and Academy|Stoke City U21]] in the [[EFL Trophy]]; Aspin went on to say that Montaño had been disappointing at left-back at the start of the campaign, but had been excellent in his traditional role as a left-winger.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Baggaley |first1=Michael |title=Port Vale's Neil Aspin looking forward with Cristian Montano |url=https://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/port-vale-cristian-montano-aspin-2305413 |access-date=8 December 2018 |work=Stoke Sentinel |date=7 December 2018}}</ref> The performance against Stoke earned him the EFL Trophy's Player of the second round award.<ref name="potr">{{cite web |title=Cristian Montano scoops Checkatrade award |url=https://www.port-vale.co.uk/news/2019/january/cristian-montano-scoops-award/ |website=port-vale.co.uk |access-date=16 January 2019 |language=en-gb}}</ref> He ended the campaign with seven goals in 20 starts and 13 substitute appearances.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sherwin |first1=Phil |title=From local heroes who impressed to lost boys: Port Vale class of 2018/19 rated |url=https://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/port-vale-player-ratings-201819-2885390 |access-date=19 May 2019 |work=Stoke Sentinel |date=19 May 2019}}</ref>

|last1=Baggaley |first1=Michael |title=Robbie Earle – Injured Port Vale winger needs change of luck not criticism |url=https://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/robbie-earle-injured-port-vale-3075576 |access-date=10 July 2019 |work=Stoke Sentinel |date=10 July 2019}}</ref> Though [[John Askey]] Rovers official matchday programme |date=15 December 2020 |url=https://pvfc-shop.com/portvale/download/TEHVFGQwGgvnf6NUyMY1.pdf |access-date=19 August 2023}}</ref> Port Vale appointed former Bristol Rovers boss Darrell Clarke as the club's new manager and he expressed his surprise at how well Montaño could play at left-back.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Baggaley |first1=Michael |title=Every word from Port Vale manager ahead of Colchester game |url=https://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/vale-press-conference-clarke-colchester-5204787 |access-date=20 March 2021 |work=StokeonTrentLive |date=19 March 2021 |language=en}}</ref> He was sent off for dissent in his final game for the club, much to Clarke's anger.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Baggaley |first1=Michael |title='Sleepless nights' about Port Vale contract decisions |url=https://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/port-vale-contracts-darrell-clarke-5367044 |access-date=2 May 2021 |work=StokeonTrentLive |date=2 May 2021 |language=en}}</ref> At the end of the [[2020–21 Port Vale F.C. season|2020–21]] season however, it was announced that Montano's contract would not be renewed and he would be leaving the club later that month.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.port-vale.co.uk/news/2021/may/202021-retained-list/|title=2020/21 Retained List|website=port-vale.co.uk|date=10 May 2021}}</ref>

===Livingston===
On 12 May 2021, Montaño signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on a two-year deal with the club having the option of an additional year following a lengthy pursuit by manager [[David Martindale]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Livingston sign Port Vale's Montano |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57085901 |access-date=12 May 2021 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=12 May 2021}}</ref> Injuries restricted him to just 11 appearances and six starts in the first half of the [[2021–22 Livingston F.C. season|2021–22]] season, only managing to get a run of games in December.<ref>{{cite news |title=Cristian Montano finding his feet after a testing start to his Livingston career |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/cristian-montano-finding-his-feet-after-a-testing-start-to-his-livingston-career-1639157181000 |access-date=28 May 2022 |work=fourfourtwo.com |date=10 December 2021 |language=en}}</ref> However, he was then again sidelined with a hamstring injury.<ref>{{cite news |title=Cristian Montano sidelined for up to three weeks as Livingston host Ross County |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/cristian-montano-sidelined-for-up-to-three-weeks-as-livingston-host-ross-county-1639764429000 |access-date=28 May 2022 |work=fourfourtwo.com |date=17 December 2021 |language=en}}</ref> On 5 February, he was sent off after receiving two yellow cards during a 2–1 win over [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] at the [[Almondvale Stadium]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Herrall |first1=Jack |title=Livingston defended 'magnificently' |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/60178916 |access-date=28 May 2022 |work=BBC Sport |date=5 February 2022}}</ref> He started just seven league games for the "Lions" in his debut season, featuring 19 times in total.<ref name="2021–22"/> However, he started the [[2022–23 Livingston F.C. season|2022–23]] season in fine form, and his third goal of the campaign moved Livingston into third place with a 1–0 win over [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on 17 September.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Gordon |first1=Phil |title=Cristian Montano keeps Livingston flying high |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/cristian-montano-keeps-livingston-flying-high-rfvt30qvz |access-date=12 May 2023 |work=[[The Times]] |date=18 September 2022 |language=en}}</ref> He ended the season with four Premiership goals from 25 starts and six substitute appearances.<ref name="2022–23"/> He was sidelined for six weeks after sustaining a calf injury in training in August 2023.<ref>{{cite news |title=Lloyd banks Livi deal after Montano injury |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/czr142rr93ko |access-date=14 May 2024 |work=BBC Sport |date=29 August 2023}}</ref> He picked up another injury in January.<ref>{{cite news |title=Martindale keen to add to Livingston squad after Montano injury |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/david-martindale-keen-to-add-to-livingston-squad-after-cristian-montano-injury |access-date=14 May 2024 |work=STV News |date=24 January 2024}}</ref> He was named on the Premiership Team of the Week for his performance in a 2–1 win over [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on 11 May 2024.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sutherland |first1=Jonathan |title=Livingston: Montano makes Premiership team of the week |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c1366l8g0pzo |access-date=14 May 2024 |work=BBC Sport |date=13 May 2024}}</ref> On 30 March 2025, he won the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] with Livingston as they beat [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] by five goals to nil in the final at the [[Falkirk Stadium]].<ref name="scc25">{{cite news |title=Queen's Park vs Livingston: SPFL Trust Trophy final stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cz03vzdrgmpt#Report |access-date=14 April 2025 |work=BBC Sport |date=30 March 2025}}</ref> Promotion back to the Premiership was then secured with a 5–3 aggregate victory over [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] in the play-off final.<ref name="prom25">{{cite news |last1=Campbell |first1=Andy |title=Ross County 2-4 Livingston (3-5 agg): Livingston come from two goals down to stun County in the Premiership play-off final |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cpd41v9p65xt#Report |access-date=26 May 2025 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

Montaño signed a new two-year contract in July 2025.<ref>{{cite news |title=Livingston: Winger Cristian Montano signs new two-year deal |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cn5kngkxv63o |access-date=20 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport |date=18 July 2025}}</ref> On 27 December, he scored a brace against [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], though Livingston lost the game by four goals to two to keep themselves at the bottom of the table and without a win in 16 league games.<ref>{{cite news |title=PressReader.com - Digital Newspaper & Magazine Subscriptions |url=https://www.pressreader.com/uk/the-national-scotland/20251229/282110642968099 |access-date=4 January 2026 |work=The National |date=29 December 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Wilson |first1=Fraser |title=Livingston star's son's Celtic premonition left him thinking 'what's going on?' |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/livingston-star-reveals-sons-spooky-36464921 |access-date=4 January 2026 |work=Daily Record |date=28 December 2025 |language=en}}</ref> On 22 February, he was sent off for a last-man challenge on [[Djeidi Gassama]] in a 2–2 draw with [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Petrie |first1=Andrew |title=Livingston vs Rangers: Scottish Premiership updates & match report |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4g2d505g24t?page=4 |access-date=5 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport |date=22 February 2026}}</ref> He played 28 games in the [[2025–26 Livingston F.C. season|2025–26]] season,<ref name="2025–26"/> which culminated in relegation.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lindsay |first1=Clive |title=Livingston relegation confirmed after Kilmarnock win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c8d8m2mpp47o |access-date=20 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport |date=2 May 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In December 2013, Montaño and two friends were charged with the [[rape]] of a woman in [[Romford]], London.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.oldham-chronicle.co.uk/news-features/8/news-headlines/83848/sacked-montano-on-rape-charge | title=Sacked Montano on rape charge | publisher=Oldham Chronicle|date=17 December 2013 | access-date=13 March 2014}}</ref> He appeared in court in March 2014. He admitted to having sex with the woman but maintained it was entirely consensual.<ref name="consent"/><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.newhamrecorder.co.uk/news/court-crime/former_west_ham_player_cristian_montano_and_friends_gang_raped_woman_at_romford_apartments_trial_hears_1_3426592 | title=Former West Ham player Cristian Montano and friends 'gang-raped' woman at Romford apartments, trial hears | publisher=Newham Recorder | date=12 March 2014 | access-date=13 March 2014 | archive-date=22 March 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140322225702/http://www.newhamrecorder.co.uk/news/court-crime/former_west_ham_player_cristian_montano_and_friends_gang_raped_woman_at_romford_apartments_trial_hears_1_3426592 | url-status=dead }}</ref> No verdict was returned by the jury and the prosecution dropped the case.<ref name="consent">{{cite web|title=Oldham Athletic star and his friends cleared of gang rape|url=http://www.hackneygazette.co.uk/news/crime-court/oldham_athletic_star_and_his_friends_cleared_of_gang_rape_1_3522088|work=Hackney Gazette|access-date=18 January 2015|date=4 April 2014|archive-date=30 January 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150130074256/http://www.hackneygazette.co.uk/news/crime-court/oldham_athletic_star_and_his_friends_cleared_of_gang_rape_1_3522088|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Gang rape case star is cleared|url=http://oldham-chronicle.co.uk/news-features/8/news-headlines/85355/gang-rape-case-star-is-cleared|publisher=Oldham Evening Chronicle|access-date=18 January 2015|date=4 April 2014}}</ref>

Speaking in July 2018, he stated that "My missus is English [and] my two kids were born in England".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Baggaley |first1=Michael |title=Port Vale's Colombian ace Cristian Montano previews England World Cup game |url=https://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/england-colombia-port-vale-montano-1742155 |access-date=3 July 2018 |work=Stoke Sentinel |date=3 July 2018}}</ref> In 2020, he began co-hosting a mental health [[podcast]] called ''The Men Unite Podcast'' with Daniel Biddulph.<ref>{{cite web |title=Listen to The Men Unite Podcast on TuneIn |url=https://tunein.com/podcasts/Health--Wellness-Podcasts/The-Men-Unite-Podcast-p1380041/ |website=TuneIn |access-date=21 March 2021 |language=en-us}}</ref> His partner, as of 2022, is finance worker Jo-Hannah Eardley.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lawrie |first1=Alexander |title=Partner of football ace banned from driving after leading police on chase |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/news/crime/edinburgh-crime-partner-of-livingston-fcs-cristian-montano-banned-from-driving-after-crash-and-police-chase-3728675 |access-date=12 May 2023 |work=Edinburgh News |date=12 June 2022 |language=en}}</ref>
