'''Jack Hamilton'''  (born 22 March 1994) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]], who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{Scottish football updater|Livingst}} club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], in his second spell with the club.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/jack-hamilton-hearts_2241487_56368 | title=Hearts Profile | publisher=[[Heart of Midlothian F.C.]] | date=10 September 2011 | access-date=12 September 2011 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927172649/http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/jack-hamilton-hearts_2241487_56368 | archive-date=27 September 2011 | df=dmy-all }}</ref> He has previously played for [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] and [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]], as well as [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]], [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]] and [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]] on loan.

==Club career==
===Early career===
Hamilton attended both Nethermains Primary School<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/competitions/premiership/jack-hamilton-out-to-improve-skills-to-become-sweeper-keeper-1-4267282| title=Jack Hamilton out to improve skills to become sweeper-keeper| publisher=[[The Scotsman]] | work=scotsman.com | date=25 October 2016 | accessdate=28 May 2018}}</ref> and [[Denny High School]]<ref>{{cite web | url=https://blogs.glowscotland.org.uk/fa/CurriculumSupport/2013/11/06/denny-high-school-pupils-film-local-sporting-celebrities/| title=Denny High School Pupils film local sporting celebrities| publisher=Falkirk Council Children's Services Curriculum Support| work=glowscotland.org.uk | date=6 November 2013 | accessdate=28 May 2018}}</ref> and was a youth player for local side [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]] from 12 years-old. In 2009, aged 14 he joined [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] (Hearts) youth team,<ref>{{cite web | url=http://sport.scotsman.com/heartofmidlothianfc/-Klim-can-be-a.4990648.jp | title=Klim | publisher=Scotsman Publications | work=Scotsman.com | date=18 February 2009 | accessdate=12 September 2011}}</ref> along with his brother [[Colin Hamilton (footballer)|Colin Hamilton]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.stenhousemuirfc.com/news/2009/03/12/28/ | title=Brothers Join Hearts | publisher=[[Stenhousemuir F.C.]] | date=12 March 2009 | accessdate=12 September 2011 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161017153323/http://www.stenhousemuirfc.com/news/2009/03/12/28/ | archive-date=17 October 2016 | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/jack-hamilton-hungry-for-more-action-with-hearts-1-3513771 | title=Jack Hamilton hungry for more action with Hearts | publisher=[[Edinburgh Evening News]] | work=edinburghnews.scotsman.com | date=19 August 2014 | accessdate=19 August 2014}}</ref>

===Heart of Midlothian===
A member of Hearts under-19 squad, in September 2011, Hamilton was promoted to the first team due to injury to [[Marián Kello]]. He was named as a substitute for a [[Scottish Premier League]] match at [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] but did not make an appearance.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14773007 | title=Inverness v Hearts | publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation | work=BBC Sport | date=10 September 2011 | access-date=12 September 2011}}</ref> On 30 November 2012, he moved to [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]] on a one-month loan,<ref>{{cite web|title=New Signings|url=http://www.forfarathletic.co.uk/index.php?option=com_flexicontent&view=items&cid=6%3Anews&id=836%3Anew-signings&Itemid=27|publisher=Forfar Athletic F.C.|date=30 November 2012|accessdate=31 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140104001953/http://www.forfarathletic.co.uk/index.php?option=com_flexicontent&view=items&cid=6%3Anews&id=836%3Anew-signings&Itemid=27|archive-date=4 January 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> which was then extended by a further month.<ref>{{cite web|title=Forfar extend goalkeeper's loan for further month|url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/forfar-extend-goalkeepers-loan-for-further-month/|publisher=Scottish Professional Football League|date=8 January 2013|accessdate=31 December 2016|archive-date=1 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170101161814/http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/forfar-extend-goalkeepers-loan-for-further-month/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He went out on loan again the following season, signing for [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]] in March 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=JACK MOVES TO METHIL|url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/3577|publisher=Heart of Midlothian F.C.|date=28 March 2014|accessdate=31 December 2016}}</ref>

At the start of the [[2014-15 Heart of Midlothian F.C. season|2014–15 season]] Hamilton joined [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]] on loan.<ref>{{cite web|title=Player Signings 2014/15 – Official – Three New 1st Team Squad Signings|url=http://www.stenhousemuirfc.com/news/2013/06/10/932/|publisher=Stenhousemuir F.C.|last=Bulloch|first=Terry|date=25 July 2014|accessdate=31 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140103035901/http://www.stenhousemuirfc.com/news/2013/06/10/932/|archive-date=3 January 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> Following injuries to [[Neil Alexander]], [[Scott Gallacher]] and Robbie Brown, he was recalled from his loan<ref>{{cite web | url=http://sport.stv.tv/football/clubs/hearts/288502-hearts-sign-goalkeeper-lee-hollis-with-scott-gallacher-a-doubt-for-derby/ | title=Hearts sign goalkeeper Lee Hollis with Scott Gallacher a doubt for derby | publisher=[[Scottish Television|STV]] | work=sport.stv.tv | date=15 August 2014 | accessdate=17 August 2014 }}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> and made his first team debut on 17 August 2014,<ref name="cup">{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28826795 | title=Robbie Neilson praises stand-in Hearts keeper Jack Hamilton | publisher=[[BBC Sport]] | work=bbc.co.uk/sport | date=17 August 2014 | access-date=17 August 2014}}</ref> playing from the start in a 2–1 win over [[Edinburgh derby]] rivals [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28730064 | title=Heart of Midlothian 2–1 Hibernian | publisher=[[BBC Sport]] | work=bbc.co.uk/sport | date=17 August 2014 | access-date=17 August 2014}}</ref>

In May 2016, Hamilton signed a contract extension, keeping him at Hearts until May 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Goalkeeper Jack Hamilton signs new deal with Hearts|url=http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/goalkeeper-jack-hamilton-signs-new-deal-with-hearts-1-4127598|publisher=Edinburgh Evening News|last=Anderson|first=Barry|date=13 May 2016|accessdate=31 December 2016}}</ref> Hamilton played regularly for Hearts during the 2016–17 season after Alexander was sold to Aberdeen, but lost his place to [[Jon McLaughlin (footballer)|Jon McLaughlin]] in the following season.<ref name = "dundee 2018"/>

===Dundee===
Hamilton signed a three-year contract with [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on 28 May 2018, for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/6705| title=Jack Leaves Hearts| publisher=[[Heart of Midlothian F.C.]] | work=heartsfc.co.uk | date=28 May 2018 | accessdate=28 May 2018}}</ref><ref name = "dundee 2018">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44277815 |title=Jack Hamilton: Dundee sign Hearts goalkeeper for undisclosed fee |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=28 May 2018 |accessdate=28 May 2018}}</ref> He made his debut on 14 July in a 4–0 win at [[Stirling Albion]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]], and manager [[Neil McCann]] praised his performance.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cran |first1=George |title=Neil McCann hails 'super stop' from keeper Jack Hamilton on Dundee debut |url=https://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/fp/neil-mccann-hails-super-stop-from-keeper-jack-hamilton-on-dundee-debut/ |accessdate=31 January 2019 |work=Evening Telegraph |date=17 July 2018}}</ref> On 4 August, in his first Premiership match for the Dee, he made a late error that allowed hosts [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] to win 2–1.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Campbell |first1=Andy |title=St Mirren 2–1 Dundee |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44989604 |accessdate=31 January 2019 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=4 August 2018}}</ref> Hamilton would find himself in and out of the starting role all season, as Dundee were eventually relegated at the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/dundee-0-1-hamilton-dark-blues-relegated-as-accies-edge-closer-to-safety-1-4920932|title=Dundee 0-1 Hamilton: Dark Blues relegated as Accies edge closer to safety|last=Pattullo|first=Alan|date=4 May 2019|website=The Scotsman|access-date=20 April 2020}}</ref> The following season in the [[Scottish Championship|Championship]] was once again full of inconsistencies for Hamilton, at one point conceding 6 goals to [[Dundee derby|rivals]] [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] in one game. He again spent the campaign swapping in and out of the starting position before the season was ended early due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic|coronavirus pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/spfl-resolution-approved-by-clubs-in-all-four-di|title=SPFL Resolution Approved By Clubs In All Four Divisions|last=|first=|date=15 April 2020|website=SPFL.co.uk|access-date=20 April 2020}}</ref>

Hamilton would leave Dundee at the conclusion of his contract in 2021, though would leave on a positive as Dundee confirmed promotion to the Premiership.<ref>{{Cite web|date=3 June 2021|title=Player departures|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/player-departures-8/|access-date=3 June 2021|website=dundeefc.co.uk}}</ref>

=== Greenock Morton ===
In July 2021, Hamilton signed a one-year deal with [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=6 July 2021|title=Goalkeeper Jack Hamilton signs for Morton|url=https://www.gmfc.net/goalkeeper-jack-hamilton-signs-for-morton/|access-date=7 July 2021|website=gmfc.net}}</ref> After playing every game of the [[2021–22 Greenock Morton F.C. season|2021–22 season]] for Morton, Hamilton would not sign an extension and would leave the club at the end of the season.

=== Livingston ===
On 19 August 2022, Hamilton signed a two-year deal with [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Black |first=Dave |date=2022-08-19 |title=Jack Hamilton joins the Lions |url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/jack-hamilton-joins-the-lions/ |access-date=2022-08-19 |website=Livingston FC |language=en-GB}}</ref> After making 8 appearances in two seasons, Livingston confirmed in May 2024 that Hamilton would depart the club upon the expiry of his contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Black |first=Dave |date=2024-05-20 |title=End of Season Retained & Released List |url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/end-of-season-retained-released-list/ |access-date=2024-06-01 |website=Livingston FC |language=en-GB}}</ref>

=== Ross County ===
In July 2024, Hamilton signed for [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] on a one-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 July 2024|title=Ross County complete signing of former Hearts and Dundee goalkeeper Jack Hamilton to challenge Ross Laidlaw for gloves in Dingwall|url=https://www.ross-shirejournal.co.uk/sport/ross-county-snap-up-former-hearts-goalkeeper-354727/|website=ross-shirejournal.co.uk|language=en-GB}}</ref> Hamilton made his competitive debut for the ''Staggies'' on 13 July in a win over [[Stranraer F.C.|Stranraer]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Stranraer vs Ross County: League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cl7y8rjdxk2t |access-date=2024-07-13 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Hamilton made his first league appearance for County on 30 November, coming on as a substitute away to [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] after starting keeper [[Ross Laidlaw]] was forced off with an injury.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Celtic vs Ross County: Scottish Premiership stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c5yrn0ngdd9t |access-date=2024-12-01 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

=== Return to Livingston ===
On 30 January 2025, Hamilton left Ross County by mutual consent and re-joined his former club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], now in the [[Scottish Championship]], on a permanent deal until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jack Hamilton joins Livingston |url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/jack-hamilton-joins-livingston |access-date=2025-01-31 |website=RCFC |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Black |first=Dave |date=2025-01-30 |title=Jack Hamilton rejoins the Lions |url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/jack-hamilton-rejoins-the-lions/ |access-date=2025-01-31 |website=Livingston FC |language=en-GB}}</ref> Hamilton was part of the Livingston squad which lifted the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]], spending the final as an unused substitute.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Queen's Park vs Livingston: SPFL Trust Trophy final stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cz03vzdrgmpt |access-date=2025-03-30 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Despite not making an appearance in his return season, Hamilton was part of the Livi squad which earned promotion to the [[Scottish Premiership]] through winning the [[2024–25 Scottish Premiership#Premiership play-offs|Premiership play-offs]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Livingston promoted {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/livingston-promoted |access-date=2025-05-29 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref> Following Livingston's promotion, the club announced that Hamilton had penned a new two-year deal with the club.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-19 |title=Goalkeeper Jack Hamilton signs new Livingston deal |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c0k7j2jm7kro |access-date=2025-06-21 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==International career==
Hamilton has represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-15 football team|under-15]],<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=454&playerID=63097&squadID=21 | title=Jack Hamilton – U15 Squad | publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]] | accessdate=12 September 2011}}</ref> [[Scotland national under-16 football team|under-16]],<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=454&playerID=63097&squadID=17 | title=Jack Hamilton – U16 Squad | publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]] | accessdate=12 September 2011}}</ref> [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17]],<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=454&playerID=63097&squadID=13 | title=Jack Hamilton – U17 Squad | publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]] | accessdate=12 September 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.uefa.com/under17/teams/player=250022719/index.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110915122020/http://www.uefa.com/under17/teams/player=250022719/index.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=15 September 2011 | title=Uefa Profile | publisher=[[UEFA]] | access-date=12 September 2011}}</ref> [[Scotland national under-18 football team|under-18]], [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]] and [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] levels.

On 20 May 2016, Hamilton received his first call-up to the [[Scotland national football team]] for their friendlies against [[Italy national football team|Italy]] and [[France national football team|France]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36339859 |title=Scotland call up Stephen Kingsley and Jack Hamilton |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=20 May 2016 |accessdate=10 June 2016}}</ref>

'''Cameron Kerr''' (born 10 September 1995) is a Scottish [[association football|football player]] and [[Manager (association football)|coach]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|Livingst}} club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].

Kerr spent the majority of his early career with his hometown club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], coming through the youth ranks and making 272 competitive appearances over 11 seasons, earning a [[Testimonial match|testimonial]] for his time there. He has also had loan spells with [[Peterhead F.C.|Peterhead]] twice and with [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]]. Kerr then spent a year with [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]].

==Career==

===Dundee===
While growing up, Kerr supported [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] and was a season ticket holder.<ref name="Cammy Kerr Dundee">{{cite news|title=I'm living a dream, says Dundee fan Kerr|url=http://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/sport/dundee-fc/i-m-living-a-dream-says-dundee-fan-kerr-1.112807|work=Dundee Evening Telegraph|date=17 July 2013|accessdate=19 July 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130801004807/http://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/sport/dundee-fc/i-m-living-a-dream-says-dundee-fan-kerr-1.112807|archivedate=1 August 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> Kerr joined the youth ranks of the club in 2003 at the age of 8, and was given his first professional contract in 2012 by manager [[Barry Smith (footballer, born 1974)|Barry Smith]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2024-07-16 |title=Cammy Kerr leaves Dundee FC |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/cammy-kerr-leaves-dfc/ |access-date=2024-07-16 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> He was included in the first team as an unused substitute on the final day of the [[Scottish Premier League|SPL]] season in 2012–13 against [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref name="Cammy Kerr Dundee Player Profile">{{cite news|title=Dundee Player Profile Cammy Kerr|url=http://www.dundeefc.co.uk/the-teams/first-team/player-profiles/cammy-kerr|publisher=[[Dundee F.C.|Dundee Profile]]|accessdate=19 July 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140416073335/http://www.dundeefc.co.uk/the-teams/first-team/player-profiles/cammy-kerr|archivedate=16 April 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In July 2013, Kerr was included in a number of first-team pre-season matches, where he featured as a right back.<ref name="Cammy Kerr Dundee Player Profile"/> The first of those appearances came in a 5–1 win over [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]], which he described as a "dream".<ref name="Cammy Kerr Dundee"/> Having been at Dundee for a couple of years, Kerr made his breakthrough into the first team in the 2013–2014 season, on 11 January 2014, appearing as a second-half substitute against [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Livingston steal show at Dens but Dundee stay top|url=http://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/sport/dundee-fc/livingston-steal-show-at-dens-but-dundee-stay-top-1.176049|work=Dundee Evening Telegraph|date=11 January 2014|accessdate=19 July 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140731165521/http://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/sport/dundee-fc/livingston-steal-show-at-dens-but-dundee-stay-top-1.176049|archivedate=31 July 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his first start on 12 April 2014, as Dundee beat [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dundeefc.co.uk/fixtures-and-results/dundee-vs-cowdenbeath-2 |title=DUNDEE VS COWDENBEATH |publisher=[[Dundee F.C.]] |accessdate=19 July 2014 |date=12 April 2014 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140719231908/http://www.dundeefc.co.uk/fixtures-and-results/dundee-vs-cowdenbeath-2 |archivedate=19 July 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Kerr said making his first start was a great experience, adding that the win made it better.<ref>{{cite news|title=Dundee youngster believes it is Dark Blues' time to shine|url=http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-fc/dundee-youngster-believes-it-is-dark-blues-time-to-shine-1.464624|work=The Courier|date=10 July 2014|accessdate=19 July 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129022004/http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-fc/dundee-youngster-believes-it-is-dark-blues-time-to-shine-1.464624|archivedate=29 November 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> He went on to make two more appearances for Dundee, both as starts, to fill in for the suspended [[Gary Irvine]]. The club went on to win the [[2013–14 Scottish Championship|Scottish Championship]] earning promotion to the [[Scottish Premiership]]. At the end of the 2013–14 season, Kerr signed a new deal at [[Dens Park]] to remain at the club for a further two years.<ref>{{cite news|title=Kerr signs new deal with Dundee|url=http://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/sport/dundee-fc/kerr-signs-new-deal-with-dundee-1.372819|work=Dundee Evening Telegraph|date=17 May 2014|accessdate=19 July 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129030902/http://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/sport/dundee-fc/kerr-signs-new-deal-with-dundee-1.372819|archivedate=29 November 2014|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

Kerr made his Scottish Premiership debut, coming on as a substitute for [[Jim McAlister (Scottish footballer)|Jim McAlister]] in the 43rd minute, in a 2–1 loss against [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] on 27 September 2014.<ref>{{cite news|title=Ross County 2 – 1 Dundee|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/29289909|publisher=BBC Sport|date=27 September 2014|accessdate=27 June 2015}}</ref> After making another Premiership appearance, he was loaned out to [[Peterhead F.C.|Peterhead]] on a one-month loan deal on 6 November 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=CAMMY JOINS PETERHEAD ON LOAN|url=http://www.dundeefc.co.uk/news/cammy-joins-peterhead-on-loan|accessdate=9 November 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141109225424/http://www.dundeefc.co.uk/news/cammy-joins-peterhead-on-loan|archivedate=9 November 2014|url-status=live}}</ref>

====Loans at Peterhead====
Kerr made his Peterhead debut on 8 November 2014, in a 1–1 draw against [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Peterhead 1 – 1 Dunfermline Athletic|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29860364|publisher=BBC Sport|date=8 November 2014|access-date=27 June 2015}}</ref> He scored his first Peterhead goal on 6 December 2014, in a 3–2 win over [[Stirling Albion F.C.|Stirling Albion]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Stirling Albion 2–3 Peterhead|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30257416|publisher=BBC Sport|date=6 December 2014|access-date=27 June 2015}}</ref> On 9 January 2015, he extended his loan-spell until the end of the [[2014–15 Scottish League One]] season.<ref>{{cite web|title=CAMMY EXTENDS LOAN|url=http://www.dundeefc.co.uk/news/cammy-extends-loan-2|accessdate=9 January 2015|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150109182409/http://www.dundeefc.co.uk/news/cammy-extends-loan-2|archivedate=9 January 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Weeks after extending his loan spell with the club, Kerr later added two more goals for the season against [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]]<ref>{{cite news|title=Peterhead 2–0 Stenhousemuir|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30963789|publisher=BBC Sport|date=31 January 2015|access-date=27 June 2015}}</ref> and [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Forfar Athletic 3–1 Peterhead|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31071725|publisher=BBC Sport|date=7 February 2015|access-date=27 June 2015}}</ref> Kerr went on to make twenty appearances for the club.

Kerr was again loaned to Peterhead for a four-month spell in August 2015<ref>{{cite web|title=Peterhead sign Cammy Kerr on loan from Dundee|url=https://www.eveningexpress.co.uk/fp/sport/football/scottish-football/peterhead-sign-cammy-kerr-on-loan-from-dundee/|publisher=Evening Express|last=Holme|first=Ben|date=21 August 2015|accessdate=17 July 2016}}</ref> and made a further 10 appearances in the [[2015–16 Scottish League One]] season.

===Return to Dundee===
Kerr was recalled from Peterhead early by Dundee in December 2015.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dundee boss Paul Hartley praises hat-trick hero for improved workrate|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-fc/134005/dundee-boss-paul-hartley-praises-hat-trick-hero-for-improved-workrate/|work=The Courier|last=Robertson|first=Neil|date=24 December 2015|accessdate=17 July 2016}}</ref> He was awarded man-of-the-match in his first Scottish Premiership starting appearance, a [[Dundee derby]] victory over [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] on 2 January 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dundee 2–1 Dundee United|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35179979|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Davie|first=Scott|date=2 January 2016|accessdate=17 July 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=I love being a local hero says Dundee fan Cammy Kerr|url=https://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/fp/love-local-hero-says-dundee-fan-cammy-kerr/|work=Evening Telegraph|last=Duthie|first=Tom|date=31 May 2016|accessdate=17 July 2016}}</ref>

Kerr went on to establish himself as a regular starter in the Dundee side. At the end of the 2016–17 season he was awarded the [[Dundee F.C.#Andrew De Vries Player of the Year|Dundee Player of the Year]] award alongside picking up the Young Player of the Year trophy for the third time.

At the start of the 2017–18 season Kerr was made vice-captain by manager [[Neil McCann]].

After finding himself in and out of the team during the [[2020–21 Dundee F.C. season|2020–21 season]], Kerr would be a key figure at both full-back positions as he helped Dundee to win the [[2020–21 Scottish Premiership#Premiership play-offs|Premiership play-offs]] and earn promotion back to the Premiership.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|date=24 May 2021|title=Dundee promoted as Kilmarnock drop down for first time in 28 years|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/live/football/57089947|url-status=live|access-date=24 May 2021|website=BBC|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210524150946/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/live/football/57089947 |archive-date=24 May 2021 }}</ref> At the end of the season, Kerr signed a new two-year deal, entitling him to a [[testimonial match]] in the [[2022–23 Dundee F.C. season|2022–23 season]], having spent ten senior years with Dundee despite being just 27 at season's end.<ref>{{Cite web|date=1 June 2021|title=Cammy signs new deal|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/cammy-signs-new-deal-3/|url-status=live|access-date=1 June 2021|website=dundeefc.co.uk|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210601123526/https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/cammy-signs-new-deal-3/ |archive-date=1 June 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Moncur |first=James |date=2022-04-21 |title=Former Dundee FC stars lining up for Cammy Kerr testimonial event |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/news/scottish-news/former-dundee-fc-stars-lining-26762081 |access-date=2022-05-25 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref>

In July 2022, Kerr scored goals in consecutive games for the first time in his career in the [[Scottish League Cup]] for Dundee, already making it his best goalscoring season for ''The Dark Blues''.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Stranraer v Dundee |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62124305 |access-date=2022-07-19}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Queen's Park v Dundee |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62209690 |access-date=2022-07-19}}</ref> On 6 January 2023, Kerr was named as [[Captain (association football)|captain]] in his 250th appearance for Dundee.<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 January 2023 |title=@DundeeFC on Twitter |url=https://twitter.com/dundeefc/status/1611439641302810629 |access-date=2023-01-06 |website=Twitter |language=en}}</ref> After coming back from an injury in February, Kerr wouldn't play for Dundee until coming on as a substitute in the [[Scottish Championship]] title-clinching win away to [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Dundee back in Premiership after eight-goal epic |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65420805 |access-date=2023-05-05}}</ref>

On 30 May 2023, Kerr signed a new two-year extension keeping him with Dundee until 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-30 |title=New contract for Cammy Kerr |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/new-contract-for-cammy/ |access-date=2023-05-30 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> After struggling to get regular game time under new manager [[Tony Docherty]], Kerr was informed in January 2024 that he was told he could find a new club.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cran |first=George |date=2024-01-21 |title=EXCLUSIVE: Dundee pair Cammy Kerr and Zak Rudden told they can find new clubs |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/4872585/exclusive-dundee-fc-cammy-kerr-zak-rudden-find-new-clubs/ |access-date=2024-01-22 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==== Inverness Caledonian Thistle (loan) ====
On 25 January 2024, Kerr joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Media |first=ICTFC |date=2024-01-25 |title=Cammy Kerr joins ICTFC on loan |url=https://ictfc.com/cammy-kerr-joins-ictfc-on-loan/ |access-date=2024-01-25 |website=ICTFC |language=en-GB}}</ref> He made his debut two days later, in an away league victory over [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Nine-minute Samuel hat-trick dents Raith's title bid |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68039855 |access-date=2024-01-27 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Kerr scored his first goal for the ''Caley Jags'' on 17 February in a league game against [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Partick Thistle battle back to draw in Inverness |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68144690 |access-date=2024-02-17 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Kerr would score for Caley in the [[2023–24 Scottish Championship#Final|Championship play-off final]] against [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]], but was unable to stop his side from being relegated to [[Scottish League One]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hamilton Academical win promotion and relegate Inverness CT |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cq5nnjx5wrzt |access-date=2024-05-18 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 16 July 2024, Kerr's 21 years of affiliation with [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] came to an end after both parties agreed to mutually terminate his contract.<ref name=":1" />

=== Queen's Park ===
On 16 July, the same day as leaving Dundee, Kerr signed for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] on a one-year deal with an option for an extension.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cairns |first=Ian |date=2024-07-16 |title=Cammy Kerr is latest signing for Queen's Park |url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/cammy-kerr-is-latest-signing-for-queens-park/ |access-date=2024-07-16 |website=Queen's Park Football Club |language=en-US}}</ref> Kerr made his debut for the ''Spiders'' that same day in a [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage defeat away to [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hibernian vs Queen's Park: League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/ce980gl6e6zt |access-date=2024-07-16 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 21 September, Kerr scored his first goal for Queen's Park in a league game against [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Queen's Park vs Ayr United: Scottish Championship |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c6259dz34vwt |access-date=2024-09-21 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> After a successful month, Kerr was named as the [[SPFL]] [[Scottish Championship]] [[List of Scottish Professional Football League monthly award winners|Player of the Month]] for September 2024.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Kerr lands Championship award {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/kerr-lands-championship-award |access-date=2024-10-07 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref> After not making an appearance for the ''Spiders'' since December due to injury, Kerr departed the club at the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oliver |first=David |date=2025-05-30 |title=Queen's Park FC - Squad update |url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/queens-park-fc-squad-update-season2425/ |access-date=2025-05-30 |website=Queen's Park Football Club |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Livingston ===
On 14 June 2025, Kerr returned to the [[Scottish Premiership]] after signing a deal with newly-promoted [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cran |first=George |date=2025-06-14 |title=Cammy Kerr to face Dundee next season after making Premiership return |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/5268986/cammy-kerr-premiership-dundee-top-flight-rivals/ |access-date=2025-06-14 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref> Kerr made his Livingston debut in a 2-1 away defeat against Celtic on 11 February 2026 after a long spell out injured.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kerr return delayed but 'not massive problem' |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c98n66dqp7zo |website=BBC Sport |access-date=17 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Celtic 2-1 Livingston |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/ckgkg6n2m15t |website=BBC Sport |access-date=17 February 2026}}</ref>

== Coaching career ==
In 2023, Kerr coached Scottish amateur side [[Monifieth Athletic]] while completing his [[Scottish Football Association|SFA]] coaching badges.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cran |first=George |date=2023-09-11 |title=Cammy Kerr the manager? Dundee star opens up on coaching amateurs Monifieth Athletic, saying 'I absolutely love it!' |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/4712641/cammy-kerr-manager-dundee-fc-coaching-amateurs-monifieth-athletic-love-it/ |access-date=2023-09-11 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref>

'''Sam Alastair Nicholson''' (born 20 January 1995)<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.mnufc.com/players/97/sam-nicholson | title=Sam Nicholson | work=Minnesota United FC | accessdate=10 July 2017}}</ref> is a Scottish [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a left winger or left midfielder for {{Scottish football updater|Livingst}} club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].

==Career==
===Heart of Midlothian===
Nicholson attended [[Penicuik High School]] in [[Midlothian]] and grew up supporting [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Sam Nicholson: Hearts role is a dream|url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/football/sam-nicholson-hearts-role-is-a-dream.1389370573?|newspaper=The Herald|location=Glasgow|date=10 January 2014|accessdate=10 January 2014}}</ref> He joined Hearts aged 12, progressing through their youth teams until on 31 August 2013, he made his senior debut for the club, coming on as a 74th-minute substitute in a [[Scottish Premiership (association football)|Scottish Premiership]] match against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]], replacing [[Jamie Walker (footballer)|Jamie Walker]] in a 2–0 defeat.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23822889 | title=Inverness remain top of the Scottish Premiership following a convincing victory over 10 man Hearts. | publisher=BBC Sport | date=31 August 2013 | access-date=31 August 2013}}</ref> His first senior goal for the side came on 18 January 2014, helping Hearts come from 3–1 down at [[McDiarmid Park]] scoring in the 89th minute to help Hearts earn a point in a 3–3 draw against [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25693251 | title=Two late goals rescued a point for Hearts against St Johnstone in a dramatic match at McDiarmid Park | publisher=BBC Sport | date=18 January 2014 | access-date=18 January 2014}}</ref>

On 16 June 2014, Nicholson signed a new three-year contract extending his stay until the summer of 2017, following the club's relegation to the [[Scottish Championship]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27872198 | title=Levein hails new three year deal for Sam Nicholson | publisher=BBC Sport | date=16 June 2014 | access-date=16 June 2014}}</ref>

Nicholson began the [[2014–15 Scottish Championship|2014–15 season]] by setting up a goal for [[Osman Sow]] at [[Ibrox Stadium|Ibrox]] in stoppage time. He scored his first goal of the season against [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibs]] in the [[Edinburgh Derby]]; a solo effort after he nutmegged Scott Robertson and hit a left-footed drive beyond the keeper.

===Minnesota United===
On 28 June 2017, it was confirmed that Nicholson agreed to a contract with [[Major League Soccer|MLS]] side [[Minnesota United FC]], and would be eligible to join the team on 10 July 2017.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.espnfc.us/minnesota-united-fc/story/3149888/minnesota-united-agrees-deal-to-sign-sam-nicholson-from-hearts-sources | title=Minnesota United agrees deal to sign Sam Nicholson from Hearts | publisher=ESPN FC | date=28 June 2017 | accessdate=29 June 2017}}</ref>

===Colorado Rapids===
Nicholson was traded from Minnesota to [[Colorado Rapids]] on 1 May 2018. Colorado also received an [[MLS International Roster Slots|International Roster slot]]. Minnesota received [[Eric Miller (soccer)|Eric Miller]] and $50,000 of General Allocation Money in return.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2018/04/30/mls-deadline-day-every-move-primary-transfer-window-closes | title=MLS Deadline Day: Every move as Primary Transfer Window closes | publisher=MLS | date=30 April 2018 | accessdate=2 May 2018}}</ref>

===Bristol Rovers===
On 22 July 2020, Nicholson returned to the UK, delighted to sign for [[EFL League One|League One]] club [[Bristol Rovers F.C.|Bristol Rovers]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bristolrovers.co.uk/news/2020/july/sam-nicholson-signs/ | title=Sam Nicholson Joins Rovers! | publisher=Bristol Rovers | date=22 July 2020 | accessdate=22 July 2020 | archive-date=9 February 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220209221720/https://www.bristolrovers.co.uk/news/2020/july/sam-nicholson-signs/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> He made his debut for the club on 5 September 2020, in a 3-0 [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] defeat to [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53955732|title=Ipswich Town 3-0 Bristol Rovers|publisher=BBC Sport|date=5 September 2020}}</ref> Nicholson scored his first goal for the club on 31 October 2020, opening the scoring in a 1–1 draw at [[Rochdale A.F.C|Rochdale]], driving forward with the ball before firing in from the edge of the box.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54671147|title=Rochdale 1–1 Bristol Rovers|publisher=BBC Sport|date=31 October 2020|accessdate=1 November 2020}}</ref> In late March 2021, Rovers' manager [[Joey Barton]] announced that Nicholson would miss the rest of the season as Rovers would fight against the drop, due to the fact that he was to have surgery on his hip,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56539536|title=Bristol Rovers: Max Ehmer and Sam Nicholson's seasons over due to surgery|publisher=BBC Sport|date=26 March 2021|accessdate=28 March 2021}}</ref> which it was announced in April 2021 he had still yet to have had the operation and would likely miss the start of the 2021–22 season also.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/nicholson-given-grim-diagnosis-barton-5308640|title=Nicholson given grim diagnosis as Barton eyes 'overhaul' of Bristol Rovers' internal structure|publisher=Bristol Post|date=16 April 2021|accessdate=17 April 2021}}</ref>

Nicholson opened his account for the [[2021–22 Bristol Rovers F.C. season|2021–22]] season as he opened the scoring in a [[EFL League Two|League Two]] 1–1 draw with [[Barrow A.F.C.|Barrow]], who had been reduced to ten men.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58289532|title=Barrow 1–1 Bristol Rovers|publisher=BBC Sport|date=28 August 2021}}</ref> The season ended in success for Nicholson and Rovers as a 7–0 victory on the final day of the season saw Rovers move into the final automatic promotion place on goals scored.<ref name="21/22 Promotion"/>

===Return to Colorado===
On 17 June 2022, it was announced that Nicholson had re-joined MLS side [[Colorado Rapids]] on a two-and-a-half-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.coloradorapids.com/news/colorado-rapids-sign-winger-sam-nicholson|title=Colorado Rapids sign winger Sam Nicholson|first=Colorado|last=Rapids|website=Colorado Rapids}}</ref> Nicholson made his second debut for the club in a 2–2 comeback draw with [[Real Salt Lake]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.coloradorapids.com/news/recap-rapids-launch-second-half-comeback-draw-rsl-2-2-on-the-road|title=Recap: Rapids launch second-half comeback, draw RSL 2–2 on the road|website=www.coloradorapids.com|date=10 July 2022|accessdate=10 July 2022}}</ref>

On 13 October 2023, it was announced that Nicholson had undergone ankle surgery to decompress the anterior and posterior right ankle joint, causing him to miss the final two games of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-13 |title=Colorado Rapids winger Sam Nicholson undergoes successful ankle surgery  |url=https://www.coloradorapids.com/news/colorado-rapids-winger-sam-nicholson-undergoes-successful-ankle-surgery |access-date=2023-10-13 |website=coloradorapids.com}}</ref>

Nicholson was waived by Colorado on 2 January 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/colorado-rapids-waive-danny-wilson-sam-nicholson|title=Colorado Rapids waive Danny Wilson & Sam Nicholson | MLSSoccer.com|website=mlssoccer}}</ref>

===Motherwell===
On 23 January 2024, Nicholson joined Scottish Premiership club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2024/01/23/sam-nicholson-arrives-at-fir-park/|title=Sam Nicholson arrives at Fir Park|website=www.motherwellfc.co.uk|date=23 January 2024|accessdate=24 January 2024}}</ref> On 31 May 2024, Motherwell announced that they had signed Nicholson to a permanent two-year contract.<ref name="Sam Nicholson 2026">{{cite web |title=SAM NICHOLSON SECURES PERMANENT ML1 SWITCH |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2024/05/31/sam-nicholson-returns/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=31 May 2024 |date=31 May 2024}}</ref>

Nicholson was at the centre of a highly controversial incident at the end of Motherwell's league tie against Celtic at [[Fir Park]] on 13 May 2026. In the fifth and final minute of injury time, with the score at 2-2, he challenged Celtic centre back [[Auston Trusty]] for the ball in the Motherwell penalty box. After Nicholson handled the ball away, Trusty went down holding the side of his face and, though referee [[John Beaton]] initially waved play on, he was eventually asked to go and look at the [[video assistant referee|VAR]]. Upon inspection, Beaton decided that Nicholson's hand had made contact with the ball during the header and gave a penalty to Celtic.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/celtic-penalty-var-hearts-motherwell-scottish-title-b2976192.html|title='Worst VAR decision ever seen': Hearts rage at 'disgusting' Celtic penalty call|last=Jackson|first=Kieran|date=13 May 2026|website=The Independent}}</ref> The penalty was converted by [[Kelechi Iheanacho]] to win the game 3-2, meaning that Celtic remained one point behind [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] in a dramatic title race.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/auston-trusty-var-celtic-missed-37157827|title=Motherwell complaint over Trusty sin that VAR snubbed amid Celtic penalty drama|first=Mark|last=Pirie|date=14 May 2026|website=Daily Record}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/26149602.sam-nicholson-inside-story-celtic-penalty/|title=Sam Nicholson Exclusive: The inside story of THAT Celtic penalty|date=29 May 2026|website=The Herald}}</ref>

===Livingston===
It was announced on 16 May 2026 that Nicholson would be joining [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] after his Motherwell contract expired.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/sam-nicholson-the-latest-new-recruit-to-join-the-lions/|title=Sam Nicholson the latest new recruit to join the Lions!|first=Dave|last=Black|date=17 May 2026|publisher=Livingston FC}}</ref>

'''Lee Ashcroft''' (born 29 August 1993) is a [[Scottish people|Scottish]] footballer who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|PartickT}} club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]]. Ashcroft previously played for [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] and [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], as well as on loan for [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]].

==Career==

Raised in [[Barrhead]], Ashcroft was not picked up by a professional club as a youth and had transitioned into local amateur leagues when he signed for [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] in 2010.<ref>[https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/killie-kid-lee-ashcroft-not-3490545 Killie kid Lee Ashcroft not worried about relegation.. he's just thrilled to be playing professional football], Gordon Parks, Daily Record, 3 May 2014</ref> He made his senior debut for the club on 11 May 2013, as a substitute in a 3–2 victory against [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] in the [[Scottish Premier League]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Dundee 2-3 Kilmarnock|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22409599|publisher=BBC Sport|date=11 May 2013|access-date=27 March 2014}}</ref> and then four days later scored his first career goal in a 3–1 loss against [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Kilmarnock 1-3 Hibernian|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22445395|publisher=BBC Sport|date=15 May 2013|access-date=27 March 2014}}</ref> On 14 May 2013, Ashcroft signed a new contract with Kilmarnock, keeping him at the club until 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rory McKenzie & Lee Ashcroft sign new contracts|url=http://www.kilmarnockfc.co.uk/articles/20130514/rory-mckenzie-lee-ashcroft-sign-new-contracts_85961_3178873|publisher=kilmarnockfc.co.uk|date=14 May 2013|accessdate=27 March 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140327235423/http://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/articles/20130514/rory-mckenzie-lee-ashcroft-sign-new-contracts_85961_3178873|archive-date=27 March 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> He captained Kilmarnock for the first time on 4 April 2015, aged 21, in a 2–1 defeat to [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] at [[Rugby Park]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Lee Ashcroft revels in role as Kilmarnock captain|url=https://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/sport/13305787.lee-ashcroft-revels-in-role-as-kilmarnock-captain/|publisher=Evening Times|date=10 April 2015|accessdate=29 September 2019}}</ref> On 23 May 2016, he was one of six players released at the end of their contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Player === Dunfermline Athletic ===
On 25 May 2016, Ashcroft signed for recently promoted [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36385515 |title=Dunfermline sign former Kilmarnock defender Lee Ashcroft |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=25 May 2016 |accessdate=25 May 2016}}</ref> making his first start for the club in a 3–0 victory over [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://dafc.co.uk/fixture.php?SID=First+Team&D=2016-07-19&ID=957 |title=Dunfermline 3 Arbroath 0 |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=19 July 2016 |accessdate=29 August 2016}}</ref> His first goal for the club was versus [[Fife derby|Fife rivals]] [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]] in the same competition, where he scored from a [[Kallum Higginbotham]] free-kick.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://dafc.co.uk/fixture.php?SID=First+Team&D=2016-07-23&ID=958 |title=Cowdenbeath 0 Dunfermline 3 |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=23 July 2016 |accessdate=29 August 2016}}</ref> Ashcroft's first [[Scottish Championship|league]] match for the Pars was versus [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]], and saw him concede a late penalty and receive a straight red for his last-man challenge on former Dunfermline striker [[Robert Thomson (footballer, born 1993)|Robert Thomson]], though Dunfermline ended the match as 4–3 winners.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36930838 |title=Dunfermline 4 – 3 Dumbarton |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=6 August 2016 |accessdate=29 August 2016}}</ref>

Ashcroft spent four seasons with the ''Pars'' and captained the club for the 2018–19 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.deadlinenews.co.uk/2018/07/26/lee-ashcroft-fits-the-bill-perfectly-as-allan-johnston-names-ex-kilmarnock-defender-as-new-dunfermline-captain/ |title=Lee Ashcroft 'fits the bill perfectly' as Allan Johnston names ex-Kilmarnock defender as new Dunfermline captain |first=Iain |last=Collin |work=Deadline News |publisher=Capital City Press |date=26 July 2018 |accessdate=24 May 2020}}</ref> He was released by the club in May 2020 following the expiry of his contract, having appeared in over 160 matches.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52768290 |title=Dunfermline release 17 players to 'protect future of club' |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=22 May 2020 |accessdate=24 May 2020}}</ref>

=== Dundee ===
In July 2020, Ashcroft signed a two-year deal with [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=23 July 2020|title=Lee is a Dee|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/lee-is-a-dee/|access-date=23 July 2020|website=Dundee FC}}</ref> A regular starter throughout the season, Ashcroft scored his first competitive goal for the Dee in a [[Scottish Cup]] win against [[Bonnyrigg Rose Athletic F.C.|Bonnyrigg Rose Athletic]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=9 January 2021|title=Dundee v Bonnyrigg Rose Athletic|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55512468|access-date=10 January 2021|website=BBC}}</ref> Ashcroft would score his first and second league goals for them in an away win against [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=19 March 2021|title=Alloa Athletic v Dundee|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56369117|access-date=19 March 2021|website=BBC}}</ref> At the end of the league season, Ashcroft was awarded the Andrew De Vries Player of the Year award, as well as the Player's Player of the Year award.<ref>{{Cite web|date=9 May 2021|title=Lee wins De Vries and Player's Player awards|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/lee-wins-de-vries-and-players-player-awards/|access-date=9 May 2021|website=dundeefc.co.uk}}</ref> Ashcroft was also named to [[PFA Scotland]]'s Championship Team of the Year for 2020–21.<ref>{{Cite web|title=PFA Scotland Championship Team of the Year 2021|url=https://pfascotland.co.uk/pfa-scotland-championship-team-of-the-year-2021/|access-date=17 May 2021|website=pfascotland.co.uk|date=17 May 2021 }}</ref> Along with his impressive defensive performances, Ashcroft would amass 7 goals in all competitions, including one in the 2nd leg of the [[2020–21 Scottish Premiership#Premiership play-offs|Premiership play-offs]] final, and was a major factor in helping Dundee gain promotion to the [[Scottish Premiership]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|date=24 May 2021|title=Dundee promoted as Kilmarnock drop down for first time in 28 years|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/live/football/57089947|access-date=24 May 2021|website=BBC}}</ref> Ashcroft would also be named to the [[SPFL]]'s Championship Team of the Season.<ref>{{Cite web|date=9 June 2021|title=Championship Team of the Season 2020/21|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/championship-team-of-the-season-202021|access-date=9 June 2021|website=SPFL.co.uk}}</ref>

During a game against [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] in December 2021, Ashcroft would damage a tendon in his hamstring which would require surgery and keep him out for approximately 3–4 months.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Cran|first=George|title=Dundee dealt huge blow as defender Lee Ashcroft set for months on the sidelines|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/2794227/dundeefc-lee-ashcroft-months-sidelines/|access-date=2021-12-06|website=The Courier|date=4 December 2021 |language=en-GB}}</ref> While out with injury, Ashcroft would sign a contract extension with Dundee, keeping him at the club until the summer of 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-07|title=Lee extends deal|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/lee-extends-deal/|access-date=2022-01-07|website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website|language=en-US}}</ref> Ashcroft made his return from injury off the bench in a league game against [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in March 2022.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Ten-man Hibs earn point at Dens Park |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60488489 |access-date=2022-03-02}}</ref> After just two starts however, Ashcroft would experience a recurrence of the hamstring injury against [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] that would end his season and required surgery again.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cran |first=George |title=Dundee dealt huge blow as Lee Ashcroft ruled out for season - but there's positive news on Charlie Adam |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/3117029/dundee-huge-blow-lee-ashcroft-out-season-charlie-adam/ |access-date=2022-03-20 |website=The Courier |date=18 March 2022 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Ashcroft would make his return for Dundee off the bench in an away league win over [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] in August.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Raith Rovers v Dundee |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62358465 |access-date=2022-08-06}}</ref> He would score in his first start of the season in a [[Scottish League Cup]] win over [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Dundee ease past Falkirk into League Cup last eight |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62712675 |access-date=2022-08-30}}</ref> Ashcroft would start every game after in a very successful season which would culminate in scoring a goal in the win over [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] which clinched the [[Scottish Championship]] title for the ''Dark Blues''.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |title=Dundee back in Premiership after eight-goal epic |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65420805 |access-date=2023-05-05}}</ref> Ashcroft would be named to [[PFA Scotland]]'s [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year#Championship 9|Scottish Championship Team of the Year]] at the end of the season, as well as being named in the [[SPFL]]'s Championship Team of the Season.<ref name=":3">{{cite tweet|number=1655898923506999298|user=PFAScotland|title=Your PFA Scotland Championship Team of the Year - as voted for by the players|date=9 May 2023|access-date=9 May 2023}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=cinch Championship Team of the Season 22/23 {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/cinch-championship-team-of-the-season-2223 |access-date=2023-06-14 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref>

On 2 June 2023, Dundee announced that Ashcroft had signed a new two-year contract, keeping him there until the summer of 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-02 |title=New contract for Ashcroft |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/new-contract-for-ashcroft/ |access-date=2023-06-02 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> After struggling for game time under new manager [[Tony Docherty]], Ashcroft returned to the first team in January 2024 following injuries in defence, and would score his first goal of the season on 30 January to help Dundee earn a point away to [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref>{{Cite news |title='No panic' from Robson as Aberdeen and Dundee draw |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67073681 |access-date=2024-01-31 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Despite breaking back into the Dundee squad, a combination of returning squad depth and interest from clubs promising regular playing time made Ashcroft available for a loan, and on 21 February he joined Championship club [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lee Ashcroft Signs {{!}} Raith Rovers FC |url=https://www.raithrovers.net/67489/lee-ashcroft-signs.htm |access-date=2024-02-21 |website=www.raithrovers.net|date=21 February 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-21 |title=Dundee: Lee Ashcroft joins Raith Rovers on loan |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c3g00dle922o |access-date=2024-02-21 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Ashcroft made his debut on 24 February away to [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]], but had to come off in the first half after suffering a hamstring injury.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Rovers keep pace at top with victory at Ayr |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68324495 |access-date=2024-02-24 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Rovers manager [[Ian Murray (footballer)|Ian Murray]] confirmed in March that Ashcroft would be out for the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Collin |first=Iain |date=2024-03-05 |title=Raith Rovers boss Ian Murray gives injury update on Keith Watson and confirms Lee Ashcroft blow |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/4913672/raith-rovers-ian-murray-keith-watson-ashcroft/ |access-date=2024-03-06 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 24 June 2024, Dundee announced that Ashcroft had left the club as his contract had been terminated by mutual consent.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-06-24 |title=Ashcroft departs |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/ashcroft-departs/ |access-date=2024-06-24 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Partick Thistle ===
The day following his departure from Dundee, Ashcroft joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jags add Lee Ashcroft to defensive ranks |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/jags-add-lee-ashcroft-to-defensive-ranks/ |access-date=2024-06-25 |website=Partick Thistle FC |language=en}}</ref> Ashcroft made his debut on 13 July 2024 as a substitute in a 3–2 win over [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage, and assisted the winning goal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Partick Thistle vs Montrose: League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4ng8dz9yv2t |access-date=2024-07-13 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Ashcroft was named club captain of Thistle in June 2025.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Lee Ashcroft named Partick Thistle club captain  {{!}}  Partick Thistle FC | url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/lee-ashcroft-named-partick-thistle-club-captain/ | access-date=2026-10-08 | website=ptfc.co.uk}}</ref> On 15 July 2025, Ashcroft scored his first goal for Thistle in a 2–0 home win over Stranraer in the Scottish League Cup group stages.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Partick 2-0 Stranraer (Jul 15, 2025) Final Score - ESPN | url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/736197 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250722213436/https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/736197 | access-date=2026-10-08 | archive-date=2025-07-22}}</ref>

'''Robbie Muirhead''' (born 8 March 1996) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]], who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for {{Scottish football updater|Livingst}} club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].

Muirhead began his career with [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] before joining [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] in February 2015. After a loan spell with [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] between September 2015 to January 2016, Muirhead was released by Dundee United in April 2016, before signing for [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]]. In 2017, he moved to [[Milton Keynes Dons F.C.|Milton Keynes Dons]], then spent a season at [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].

He has represented Scotland at all levels up to [[Scotland national under-19 football team|U19]] level.

==Early life==
Born in [[Irvine, North Ayrshire|Irvine]], Scotland, Muirhead was known for playing football and golf locally, and was mentioned on several occasions in his local newspaper.
Muirhead is also the first and still the only boy to win both the West of Scotland Cup and Scottish Cup when representing Annanhill Primary School during year 6 and year 7 when he was Captain of the schools team.<ref>{{cite news|title=East Ayrshire pupils retain Scottish Cup|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/east-ayrshire-pupils-retain-scottish-2451360|work=Daily Record|date=3 July 2008|accessdate=8 March 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Schools are just champion|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/news/local-news/schools-are-just-champion-2453876|work=Daily Record|date=26 June 2008|accessdate=8 March 2015}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Kilmarnock===
Muirhead joined [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] academy before joining the first team.<ref>{{cite news|title=Kilmarnock FC: Killie kid Robbie Muirhead a Scotland scoring sensation.|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/kilmarnock-fc-killie-kid-robbie-2407405|work=Daily Record|date=21 September 2012|accessdate=8 March 2015}}</ref> He made his professional league debut in the last game of the season, coming on as a substitute in the second half for [[Cillian Sheridan]], in a 3–1 loss against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]], which was [[Kenny Shiels]]'s last game as Kilmarnock Manager.<ref>{{cite news|title=Kilmarnock 1 – 3 St Mirren|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22491346|publisher=BBC Sport|date=18 May 2013|access-date=8 March 2015}}</ref>

Muirhead's playing time in the 2013–14 season soon increased with 21 appearances and scoring twice against [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Partick Thistle 1–1 Kilmarnock|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25693256|publisher=BBC Sport|date=18 January 2014|access-date=8 March 2015}}</ref> and [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Kilmarnock 1–2 St Johnstone|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26796708|publisher=BBC Sport|date=5 March 2015|access-date=8 March 2015}}</ref> His first team chance attracted interests from English clubs.<ref>{{cite news|title=Transfer Talk, 29 January: Moves at Hearts, Lee Wallace on the way out at Rangers while Celtic make a second bid for Leigh Griffiths|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-transfer-news/transfer-talk-january-29-moves-3088322|work=Daily Record|date=29 January 2014|accessdate=8 March 2015}}</ref>

In the first half of the 2014–15 season, Muirhead added two more goals to his career tally, against [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]]<ref>{{cite news|title=Kilmarnock 2 Motherwell 0: Josh Magennis insists Killie are on the verge of a goals fest|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-match-reports/kilmarnock-2-motherwell-0-josh-4098293|accessdate=8 March 2015}}</ref> and St Mirren.<ref>{{cite news|title=Kilmarnock 2–1 St Mirren|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29090489|publisher=BBC Sport|date=13 September 2014|access-date=8 March 2015}}</ref> His two goals to his tally career led [[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]] naming Muirhead as the next successor to [[Kris Boyd]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Record FC Kilmarnock: Killie have found a successor to goal king Kris Boyd in young star Robbie Muirhead|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/opinion/sport/record-fc-kilmarnock-killie-found-4106854|work=Daily Record|date=25 August 2014|accessdate=8 March 2015}}</ref>

===Dundee United===
Muirhead left Kilmarnock to sign for [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] on the transfer deadline day for a fee of £150,000 plus add-ons, as well as signing a three-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dufc.co/news/muirhead-becomes-tangerine/ |title=MUIRHEAD BECOMES A TANGERINE |publisher=Dundee United F.C. |accessdate=8 March 2015 |date=3 February 2015 |url-status=usurped |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150308192552/http://dufc.co/news/muirhead-becomes-tangerine/ |archivedate=8 March 2015 }}</ref> The sale of Muirhead caused the Kilmarnock manager [[Allan Johnston]] to resign in protest.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31161073 |title=Allan Johnston: Kilmarnock manager relieved of duties |publisher=BBC Sport |date=6 February 2015 |access-date=6 February 2015}}</ref> [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] was also keen to sign Muirhead, having signed Dundee United's [[Stuart Armstrong]] and [[Gary Mackay-Steven]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Celtic make move for teenage Kilmarnock forward Robbie Muirhead |url=http://sport.stv.tv/football/clubs/celtic/308882-celtic-make-move-for-teenage-kilmarnock-forward-robbie-muirhead/ |work=STV Sport |publisher=STV |date=2 February 2015 |accessdate=8 March 2015}}</ref> Muirhead made his Dundee United debut, coming on as a substitute for [[Henri Anier]], in a 3–2 loss against Kilmarnock.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kilmarnock 3 – 2 Dundee United |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31367647|publisher=BBC Sport |date=14 February 2015|access-date=8 March 2015}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club in a 1–0 win against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] on 2 May.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dundee United 1 – 0 Aberdeen|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32447990|publisher=BBC Sport |date=2 May 2015|access-date=29 June 2015}}</ref> He followed this up three days later with another goal, in a 2–1 defeat against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Inverness Caledonian Thistle 2 – 1 Dundee United|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31776402|publisher=BBC Sport |date=5 May 2015|access-date=29 June 2015}}</ref>

On 1 September 2015, Muirhead was loaned to fellow [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on an initial three-month deal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34114755 |title=Robbie Muirhead: Partick Thistle sign Dundee United forward on loan |publisher=BBC Sport |date=1 September 2015 |access-date=1 September 2015}}</ref> Muirhead scored his first and second goal, including a 30-yard strike, for Thistle in a 5–2 win on 28 November against his former club Kilmarnock.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34887441 |first=Jonathan |last=Sutherland |publisher=BBC Sport |date=28 November 2015 |accessdate=30 April 2016 |title=Kilmarnock 2–5 Partick Thistle}}</ref> He returned to Dundee United on 4 January 2016 following the expiry of his loan period.<ref>{{cite web |title=Robbie Muirhead back at Dundee Utd after Partick Thistle loan| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35225352 |access-date=4 January 2016|publisher=BBC Sport |date=4 January 2016}}</ref> Muirhead did not play for United after his return, and was released from his contract in April 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36172361 |title=Robbie Muirhead: Striker parts company with Dundee United |publisher=BBC Sport |date=29 April 2016 |accessdate=30 April 2016}}</ref>

===Heart of Midlothian===
Muirhead signed a one-year deal with [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] in June 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36515471 |title=Robbie Muirhead: Hearts sign forward on one-year deal |first=Brian |last=McLaughlin |publisher=BBC Sport |date=13 June 2016 |accessdate=13 June 2016}}</ref> On 30 November 2016, Muirhead scored twice in a 2–0 win over [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/38073798 |title=Heart of Midlothian 2–0 Rangers |publisher=BBC Sport |date=30 November 2016 |accessdate=19 January 2017 }}</ref>

===Milton Keynes Dons===
On 19 January 2017, Muirhead signed a two-and-a-half-year deal to join English [[Football League One|League One]] side [[Milton Keynes Dons F.C.|Milton Keynes Dons]] for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.mkdons.com/news/article/2016-17/muirhead-makes-mk1-move-mk-dons-robbie-muirhead-heart-of-midlothian-efl-transfer-mk-dons-transfer-scottish-premiership-3528221.aspx |title=Muirhead makes MK1 move |publisher=Milton Keynes Dons Official Site |date=19 January 2017 |accessdate=19 January 2017 }}</ref>

He made his debut coming on as a substitute in a 5–3 home league win over Northampton Town on 21 January 2017. On 1 April 2017, Muirhead scored his first goal for the club in a 3–2 home league win over [[Gillingham F.C.|Gillingham]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.mkdons.com/news/article/2016-17/report-mk-dons-3-2-gillingham-3652312.aspx |title=Report: MK Dons 3–2 Gillingham |publisher=Milton Keynes Dons Official Site |date=1 April 2017 |accessdate=1 April 2017 }}</ref> On 13 March 2018, Muirhead scored twice in a 3–2 home win against [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42756423 |title=Milton Keynes Dons 3-2 Rotherham United |publisher=BBC Sport |date=13 March 2018 |accessdate=13 March 2018 }}</ref>

===Dunfermline Athletic===
On 31 August 2018, Muirhead joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] for an undisclosed fee, signing a one-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=DAFC_sign_Robbie_Muirhead_&ID=10812 |title=DAFC sign Robbie Muirhead |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic |date=31 August 2018 |accessdate=31 August 2018 }}</ref> He left in May 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Player_Update_&ID=11225 |title=Player update |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=6 May 2019 |accessdate=6 May 2019}}</ref>

===Greenock Morton===
On 12 June 2019, Muirhead signed for [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] on a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Muirhead: 'Morton boss will get the best out of me'|url=https://www.greenocktelegraph.co.uk/sport/17697612.muirhead-morton-boss-will-get-the-best-out-of-me/|publisher=Greenock Telegraph|last=Thomas|first=Adam|date=12 June 2019|accessdate=21 July 2019}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club in a 0–5 victory against [[Annan Athletic F.C.|Annan Athletic]] in the Scottish League Cup group stages on 23 July 2019.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Annan Athletic v Greenock Morton |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/48998162 |access-date=2023-02-26}}</ref>

Muirhead would have a slow start to life at Morton, scoring very rarely for the club. He would be offered another contract by manager [[David Hopkin]] at the early end of the season brought on by the COVID-19 pandemic.

His second season in white and blue was also fairly quiet, scoring 4 goals for the season, 3 of these coming in both legs of the Championship play-off final against [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]], including a stunning 18-yard volley at Cappielow.<ref>{{Cite news |title=MacPherson hails Morton 'miracle' |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/57110435 |access-date=2023-02-26}}</ref> Muirhead was promptly offered another year-long contract following this.

Muirhead started slowly again in season 2021/2022; however, his form took a slight turn for the better under manager [[Dougie Imrie]], scoring 4 times in the second half of the season, including against [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]]<ref>{{Cite news |title=Motherwell beat Morton after extra time |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60005997 |access-date=2023-02-26}}</ref> and his former club Partick Thistle.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Thistle promotion bid dented by Morton |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60628569 |access-date=2023-02-26}}</ref> Muirhead would sign a two-year contract<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-05-30 |title=Robbie Muirhead Pens Contract Extension |url=https://www.gmfc.net/robbie-muirhead-pens-contract-extension/ |access-date=2023-02-23 |website=Greenock Morton FC |language=en-GB}}</ref> in the summer of 2022.

Muirhead would finally regain his form in the 2022/2023 season, scoring his first goal of the season against [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] in a 2–1 home defeat,<ref>{{Cite news |title=Championship leaders Ayr extend unbeaten start |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62697821 |access-date=2023-02-23}}</ref> however would go on to hit the 10 goal mark in a season for the first time in his career. Muirhead was also awarded Championship Player of the Month for September/October.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Muirhead nets Championship award {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/muirhead-nets-championship-award |access-date=2023-02-23 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref> He would go on to finish the season with a total of 13 goals, scoring on the last day of the season in a 2–1 away win over [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]], a goal which would relegate the Aberdeenshire side to league 1.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Cove relegated as Morton miss out on play-off spot |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65420806 |access-date=2023-05-06}}</ref>

The 23/24 season would further build upon Muirhead's form at Morton. The striker would score his first of the season in a pre-season "friendly" against Morton's rivals [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] at Cappielow in a 2–0 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sofascore |title=Greenock Morton vs St. Mirren live score, H2H and lineups {{!}} Sofascore |url=https://www.sofascore.com/greenock-morton-st-mirren/jXszX |access-date=2024-05-13 |website=www.sofascore.com |language=en}}</ref> Muirhead's first competitive goal of the season would come in the opening game of the Championship, scoring a Penalty to take the lead against Ayr United in what would become a 3–1 victory.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Morton battle back to beat Ayr |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66194523 |access-date=2024-05-13 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> In spite of what proved to be an up-and-down season for Morton, Muirhead was a consistent source of goals for the club, especially in the middle of the season, as he not only bagged his first career hattrick in a 4–1 cup win over [[Kelty Hearts F.C.|Kelty Hearts]] on 14 October 2023,<ref>{{Cite news |title=Greenock Morton v Kelty Hearts |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67112053 |access-date=2024-05-13 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> he also bagged his second "perfect" hattrick in a 3–0 home victory against Ayr United just 3 months later on 2 January 2024.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Muirhead hat-trick propels Morton past Ayr |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67821093 |access-date=2024-05-13 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Similar to the 22/23 season, not only did Morton finish 5th, but Muirhead was the club's top goalscorer again, scoring 17 goals in 45 games, bettering his tally from the previous season by 4 goals. This, however, would prove to be Muirhead's final season at Cappielow, as on 10 May 2024, Morton announced that Muirhead would be departing the club upon the expiry of his contract in summer 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-10 |title=Robbie Muirhead departs - Greenock Morton FC |url=https://gmfc.net/robbie-muirhead-departs/,%20https://gmfc.net/robbie-muirhead-departs/ |access-date=2024-05-13 |language=en-US}}</ref> In his time at Greenock Morton (2019-2024), Muirhead racked up a total of 167 appearances, scoring 44 goals.

===Livingston===
On 10 May 2024, [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston Football Club]] announced that Robbie Muirhead had signed a pre-contract agreement, and would join the club upon the expiry of his contract at Greenock Morton in summer 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Black |first=Dave |date=2024-05-10 |title=Robbie heads for the Lions! |url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/robbie-heads-for-the-lions/ |access-date=2024-05-13 |website=Livingston FC |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==International career==
Muirhead has previously represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-16 football team|U16]], [[Scotland national under-17 football team|U17]], [[Scotland national under-18 football team|U18]] and [[Scotland national under-19 football team|U19]] international levels.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=1921&playerID=127112&squadID=21 |title=Robbie Muirhead |publisher=scottishfa.co.uk |accessdate=19 January 2014 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150308175547/http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=1921&playerID=127112&squadID=21 |archivedate=8 March 2015 |url-status=unfit }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kilmarnockfc.co.uk/Article?id=1327 |title=Q&A Robbie Muirhead |publisher=Kilmarnock F.C. |accessdate=8 March 2015 |date=15 October 2014 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150308192843/http://www.kilmarnockfc.co.uk/Article?id=1327 |archivedate=8 March 2015 |url-status=unfit }}</ref> While playing for Scotland U19, Muirhead scored a goal that was nominated for a "goal of the season" award by [[UEFA]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33679153 |title=Scots teenager up against Messi, Ronaldo & Neymar for best goal |publisher=BBC Sport |date=27 July 2015 |access-date=27 July 2015}}</ref> On 13 March 2018, Muirhead was called up to the Scotland [[Scotland national under-21 football team|U21]] national team for the first time.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43388190 |title=Scotland U21s call on Chelsea's Harvey St Clair, Anthony Ralston returns |publisher=BBC Sport |date=13 March 2018 |accessdate=15 March 2018 }}</ref>
