'''Jérôme Prior''' (born 8 August 1995) is a French professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{Scottish football updater|Livingst}} club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref name="sw">{{Soccerway|259268|accessdate=28 June 2023}}</ref>

==Career==
===Girondins de Bordeaux===
In 2012, Prior made his debut for [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Girondins de Bordeaux]] II. He made his [[Ligue 1]] debut at 15 August 2015 in a 1–1 draw against [[AS Saint-Étienne]].<ref name="soccerway2">{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2015/08/15/france/ligue-1/association-sportive-de-saint-etienne-loire/fc-girondins-de-bordeaux/2045826/|title=Saint-Étienne vs. Bordeaux - 15 August 2015 - Soccerway|publisher=soccerway.com|accessdate=2015-08-15}}</ref>

===Miedź Legnica===
In February 2019, he signed for [[Miedź Legnica]] of the Polish [[Ekstraklasa]] on loan until the end of the [[2018–19 Ekstraklasa|2018–19 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.foot-national.com/foot-bordeaux-un-gardien-vers-la-pologne-115222.html|title=Bordeaux : Un gardien vers la Pologne|publisher=foot-national.com|language=fr|date=15 February 2019|accessdate=15 February 2019}}</ref>

===Valenciennes===
In July 2019, Prior joined [[Ligue 2]] club [[Valenciennes FC|Valenciennes]].<ref name="girondins">{{cite web|url=https://www.girondins.com/fr/jerome-prior-rejoint-valenciennes|title=Jérôme Prior rejoint Valenciennes|publisher=girondins.com|accessdate=2019-07-24|archive-date=26 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190626174245/https://www.girondins.com/fr/jerome-prior-rejoint-valenciennes|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 14 August 2021, he moved abroad and signed a one-year deal with Spanish [[Segunda División]] side [[FC Cartagena|Cartagena]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fccartagena.es/noticia/el-frances-jerome-prior-un-refuerzo-de-garantias-para-la-porteria-albinegra|title=El francés Jerome Prior, un refuerzo de garantías para la portería albinegra|trans-title=Frenchman Jerome Prior, a secure addition for the white-and-black goal|publisher=FC Cartagena|language=es|date=14 August 2021|accessdate=15 August 2021}}</ref>

===PAS Giannina===
On 29 June 2022, Prior signed a three-year contract with [[PAS Giannina F.C.|PAS Giannina]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sport24.gr/football/pas-giannina-metagrafes-ypegrapse-o-prior.9675665.html |title=ΠΑΣ Γιάννινα μεταγραφές: Υπέγραψε ο Πριόρ | publisher=www.sport24.gr |date=29 June 2022}}</ref>

===Livingston===
In May 2024, Prior signed a pre-contract with Scottish side [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on an initial one-year-deal, with an automatic one-year extension triggered by promotion.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c4nnp42jmd6o|title=Livingston sign goalkeeper Prior|date=23 May 2024|publisher=BBC}}</ref>

'''Scott Pittman''' (born 9 July 1992) is a Scottish [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as an [[attacking midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Livingst}} club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].

==Background==
He is a son of [[Steve Pittman]], who played for [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]] and [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] as a [[full back (association football)|full back]], and also represented the [[USMNT|United States]] at international level.<ref name=dad/>

==Career==
Pittman began his career at [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] and on 25 March 2011, he signed on loan for [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Scott Pittman joins club|url=http://www.alloaathletic.co.uk/BlogView.aspx?pageid=2&ItemID=511&mid=2|publisher=Alloa Athletic F.C.|date=25 March 2011|accessdate=6 June 2019}}</ref> He was first called up for a matchday squad on 26 March 2011, remaining an unused substitute for their goalless home draw with [[Peterhead F.C.|Peterhead]] in the [[Scottish Second Division]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Alloa Athletic 0–0 Peterhead|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/12867166|access-date=22 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=26 March 2011}}</ref> Three days later, he made his only appearance for the club, as a last-minute substitute for [[Jim Lister]] in a 3–2 defeat at [[Brechin City]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Brechin stay second|url=http://spfl.co.uk/league-one/fixture/3377275/|accessdate=22 August 2015|publisher=[[Scottish Professional Football League]]|date=29 March 2011}}</ref>

On 11 August 2011, having been released by Hamilton,<ref>{{cite web|title=Hamilton wield axe for the drop|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/13398942|publisher=BBC Sport|date=14 May 2011|accessdate=6 June 2019}}</ref> Pittman signed for [[Scottish Junior Football Association|junior]] club [[Broxburn Athletic F.C.|Broxburn Athletic]], managed by his father.<ref name=dad>{{cite news|title=Pittman joins Dad at Broxburn|url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/pittman-joins-dad-at-broxburn/|accessdate=22 August 2015|publisher=[[Scottish Professional Football League]]|date=11 August 2011}}</ref> He later continued his junior career with [[Bo'ness United F.C.|Bo'ness United]] joining the club in June 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=Livingston set to sign Scott Pittman from Bo'ness|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/lower-leagues/livingston-set-to-sign-scott-pittman-from-bo-ness-1-3677020/amp|publisher=Edinburgh Evening News|date=2 February 2015|accessdate=6 June 2019}}</ref>

On 3 February 2015, after three other [[Scottish Professional Football League]] teams had made offers, he joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Livingston: David Robertson leaves as Bo'ness striker arrives|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31116090|access-date=22 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=3 February 2015}}</ref> Four days after his acquisition, he made his debut in a 3–2 home defeat to [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], playing the final four minutes in place of [[Ibra Sekajja]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Livingston 2–3 Hearts|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31071717|access-date=22 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=7 February 2015}}</ref> On 5 April, Pittman played the full 90 minutes of the [[2015 Scottish Challenge Cup Final]] at [[McDiarmid Park]] in [[Perth, Scotland|Perth]], scoring the first goal of a 4–0 win over his former team Alloa.<ref name=challenge>{{cite news|last1=Lindsay|first1=Clive|title=Livingston 4–0 Alloa|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32088242|access-date=22 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=5 April 2015}}</ref> On 24 October 2015, he scored the first league goal of his career, equalising in a 4–1 win at [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Queen of the South 1–4 Livingston|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34558825|accessdate=13 April 2016|publisher=BBC Sport|date=24 October 2015}}</ref>

On 7 May 2018, in the first leg of the [[2017–18 Scottish Premiership#Premiership play-offs|Scottish Premiership play-off semi-final]], Pittman scored the winning goal as Livingston won 3–2 away to [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dundee United 2–3 Livingston|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43945294|publisher=BBC Sport|last=McLauchlin|first=Brian|date=7 May 2018|accessdate=6 June 2019}}</ref> He scored again in the first leg of the final, getting Livingston's second goal in a 2–1 win at home against [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Livingston 2–1 Partick Thistle|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44063769|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Dowden|first=Martin|date=17 May 2018|accessdate=6 June 2019}}</ref> He also played in the second leg as Livingston won 1–0 to complete a 3–1 aggregate victory to gain promotion to the [[Scottish Premiership]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Partick Thistle 0–1 Livingston|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44097532|publisher=BBC Sport|last=McLauchlin|first=Brian|date=20 May 2018|accessdate=6 June 2019}}</ref>

On 22 March 2019, Pittman signed a new contract, keeping him at Livingston until 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Livingston: Keaghan Jacobs and Scott Pittman sign new deals|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47675311|publisher=BBC Sport|date=22 March 2019|accessdate=6 June 2019}}</ref>

During his spell at Livingston, Pittman has broken several records. In April 2022 he became the club's record top-flight appearance holder with 124, surpassing [[Rubio (footballer, born 1976)|Oscar Rubio]]'s tally.<ref>{{cite web|title=Livingston 1-0 Hibernian: Pittman's goal sends Livi seventh | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61198578|publisher=BBC Sport|date=30 April 2022|accessdate=24 September 2024}}</ref> In August the same year he became the record appearance holder in the Livingston era, breaking [[Keaghan Jacobs]]' record.<ref>{{cite web|title=David Martindale 'proud' of Scott Pittman ahead of record Livingston appearance | url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/david-martindale-proud-of-scott-pittman-ahead-of-record-livingston-appearance-1660911751000|publisher=FourFourTwo|date=19 August 2022|accessdate=24 September 2024}}</ref>

In October 2022 Pittman signed a further contract extension, penning a three-year deal lasting until the end of the 2025/26 season and taking him into a [[testimonial match|testimonial]] year.<ref>{{cite web|title='Livingston legend': Praise for Scott Pittman as new contract takes midfielder into testimonial year | url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/livingston-legend-praise-for-scott-pittman-as-new-contract-takes-midfielder-into-testimonial-year-3892493|publisher=Eduinburgh News|date=25 October 2022|accessdate=24 September 2024}}</ref>

'''Alexander Kinloch Samuel''' (born 20 September 1995) is a Welsh professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].

Samuel began his career in the youth academy at [[Aberystwyth Town F.C.|Aberystwyth Town]], breaking into the first team during the [[2011–12 in Welsh football|2011–12 season]]. He joined [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]]'s academy in the summer of 2012 and spent time on [[Loan (sports)|loan]] at [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] and [[Newport County A.F.C.|Newport County]]. He signed for [[Stevenage F.C.|Stevenage]] ahead of the [[2017–18 Stevenage F.C. season|2017–18 season]], spending one year at the club before joining [[Wycombe Wanderers F.C.|Wycombe Wanderers]] of [[EFL League One|League One]] in August 2018. 

He spent three seasons at Wycombe, scoring 11 goals in 88 appearances and helping [[2020 EFL League One play-off Final|the club earn promotion]] to the [[EFL Championship|Championship]]. Samuel joined [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] of the [[Scottish Premiership]] on a free transfer in August 2021, but his time there was limited by injuries. He spent the second half of the [[2023–24 Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C. season|2023–24 season]] on loan at [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]], was released by Ross County in June 2025, and signed for Partick Thistle in August 2025. He has also represented [[Wales national football team|Wales]] at [[Wales national under-18 football team|under-18]] level.

==Club career==
===Aberystwyth Town===
Samuel started his career at [[Cymru Premier]] club [[Aberystwyth Town F.C.|Aberystwyth Town]], progressing through the club's academy.<ref name="Academy Honours – Alex Samuel">{{cite news| title = Academy Honours – Alex Samuel| url = https://www.atfc.org.uk/academyhonours.html| publisher = Aberystwyth Town F.C.| access-date = 27 October 2017| archive-date = 3 October 2017| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20171003183935/https://www.atfc.org.uk/academyhonours.html| url-status = bot: unknown}}</ref> While still in the academy, he briefly joined boyhood club [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]], but travelling difficulties led to a return to Aberystwyth.<ref name="Academy Honours – Alex Samuel"/> He trained with the Aberystwyth first team in the opening months of the [[2011–12 in Welsh football|2011–12 season]] while continuing to feature for the under-16 team.<ref name="Academy Honours – Alex Samuel"/> Samuel made his senior debut two weeks after his 16th birthday,<ref name="WPL career details for Alex Samuel">{{cite news| title = WPL career details for Alex Samuel| url = http://welsh-premier.com/player_detail.php?player_id=2261| publisher = Welsh Premier League| access-date = 27 October 2017| archive-date = 10 August 2016| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160810190312/http://welsh-premier.com/player_detail.php?player_id=2261| url-status = bot: unknown}}</ref> coming on as a 77th-minute [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] in a 2–0 away defeat to [[Llanelli Town A.F.C.|Llanelli Town]] on 8 October 2011.<ref name="Llanelli Town 2–0 Aberystwyth Town">{{cite news
| title = Llanelli Town 2–0 Aberystwyth Town| url = https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2011/10/08/wales/premier-league/llanelli-afc/aberystwyth-town-fc/1127108/| website = Soccerway | date = 8 October 2011| access-date = 27 October 2017}}</ref> In his third appearance, he came off the substitutes' bench to score a late equaliser in Aberystwyth's 1–1 [[2011–12 Welsh Cup|Welsh Cup]] draw with [[Llandudno F.C.|Llandudno]] in January 2012.<ref name="Aberystwyth Town 1–1 Llandudno">{{cite news| title = Aberystwyth Town 1–1 Llandudno| url = https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2012/01/28/wales/welsh-cup/aberystwyth-town-fc/llandudno-town-fc/1232078/| website = Soccerway| date = 28 January 2012| access-date = 27 October 2017}}</ref> He made nine first-team appearances that season in all competitions, scoring once.<ref name="Soccerway – Alex Samuel"/>

| access-date = 9 July 2021}}</ref> He made 27 appearances over the course of the season, scoring four goals.<ref name="Games played by Alex Samuel in 2019/2020"/> That total included three appearances and one goal in the [[2019–20 EFL League One#Play-offs|League One play-offs]].<ref name="Games played by Alex Samuel in 2019/2020"/> Samuel started [[2020 EFL League One play-off final|the final]] at [[Wembley Stadium]], playing 62 minutes as Wycombe defeated [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]] 2–1 to secure promotion on 13 July 2020.<ref name="Games played by Alex Samuel in 2019/2020"/><ref name="Oxford United 1–2 Wycombe Wanderers">{{cite news
| title = Oxford United 1–2 Wycombe Wanderers
| url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53316283
| website = BBC Sport
| date = 13 July 2020
| access-date = 9 July 2021
|first=Adam 
|last=Williams}}</ref> He made 23 appearances in the [[EFL Championship|Championship]] during the [[2020–21 Wycombe Wanderers F.C. season|following season]], scoring once, as Wycombe were relegated back to League One after finishing in 22nd place.<ref name="Games played by Alex Samuel in 2020/2021">{{soccerbase season|87884|2020|access-date=26 September 2020}}</ref><ref name="Championship – 2020–21 – League Table">{{cite news
| title = Championship – 2020–21 – League Table
| url = https://uk.soccerway.com/national/england/championship/20202021/regular-season/r59442/
| website = Soccerway
| access-date = 9 July 2021}}</ref>

===Ross County===
Samuel signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] on a two-year contract on 31 August 2021, joining on a free transfer following his departure from Wycombe by mutual consent.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/alex-samuel-is-a-staggie|title=Alex Samuel is a Staggie|publisher=Ross County F.C.|website=rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk|date=31 August 2021|accessdate=31 August 2021}}</ref> He debuted for Ross County in a 3–0 defeat to [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] on 11 September 2021.<ref name="Celtic 3–0 Ross County">{{cite news
|title= Celtic 3–0 Ross County
|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58444925
|website=BBC Sport
|date=11 September 2021
|access-date=24 July 2025
|first=Nick
|last=McPheat}}</ref> Later that season, he suffered an [[anterior cruciate ligament]] injury that sidelined him for a year.<ref name="Alex Samuel signs new two-year deal">{{cite news
|title= Alex Samuel signs new two-year deal
|url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/alex-samuel-signs-new-2-year-deal
|publisher=Ross County F.C.
|date=27 June 2023
|access-date=24 July 2025}}</ref> Samuel returned to the first team on 21 January 2023, appearing as a substitute in extra time during a [[Scottish FA Cup]] penalty shoot-out defeat to [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]].<ref name="Games played by Alex Samuel in 2022/2023">{{soccerbase season|87884|2022|accessdate=19 August 2022}}</ref><ref name="Hamilton Academical 0–0 Ross County (AET 5–3 on penalties)">{{cite news
|title= Hamilton Academical 0–0 Ross County (AET, 5–3 on penalties)
|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64272752
|website=BBC Sport
|date=21 January 2023
|access-date=24 July 2025
|first=Kenny
|last=Crawford}}</ref> He scored his first goal in a 2–0 victory against [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on 6 May 2023,<ref name="Ross County 2–0 Livingston">{{cite news
|title= Ross County 2–0 Livingston
|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65433523
|website=BBC Sport
|date=6 May 2023
|access-date=24 July 2025
|first=Martin
|last=Dowden}}</ref> and made 13 appearances during the second half of that season, helping the club retain its Premiership status with a comeback win over [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] in the [[2022–23 Scottish Premiership#Premiership play-offs|Premiership play-off final]].<ref name="Games played by Alex Samuel in 2022/2023"/><ref name="Ross County 3–1 Partick Thistle (agg 3–3; County win 5–4 on pens)">{{cite news
|title= Ross County 3–1 Partick Thistle (agg 3–3; County win 5–4 on pens)
|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65736747
|website=BBC Sport
|date=4 June 2023
|access-date=24 July 2025
|first = Martin
|last=Watt}}</ref> Samuel signed a new two-year contract on 27 June 2023, with the club highlighting his impact following his return from injury.<ref name="Alex Samuel signs new two-year deal"/>

====Loan to Inverness Caledonian Thistle====
Having made 14 appearances for Ross County during the first half of the [[2023–24 in Scottish football|2023–24 season]],<ref name="AS2324">{{soccerbase season|87884|2023|accessdate=4 April 2025}}</ref> Samuel joined [[Highland derby|Highland rivals]] [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] on 19 January 2024, on a loan agreement until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=19 January 2024 |title=Alex Samuel signs for ICTFC on loan |url=https://ictfc.com/alex-samuel-signs-for-ictfc-on-loan/ |access-date=19 January 2024 |website=www.ictfc.com |publisher=Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C. |language=en-GB}}</ref> He scored on his debut the following day in a 4–0 victory over [[Broomhill F.C. (Scotland)|Broomhill]], and followed this up with a nine-minute hat-trick, the first of his senior career, in a 3–2 win away to [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on 27 January 2024.<ref name="AS2324"/><ref name="Raith Rovers 2–3 Inverness CT: Nine-minute Alex Samuel hat-trick dents hosts' title hopes">{{cite news
|title= Raith Rovers 2–3 Inverness CT: Nine-minute Alex Samuel hat-trick dents hosts' title hopes
|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68039855
|website=BBC Sport
|date=27 January 2024
|access-date=24 July 2025}}</ref> Samuel finished the loan spell with six goals in 19 appearances, as Inverness were relegated to [[Scottish League One]] after a [[2023–24 Scottish Championship#Championship play-offs|play-off final defeat]] to Hamilton.<ref name="AS2324"/><ref name="Inverness CT 2–3 Hamilton Academical (Agg 3–5)">{{cite news
|title= Inverness CT 2–3 Hamilton Academical (Agg 3–5)
|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cq5nnjx5wrzt
|website=BBC Sport
|date=18 May 2024
|access-date=24 July 2025}}</ref>

Samuel returned to Ross County and featured regularly during the first half of the [[2024–25 Ross County F.C. season|2024–25 season]].<ref name="AS2425">{{soccerbase season|87884|2024|accessdate=4 April 2025}}</ref> He sustained a thigh injury in the club's 3–1 defeat to [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on 14 December 2024,<ref name="'It doesn't look good' – Samuel out for up to three months">{{cite news
|title= 'It doesn't look good' – Samuel out for up to three months
|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cn54eee723wo
|website=BBC Sport
|date=17 December 2024
|access-date=24 July 2025
|first=Tyrone
|last=Smith}}</ref> which sidelined him until March 2025.<ref name="AS2425"/> He made 29 appearances and scored twice during the season,<ref name="AS2425"/> as Ross County were relegated to the Scottish Championship via the [[2024–25 Scottish Premiership#Premiership play-offs|Premiership play-offs]].<ref name="Ross County 2–4 Livingston (Agg 3–5)">{{cite news
|title= Ross County 2–4 Livingston (Agg 3–5)
|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cpd41v9p65xt
|website=BBC Sport
|date=26 May 2025
|access-date=24 September 2025
| first = Andy
| last = Campbell}}</ref> Samuel left the club following the expiry of his contract in June 2025.<ref name="Squad update: Alex Samuel and Logan Ross">{{cite news
|title= Squad update: Alex Samuel and Logan Ross
|url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/squad-update-alex-samuel-and-logan-ross
|publisher=Ross County F.C.
|date=4 June 2025
|access-date=24 July 2025}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle===
Following his departure from Ross County, Samuel signed a one-year contract with Scottish Championship club Partick Thistle on 12 August 2025, with the club retaining the option to extend for a further year.<ref name="Alex Samuel becomes a Jag">{{cite news
|title= Alex Samuel becomes a Jag
|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/alex-samuel-becomes-a-jag/
|publisher=Partick Thistle F.C.
|date=12 August 2025
|access-date=13 August 2025}}</ref> He made his debut four days later, as a substitute in a 2–0 win over [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] in the Scottish League Cup.<ref name="Partick Thistle 2–0 Ayr United">{{cite news
|title= Partick Thistle 2–0 Ayr United
|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cg5005y5q7qt
|website=BBC Sport
|date=16 August 2025
|access-date=1 September 2025
| first = Jack
| last = Herrall}}</ref> Samuel scored his first goal for the club in a 2–1 home victory over [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] on 12 September 2025, coming on as a second-half substitute and scoring the decisive goal.<ref name="Partick Thistle 2–1 Airdrieonians">{{cite news
|title= Partick Thistle 2–1 Airdrieonians
|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cg7dgp3gvg8t#Report
|website=BBC Sport
|date=12 September 2025
|access-date=24 September 2025
| first = George
| last = O'Neill}}</ref>

In March 2026, Partick Thistle activated the option in Samuel’s contract to extend his deal by a further year.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Alex Samuel contract extension triggered  {{!}}  Partick Thistle FC | url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/alex-samuel-contract-extension-triggered/ | access-date=2026-10-06 | website=ptfc.co.uk}}</ref>

==International career==
Samuel represented Wales at [[Wales national under-18 football team|under-18]] level.<ref name="Academy Honours – Alex Samuel"/> He made his debut in a 2–1 victory over the [[Republic of Ireland national under-18 football team|Republic of Ireland]] in February 2012, scoring the winning goal.<ref name="Academy Honours – Alex Samuel"/>

==Style of play==
Samuel has been described by manager Gareth Ainsworth as an energetic, direct player, noted for his persistence and willingness to [[Glossary of association football terms#P|press]] opponents.<ref name="Alex Samuel – Forward"/> His strong work ethic has been highlighted,<ref name="Alex Samuel – Forward"/><ref name="Ex-Wycombe Wanderers striker Alex Samuel finds new club">{{cite news
|title= Ex-Wycombe Wanderers striker Alex Samuel finds new club
|url=https://www.bucksfreepress.co.uk/highwycombe/25391618.ex-wycombe-wanderers-striker-alex-samuel-finds-new-club/
|work=Bucks Free Press
|publisher=Newsquest Media Group Ltd
|date=15 August 2025
|access-date=4 October 2025
|first=James
|last=Richings}}</ref> with Samuel also identifying it as one of his key attributes, stating that he always commits fully and believes supporters value that aspect of his game.<ref name="Alex Samuel embracing fresh Ross County start following bittersweet Caley Thistle spell">{{cite news
|title= Alex Samuel embracing fresh Ross County start following bittersweet Caley Thistle spell
|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/inverness-caledonian-thistle/6559439/alex-samuel-embraces-fresh-start-ross-county/
|work=The Press & Journal
|publisher=Aberdeen Journals Ltd
|date=16 August 2024
|access-date=4 October 2025
|first=Andy
|last=Skinner}}</ref>

'''Liam Smith''' (born 10 April 1996) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[right-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|StJohnst}} club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]]. He has previously played for [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]], [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]], [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]], [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]], [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], [[Cheltenham Town F.C.|Cheltenham Town]], [[Grimsby Town F.C.|Grimsby Town]] and [[Bohemian F.C.|Bohemians]].

==Career==

Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] (Hearts).<ref name = "Methil"/> Smith signed a 2-year professional contract in July 2014, extending his stay with the club until at least 2016.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/13171947.Hearts_kids_sign_on_until_2016______/ | title=Hearts kids sign on until 2016 . . . | publisher=[[The Herald (Glasgow)|The Herald]] | work=heraldscotland.com | date=26 July 2014 | accessdate=26 October 2015}}</ref> Aged 18 he made his first team debut<ref>{{cite web | url=http://sport.stv.tv/football/clubs/livingston/289152-hearts-boss-hopes-fans-understand-decision-to-field-kids-in-livi-defeat/ | title=Hearts boss hopes fans understand decision to field kids in Livi defeat | publisher=[[Scottish Television|STV]] | work=sport.stv.tv | date=21 August 2014 | accessdate=26 October 2015 | manager's plans | publisher=The Courier | work=thecourier.co.uk/ | date=8 October 2014 | accessdate=26 October 2015}}</ref> He made his league debut on 30 August 2014, against [[East Stirlingshire F.C.|East Stirlingshire]] in a 3–1 win,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28908741 | title=East Fife bounced back from defeat by Albion Rovers with a comfortable win over East once.<ref name = "games"/>

On his return to Hearts Smith made his [[Scottish Premiership]] debut on 18 October, coming on as a 71st-minute substitute against [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] at [[Tannadice Park]], replacing [[Juwon Oshaniwa]] in a 1–0 win.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34498795 | title=Mixu Paatelainen's reign as Dundee United manager began with a hot-tempered defeat by Hearts, courtesy of Juanma's early penalty at Tannadice. | publisher=[[BBC Sport]] | work=bbc.co.uk/sport | date=18 October 2015 | access-date=26 October 2015}}</ref>

====Raith Rovers loan====
On 24 September 2016, it was announced that Smith had signed on loan at [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] for a month.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.raithrovers.net/26924/liam-smith-arrives-on-emergency-loan.htm | title=Liam Smith Arrives on Emergency Loan | publisher=[[Raith Rovers F.C.]] | work=raithrovers.net | date=24 September 2016 | accessdate=24 September 2016}}</ref> He was recalled  by Hearts on 29 October 2016.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://twitter.com/RaithRovers_FC/status/792473001799323649 | title=RRFC Official ✔ @RaithRovers_FC | publisher=[[Raith Rovers F.C.]] on [[Twitter]] | date=29 October 2016 | accessdate=29 October 2016}}</ref>

====St Mirren loan====
On 14 August 2017, Smith signed a season-long loan deal with [[Scottish Championship]] club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.stmirren.com/news/club/all-news/1065-liam-smith-joins-on-loan |title=Liam Smith joins on loan |publisher=St Mirren FC |date=14 August 2017 |accessdate=14 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170814175006/https://www.stmirren.com/news/club/all-news/1065-liam-smith-joins-on-loan |archive-date=14 August 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref> It proved to be a successful loan spell as Saints won the Scottish Championship, with Smith playing 34 games and scoring twice. Smith was also part of the [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year#Championship 5|PFA Scotland Championship Team of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Good night for the Buddies at PFA Scotland Player of the Year awards|url=https://www.stmirren.com/news/club/all-news/1856-good-night-for-the-buddies-at-pfa-scotland-player-of-the-year-awards|publisher=St Mirren F.C.|date=2 May 2018|accessdate=14 May 2019|archive-date=14 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190514164819/https://www.stmirren.com/news/club/all-news/1856-good-night-for-the-buddies-at-pfa-scotland-player-of-the-year-awards|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Ayr United===
Smith signed a one-year contract with [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] in August 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ayrunitedfc.co.uk/smith-is-latest-signing/ |title=Smith is latest signing |publisher=Ayr United FC |date=14 August 2018 |accessdate=14 August 2018 |archive-date=21 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210121085141/https://ayrunitedfc.co.uk/smith-is-latest-signing/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Dundee United===
On 16 April 2019, [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] confirmed that Smith had signed a pre-contract to join the club in the summer, agreeing a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ayr Utd full-back Liam Smith to join Dundee Utd on two-year deal|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47916894|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Crawford|first=Kenny|date=16 April 2019|accessdate=14 May 2019}}</ref> Following relegation to the [[Scottish Championship]] in the [[2022–23 Dundee United F.C. season|2022–23 season]], Smith was released by United at the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=SQUAD UPDATE {{!}} DEPARTING PLAYERS |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/7867/SQUAD-UPDATE--DEPARTING-PLAYERS.html#:~:text=Ryan%20Edwards,%20Peter%20Pawlett,%20Ian,Wigan%20Athletic%20and%20Huddersfield%20Town. |access-date=2023-06-27 |website=Dundee United Football Club |language=en}}</ref>

===Cheltenham Town===
On 20 July 2023, Smith signed for [[Cheltenham Town F.C.|Cheltenham Town]], following a successful trial with the club.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Liam Smith becomes fifth summer signing |url=https://www.ctfc.com/news/2023/july/liam-smith-becomes-fifth-summer-signing/ |access-date=2023-07-20 |website=www.ctfc.com |language=en-gb}}</ref>

====Grimsby Town loan====
On 1 February 2024, Smith joined [[EFL League Two|League Two]] club [[Grimsby Town F.C.|Grimsby Town]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gtfc.co.uk/smith-signs-for-town/|title=SMITH SIGNS FOR TOWN|website=gtfc.co.uk|date=1 February 2024|accessdate=1 February 2024}}</ref>

===Bohemians===
On 12 July 2024, he signed for [[League of Ireland Premier Division]] side [[Bohemian F.C.|Bohemians]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/soccer/soccer-news/bohemians-add-another-scottish-player-33231660|title=Bohemians snap up ex-Hearts and Dundee United defender|first=Mark|last=McCadden|date=12 July 2024|website=Irish Mirror}}</ref>

===St Johnstone===
On 27 August 2025, Smith signed for [[Scottish Championship]] side [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web | title=Liam Smith joins the Saints! | ST JOHNSTONE FC | url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/liam-smith-joins-the-saints/ }}</ref>

'''Connor McLennan''' (born 5 October 1999) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[winger (association football)|winger]] for {{Scottish football updater|Livingst}} side [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].

He has previously played for [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]], [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]], [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]], [[Salford City F.C.|Salford City]] and [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]].

==Club career==
McLennan was born and raised in [[Peterhead]], [[Aberdeenshire]], and attended [[Peterhead Academy]].<ref name=int16>{{cite web|url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2016/05/03/connor-mclennan-interview/|title=Connor McLennan interview|date=3 May 2016|accessdate=4 February 2019|publisher=Aberdeen F.C.}}</ref><ref name=firststart/> He joined [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]]'s youth system at the age of eight, and turned professional aged 16 in December 2015.<ref name=int16/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.afc.co.uk/news/7194.php|title=Connor McLennan signs deal|date=22 December 2015|accessdate=16 May 2016|publisher=Aberdeen F.C.|archive-date=22 December 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222231934/http://www.afc.co.uk/news/7194.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his debut as a substitute away to [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on 22 April 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=St Johnstone 3-0 Aberdeen: Dons need more physical players - McInnes|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36117844|publisher=BBC Sport|date=22 April 2016|accessdate=30 August 2017}}</ref>

On 16 December 2016, McLennan joined [[Scottish League One]] side [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]] on a one-month emergency loan deal, playing three times and scoring once.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eveningexpress.co.uk/fp/aberdeen-fc/aberdeen-brechin-connor-mclennan/ |title=Young Dons forward joins Brechin City on emergency loan deal |first=Sean |last=Douglass |work=Evening Express |publisher=DC Thomson & Co Ltd |date=16 December 2016 |accessdate=16 December 2016}}</ref> He returned to Brechin for a second loan spell on 30 August 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Connor McLennan Returns on Loan |url=http://www.brechincity.com/bcfc/servlet/BCFCFrontControllerServlet?action=News&page_id=1918&category=2|publisher=Brechin City F.C.|date=30 August 2017 |accessdate=30 August 2017}}</ref>

Having scored in the final of the [[2017–18 Scottish Youth Cup]]<ref name = "2018 hibs">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43915764 |title=Scottish Youth Cup final: Hibernian beat Aberdeen 3-1|author=Kenny Crawford|work=BBC Sport|date=26 April 2018|accessdate=4 February 2019}}</ref> and made further appearances in the first team,<ref name=firststart>{{cite web |url=https://www.buchanobserver.co.uk/sport/football/first-dons-start-and-goal-for-connor-1-4811690/amp|title=First Dons start and goal for Connor|work=[[Buchan Observer]]|accessdate=8 October 2018|date=4 February 2019}}</ref> including as a substitute in the [[2018 Scottish League Cup Final]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46337733 |title=Celtic 1–0 Aberdeen|publisher=BBC Sport |accessdate=2 December 2018|date=4 February 2019}}</ref> In December 2018, he signed a new contract with Aberdeen until 2021.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2018/12/07/dons-teenager-signs-on/|title=Dons teenager signs on|publisher=Aberdeen F.C.|date=7 December 2018|accessdate=10 December 2018}}</ref> In January 2021, he signed a new contract until 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=Connor signs two year contract extension |url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2021/01/28/connor-signs-two-year-contract-extension/|publisher=Aberdeen FC|access-date=28 January 2021}}</ref>

He moved on loan to [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on 1 September 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62757882|title=Bates and McLennan leave Aberdeen for new clubs|work=BBC Sport |date=September 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/4740412/aberdeen-winger-connor-mclennan-joins-st-johnstone-on-loan/|title=Aberdeen winger Connor McLennan joins St Johnstone on loan|first=Paul|last=Third |date=September 2022 }}</ref> He left Aberdeen in 2023 after fifteen years at the club.<ref>{{cite news|title=End of Season update|url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2023/06/13/end-of-season-2022-23-squad-update/|access-date=14 June 2023 |publisher=AFC|date=13 June 2023}}</ref>

In July 2023, he signed for English club [[Salford City F.C.|Salford City]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66302803|title=Salford sign winger McLennan and keeper Wright|work=BBC Sport |date=25 July 2023 }}</ref> He was released by the club at the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 May 2024 |title=Salford City: Mariappa heads exit list from League Two strugglers |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cd11j7868rxo |access-date=21 May 2024 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 11 October 2024, he signed for [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ayrunitedfc.co.uk/connor-mclennan-joins-the-honest-men|title=Connor McLennan Joins The Honest Men|work=Ayr United FC |via=www.ayrunitedfc.co.uk}}</ref>

On 9 June 2025, McLennan joined newly-promoted [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 June 2025 |title=Jamie Brandon departs Livingston as Connor McLennan joins |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/crlj7y6jpeeo |access-date=14 June 2025 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==International career==
McLennan represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-16 football team|under-16]], [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17]] and [[Scotland national under-20 football team|under-20]] levels,<ref>{{SFA Profile|id=187721}}</ref>  including at the [[2016 UEFA European Under-17 Championship]] in Azerbaijan.<ref name=int16/> He then played for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] team, and scored both goals in a 2–1 win against [[Croatia national under-21 football team|Croatia]] in September 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49655399 |title=Croatia U21 1-2 Scotland U21: Connor McLennan's late double secures victory |website=BBC Sport |date=10 September 2019 |accessdate=10 September 2019}}</ref>

'''Robbie Crawford''' (born 22 June 1994) is a Scottish [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder#Central midfielder|central midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|PartickT}} club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] He has previously played for [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]], [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]], [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] and is now in his second spell with [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].

==Career==

===Early career===
After making more than 200 appearances for [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]], on 15 June 2019 Crawford joined [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48649219|title=Robbie Crawford: Livingston sign midfielder from Ayr United|publisher=BBC Sport|date=15 June 2019|accessdate=17 June 2019}}</ref>

===Motherwell===
On 18 September 2020, Crawford signed on loan for [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] until January 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Motherwell: Robbie Crawford joins on loan from Livingston|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54212719|website=BBC Sport|date=18 September 2020|accessdate=18 September 2020}}</ref> He moved to Motherwell on a permanent basis on 1 February 2021.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55888515 |title=Robbie Crawford makes Motherwell move permanent after Livingston release |website=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=1 February 2021 |accessdate=1 February 2021}}</ref>

On 2 April 2021, Crawford signed a one-year contract extension with Motherwell.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2021/04/02/new-contract-for-robbie-crawford/|title=New contract for Robbie Crawford|publisher=Motherwell FC|date=2 April 2021|access-date=2 April 2021}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle (first spell)===
On 7 January 2022, Crawford signed a 6-month contract with [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=SIGNING NEWS: Robbie Crawford joins on a six-month contract|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/signing-news-robbie-crawford-joins-on-a-six-month-contract/|access-date=2022-01-07|website=Partick Thistle FC|language=en}}</ref> Crawford scored his first goal for Thistle in a 2–1 Scottish Premiership play off quarter final first leg defeat against Inverness.<ref>{{cite web | title=Partick Thistle 1-2 Inverness Caledonian Thistle: Highland side secure comeback win in play-off first leg | work=BBC Sport | date=3 May 2022 | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61311734 }}</ref>

===Greenock Morton===
Crawford signed for [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] in August 2022,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Robbie Crawford joins the Ton|url=https://www.gmfc.net/robbie-crawford-joins-the-ton/|date=18 August 2022|website=Greenock Morton FC|language=en}}</ref> scoring his first goal in a 2–1 away victory against [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]]<ref>{{Cite news |title=Morton only point off top after battling win at Cove |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63606504 |access-date=2023-02-26}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle return===
Crawford returned to Partick Thistle for a second spell, signing a two-year pre contract deal in May 2024.<ref>{{cite web | title=Robbie Crawford joining on a pre-contract | url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/robbie-crawford-joining-on-a-pre-contract/ }}</ref>

Crawford scored the first goal of his second spell at Thistle in a Scottish Cup tie away to Queen's Park.<ref>{{cite web | title=Queen's Park vs Partick Thistle: Scottish Cup stats & head-to-head | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cg4l7r7v5x5t }}</ref>

'''Euan Drennan Henderson''' (born 29 June 2000) is a Scottish [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].

==Career==
Henderson joined Hearts at under-15 level from [[Lothian Thistle Hutchison Vale F.C.|Hutchison Vale]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-academy-laying-local-foundations-for-the-future-1-4405916|title=Hearts academy laying local foundations for the future|date=29 March 2017|accessdate=15 July 2018|author=Barry Anderson|publisher=Edinburgh Evening News|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180715210533/https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-academy-laying-local-foundations-for-the-future-1-4405916|archive-date=15 July 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> and made his debut against [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in May 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/fixtures/585|title=Heart of Midlothian - Fixtures|website=Heartsfc.co.uk|accessdate=21 December 2017}}</ref>

He was loaned to [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]] for most of the 2018–19 season.

Henderson scored his first goal for the Hearts first team in a Scottish Cup match against [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrie]] on 18 January 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-5-0-airdrie-recap-jambos-thrash-diamonds-scottish-cup-1369140|title=Hearts 5-0 Airdrie RECAP: Jambos thrash Diamonds in Scottish Cup}}</ref>

He moved on loan to [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]] in September 2021.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/euan-henderson-leaves-hearts-on-loan-after-completing-league-one-switch-3370126 |title=Euan Henderson leaves Hearts on loan after completing League One switch |first=Matthew |last=Elder |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=3 September 2021 |accessdate=3 September 2021}}</ref> He was recalled in January 2022.

On 27 January 2023, Henderson joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cairns |first=Ian |date=2023-01-27 |title=Euan Henderson on loan from Hearts |url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/euan-henderson-on-loan-from-hearts/ |access-date=2023-01-27 |website=Queen's Park Football Club |language=en-US}}</ref> Queen's Park used Henderson in a Scottish Cup match against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness CT]] on 31 January, even though he had been signed by the club after the original scheduled date for the tie.<ref name = ineligible/> This was a breach of the competition rules,<ref name = ineligible>{{cite web |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/queens-park-face-scottish-cup-expulsion-over-ineligible-player |title=Queen's Park face Scottish Cup expulsion over 'ineligible player' |first=Andy |last=Coyle |website=STV News |date=1 February 2023 |accessdate=2 February 2023}}</ref> and Queen's Park were ejected from the cup after a disciplinary hearing.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/queens-park-kicked-out-of-scottish-cup-for-fielding-ineligible-player |title=Queen's Park kicked out of Scottish Cup for fielding ineligible player |first=Peter |last=Cassidy |website=STV News |date=3 February 2023 |accessdate=3 February 2023}}</ref>

Following his release from Hearts, Henderson signed for [[Scottish League One]] side [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] in June 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/henderson-makes-it-seven/ |title=Henderson makes it seven! |first=Gillian |last=Gunning |website=Hamilton Academical FC |date=21 June 2023 |accessdate=25 June 2023}}</ref>

After his contract expired at Hamilton in June 2025, he  joined Airdrieonians FC. In the first match of the season he scored twice against Ross County, to give Airdrie a draw after being 2-0 down.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Airdrieonians vs Ross County: Scottish Championship updates & match report, BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c1jnd1x8np1t |access-date=2025-08-03 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle===
In June 2026, Henderson joined fellow [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] signing a two year deal.<ref>https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/euan-henderson-signs-two-year-deal-at-firhill/</ref>

Henderson scored on his Thistle debut in a 6–0 home win over Brechin City in a [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage tie.<ref>https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cn0vv0zzk78t</ref>

In October 2026, Henderson scored a hat-trick in a 3–0 home win over Stenhousemuir which sent Thistle top of the Scottish Championship.<ref>https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cxq6n5724lvjt</ref>

'''Logan Chalmers''' (born 24 March 2000) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Winger (association football)|winger]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[St Johnstone F.C.|St. Johnstone]]. He has also previously played for [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] and [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], as well as having loan spells at [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]], [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]], twice with [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] and [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]].

==Early life==
Chalmers was born in [[Dundee]] on 24 March 2000 and joined the [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] Academy at the age of 10. He attended the [[Scottish Football Association]] Performance School at [[St John's Roman Catholic High School]] in Dundee.<ref name="DUFC">{{cite web|title=Logan Chalmers|url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/team/development-squad/logan-chalmers|accessdate=10 January 2018|publisher=Dundee United FC|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180111052918/https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/team/development-squad/logan-chalmers|archive-date=11 January 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Club career==

===Dundee United===
Chalmers signed his first professional contract with Dundee United in July 2016. His first involvement with the first team was for [[Seán Dillon]]'s testimonial match in March 2017.<ref name="DUFC" /> His competitive debut came in the [[Scottish League Cup]] in July 2017, when he came on as a substitute in a 4–1 home win over [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Duthie|first1=Tom|title=Dundee United 4 Cowdenbeath 1: United stroll to Betfred victory|url=https://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/fp/dundee-united-4-cowdenbeath-1-united-stroll-betfred-victory/|accessdate=10 January 2018|newspaper=Evening Telegraph|date=23 July 2017|location=Dundee}}</ref> He scored his first senior goal in October 2017, a late winner against [[Linfield F.C.|Linfield]] in a [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] tie at [[Tannadice Park]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Chalmers looks back on memorable last few months|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/chalmers-looks-back-on-memorable-last-few-months/|accessdate=10 January 2018|publisher=Scottish Football Association|date=19 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Challenge Cup: Linfield lose to last-gasp goal as Crusaders progress|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41540430|accessdate=10 January 2018|website=BBC Sport|date=7 October 2017}}</ref>

====Loan spells====
Chalmers was loaned to [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] in January 2020.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51071557 |title=Dundee United sign Dillon Powers from Orlando City and Kieran Freeman from Southampton |website=BBC Sport |date=10 January 2020 |accessdate=11 January 2020}}</ref>

On 21 January 2022, Chalmers joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] on loan for the remainder of the 2021–22 season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://ictfc.com/logan-chalmers-signs-for-ictfc-on-loan |title=Logan Chalmers signs for ICTFC on loan |publisher=Inverness Caledonian Thistle FC |date=21 January 2022 |accessdate=21 January 2022}}</ref>

He was then loaned to [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] in September 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/7517/LOGAN-CHALMERS-JOINS-AYR-UNITED-ON-LOAN.html |title=LOGAN CHALMERS JOINS AYR UNITED ON LOAN |publisher=Dundee United FC |website=dundeeunitedfc.co.uk |date=30 September 2022 |accessdate=1 October 2022}}</ref> After a successful loan spell, Chalmers was recalled on 14 January 2023 amid speculation of a move to England.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Temple |first=Alan |title=Logan Chalmers recalled by Dundee United amid talks over England switch |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/4057144/logan-chalmers-dundee-united-england-switch/ |access-date=2023-01-14 |website=The Courier |date=14 January 2023 |language=en-GB}}</ref> Two days later, he moved on loan to [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64297659 |title=Logan Chalmers: Tranmere Rovers sign Dundee United winger on loan until end of season |website=BBC Sport |date=16 January 2023 |accessdate=16 January 2023}}</ref>

On 19 August 2023, Chalmers returned on a season-long loan to [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Stuart |date=2023-08-19 |title=Logan Chalmers: 'I'm back and can't wait to get going' |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/ayrshire/logan-chalmers-back-ayr-united-30740484 |access-date=2023-08-20 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle===
Chalmers signed a two-year deal with Scottish Championship side [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] in June 2024.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/logan-chalmers-joining-on-a-pre-contract/ | title=Logan Chalmers joining on a pre-contract }}</ref> Chalmers scored his first Thistle goal, scoring the winner in a 1–0 away win at Hampden against [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] in the Scottish Championship.<ref>{{cite web | title=Queen's Park vs Partick Thistle: Scottish Championship | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/crl8ll839jet }}</ref>

The winger played a key part in Partick Thistle's league campaigns across his two seasons at the club, including 21 goals and assists in all competitions in the [[2025–26 Partick Thistle F.C. season|2025–26 season]]. Chalmers departed [[Firhill Stadium|Firhill]] at the conclusion of his contract, despite being offered a new deal to stay with the club.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Logan Chalmers departs |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/logan-chalmers-departs/ |access-date=2026-06-27 |website=Partick Thistle FC |language=en}}</ref>

=== St. Johnstone ===
Logan Chalmers signed a two-year deal with [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[St Johnstone F.C.|St. Johnstone]] in June 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-21 |title=St Johnstone: Logan Chalmers leaves Partick Thistle after 'step up' |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cjegy2p3l12o |access-date=2026-06-27 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==International career==
Chalmers represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17]] level once, playing against the [[Czech Republic national under-17 football team|Czech Republic]] in August 2016.<ref name = SFA>{{SFA Profile|id=198113}}</ref> He was then capped by the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] team in October 2020.<ref name = SFA/>

'''Shane Blaney''' (born 20 January 1999) is an Irish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|Livingst}} club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].

==Early and personal life==
Blaney was born in [[Letterkenny]].<ref name = "SW"/>

==Career==
===Finn Harps===
Blaney began his career with [[Finn Harps F.C.|Finn Harps]], captaining their under-17 team and also playing for their under-19 team.<ref name = "contract">{{cite web|url=http://www.finnharps.com/fhfc/?p=5501|title=Coll and Blaney re-sign for Harps|date=6 December 2017|accessdate=5 November 2018|publisher=Finn Harps F.C.}}</ref> He made his senior debut in the 2017 season, making 3 League of Ireland appearances.<ref name = "SW">{{soccerway|shane-blaney/500139|accessdate=8 April 2019}}</ref> He signed a new contract for the 2018 season in December 2017.<ref name = "contract"/>

===Doncaster Rovers===
He turned professional in January 2018 after signing a two-and-a-half-year contract with English club [[Doncaster Rovers F.C.|Doncaster Rovers]] in January 2018.<ref name = "DN">{{cite web|url=https://donegalnews.com/2018/01/donegal-teenager-joins-professional-ranks/|title=Donegal teenager joins the professional ranks|date=15 January 2018|accessdate=5 November 2018|author=Harry Walsh|publisher=Donegal News}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42704328|title=Shane Blaney: Doncaster Rovers sign teenage Finn Harps defender|date=16 January 2018|accessdate=16 January 2018|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.doncasterroversfc.co.uk/news/2018/january/blaney-ambitious-after-rovers-move/|title=Blaney ambitious after Rovers move|date=16 January 2018|accessdate=5 November 2018|publisher=Doncaster Rovers F.C.}}</ref> He moved on loan to [[Tamworth F.C.|Tamworth]] in July 2018 for an intended six months.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.doncasterroversfc.co.uk/news/2018/july/blaney-makes-loan-move-to-tamworth/|title=Blaney makes loan move to Tamworth|date=24 July 2018|accessdate=26 July 2018|publisher=BBC ===Sligo Rovers===
He signed for [[Sligo Rovers F.C.|Sligo Rovers]] for the 2021 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2020/1228/1186749-sligo-rovers-sign-ex-doncaster-defender-shane-blaney/|title=Sligo Rovers sign ex-Doncaster defender Shane Blaney|date=28 December 2020|via=www.rte.ie}}</ref>

===Motherwell===
In December 2022 it was announced that he would sign for Scottish club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] in January 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/motherwell-announce-signing-of-defender-shane-blaney-from-sligo-rovers|title=Motherwell announce signing of defender Shane Blaney from Sligo Rovers|first=Andy|last=Coyle|date=20 December 2022|website=STV News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/sligo/sport/soccer/former-sligo-rovers-defender-shane-blaney-signs-for-motherwell/42232153.html|title=Former Sligo Rovers defender Shane Blaney signs for Motherwell|date=20 December 2022|website=Irish Independent}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/this-is-a-really-exciting-move-for-me-shane-blaney-cant-wait-to-join-motherwell-from-sligo-rovers/42232497.html|title='This is a really exciting move for me' – Shane Blaney can't wait to join Motherwell from Sligo Rovers|date=20 December 2022|website=Irish Independent}}</ref>

===Livingston===
On 13 June 2025, Blaney joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 June 2025 |title=Livingston: Shane Blaney makes switch from Motherwell |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c15nezk80k9o |access-date=14 June 2025 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 18 October 2025, Blaney suffered a hamstring injury that would keep him out of action for at least a three-month spell.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c8dr5yzd9z3o|title=Martindale: We've got to be 'careful' after Blaney's injury|date=6 November 2025|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 19 January 2026, Blaney returned to his former club [[Sligo Rovers F.C.|Sligo Rovers]] on loan until 30 June 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sligorovers.com/defender-shane-blaney-returns-to-the-showgrounds-on-loan/|title=Defender Shane Blaney returns to the Showgrounds on loan – Sligo Rovers|date=19 January 2026}}</ref>

'''Cammy Logan''' (born 28 January 2002) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]]. Logan has previously played for [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] and [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]], as well as loan spells with [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]], [[Edinburgh City F.C.|Edinburgh City]], [[Kelty Hearts F.C.|Kelty Hearts]] and [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]].

==Club career==

===Heart of Midlothian===
Logan debuted for [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] on 13 May 2018, in a 1–0 league defeat away at [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref name = "2017-18"/> He was one of four Hearts youth players to make their debuts in that match, alongside [[Chris Hamilton (footballer, born 2001)|Chris Hamilton]], [[Leeroy Makovora]] and [[Connor Smith (footballer, born 2002)|Connor Smith]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/6684|title=CRAIG'S PRIDE AT YOUNG DEBUTANTS|date=13 May 2018|accessdate=14 May 2018|publisher=Heart of Midlothian F.C.|archive-date=15 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180515043825/http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/6684|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-reaction-teenagers-help-craig-levein-in-face-of-adversity-1-4738887|title=Hearts reaction: Teenagers help Craig Levein in face of adversity|date=14 May 2018|accessdate=16 May 2018|author=Anthony Brown|publisher=The Scotsman}}</ref>

Logan was loaned to [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]] in January 2021.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/cove-rangers/2795200/cove-rangers-sign-hearts-duo-cammy-logan-and-connor-smith-on-loan-deals/ |title=Cove Rangers sign Hearts duo Cammy Logan and Connor Smith on loan deals |first=Jamie |last=Durent |newspaper=Press and Journal |date=7 January 2021 |accessdate=17 January 2021}}</ref>

On 3 January 2022, Logan joined [[Scottish League Two]] side [[Edinburgh City F.C.|Edinburgh City]] on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/article/logan-loan-move |title=Logan loan move |publisher=Heart of Midlothian FC |date=3 January 2022 |accessdate=3 January 2022}}</ref> He was a key part of helping the club gaining promotion to the [[Scottish League One]] via the play-offs.<ref name=":0" />

Logan was loaned to [[Scottish League One]] club [[Kelty Hearts F.C.|Kelty Hearts]] in August 2022.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dunfermlinepress.com/news/20603053.kelty-hearts-john-potter-signs-hearts-defender-cammy-logan/ |first=Ross |last=Hart |title=Kelty Hearts: John Potter signs Hearts defender Cammy Logan |newspaper=Dunfermline Press |date=5 August 2022 |accessdate=7 August 2022}}</ref> He returned to his parent club in January 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Phil |date=12 January 2023 |title=Hearts duo Scott McGill and Cammy Logan return from loan spell at Kelty Hearts |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-duo-scott-mcgill-and-cammy-logan-return-from-loan-spell-at-kelty-hearts-3984150 |access-date=13 January 2023 |website=edinburghnews.scotsman.com}}</ref>

Logan was loaned to Scottish League One club [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] in February 2023.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://qosfc.com/news-6005 | title=QosFC: Welcome - Cammy Logan }}</ref>

===Queen of the South===
Following his loan spell, on 26 June 2023, Logan signed a one-year contract with [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.qosfc.com/news-6114|title=QosFC: Welcome Back - Cammy Logan|website=www.qosfc.com}}</ref>

===Forfar Athletic===
In October 2024, Logan joined [[Scottish League Two]] side [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]] on a contract until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://forfarathletic.co.uk/item/6104-welcome-to-the-loons-cammy-logan|title=Welcome to the Loons - Cammy Logan|website=forfarathletic.co.uk|date=5 October 2024|accessdate=18 October 2024}}</ref> Logan scored the first goal of his professional career, scoring the equaliser in a 1-1 draw with Elgin City.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cx2vejxexlkt|title=Forfar Athletic vs Elgin City: Scottish League Two stats & head-to-head|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle===
Following a successful trial period, Logan joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on a one year deal with the option for an additional year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/cammy-logan-arrives-at-the-wyre-stadium-at-firhill/|title=Cammy Logan arrives at the Wyre Stadium at Firhill|website=Partick Thistle FC}}</ref>

On 11 July 2025 Logan made his Partick Thistle debut, as well as scoring his first Thistle goal in a 4–1 away victory over his former club Edinburgh City in the [[Scottish League Cup]] group stages.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cx24yx2krgnt|title=Edinburgh City vs Partick Thistle: League Cup stats & head-to-head|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

In April 2026 Thistle activated the extension clause in Logan's contract, extending his deal until summer 2027.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/cammy-logan-contract-option-triggered/|title=Cammy Logan contract option triggered|website=Partick Thistle FC}}</ref>

==International career==
Logan has represented both [[Scotland national under-16 football team|Scotland U16]] and [[Scotland national under-17 football team|Scotland U17]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/players/?pid=282942|title=Profile|website=Scottish FA|accessdate=25 May 2019}}</ref>

'''Cameron MacPherson''' (born 29 December 1998) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays for [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] as a [[midfielder]].<ref name="Soccerway">{{cite news|title=Scotland - C. MacPherson|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/cameron-macpherson/490530/|access-date=28 May 2018|work=Soccerway|date=28 May 2018}}</ref>

==Career==
MacPherson started out in the youth system of [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]], prior to appearing for the first-team.<ref name="St Mirren F.C. 1">{{cite news|title=Cameron MacPherson signs contract extension|url=https://www.stmirren.com/news/club/all-news/648-cameron-macpherson-signs-contract-extension|access-date=28 May 2018|work=St Mirren F.C.|date=28 February 2017|archive-date=17 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181217110622/https://www.stmirren.com/news/club/all-news/648-cameron-macpherson-signs-contract-extension|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his career debut on 21 January 2017 during a [[Scottish Cup]] fixture with [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], while his [[Scottish Championship|Championship]] bow arrived ten months later against [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] on 21 October.<ref name="Soccerway"/><ref name="St Mirren F.C. 1"/> In total, MacPherson featured six times for St Mirren throughout [[2017–18 Scottish League One|2017–18]].<ref name="Soccerway"/> On 30 January 2018, [[Stranraer F.C.|Stranraer]] of [[Scottish League One|League One]] loaned MacPherson.<ref name="Soccerway"/><ref name="St Mirren F.C. 2">{{cite news|title=Cameron MacPherson joins Stranraer on loan|url=https://www.stmirren.com/news/club/all-news/1552-cameron-macpherson-joins-stranraer-on-loan|access-date=28 May 2018|work=St Mirren F.C.|date=31 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180201193008/https://www.stmirren.com/news/club/all-news/1552-cameron-macpherson-joins-stranraer-on-loan|archive-date=1 February 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> One goal, versus [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] on 20 February, in nine matches followed as the club finished 5th.<ref name="Soccerway"/><ref name="Stranraer F.C.">{{cite news|title=Cameron MacPherson|url=http://www.stranraerfc.org/index.php/78-website-content/1074-cameron-macpherson|access-date=28 May 2018|work=Stranraer F.C.|date=28 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180528010801/http://www.stranraerfc.org/index.php/78-website-content/1074-cameron-macpherson|archive-date=28 May 2018}}</ref> He returned to his parent club in August 2018, before netting his first goal for them in December against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] at [[St Mirren Park]].<ref name="Soccerway"/>

In October 2019, MacPherson signed a two-year contract extension with St Mirren, keeping him at the club until 2022.<ref>{{cite news |title=CAMMY MACPHERSON EXTENDS DEAL TILL 2022 |url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/3193-cammy-macpherson-extends-deal-till-2022 |access-date=19 October 2019 |work=www.stmirren.com |date=19 October 2019}}</ref>

MacPherson moved on loan to [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] in August 2021.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58394873 |title=St Johnstone: Jason Kerr & Ali McCann depart as replacements arrive |website=www.bbc.co.uk/sport |publisher=BBC Sport |date=1 September 2021 |accessdate=11 September 2021}}</ref> After MacPherson signed a pre-contract agreement with St Johnstone in January 2022, his parent club St Mirren recalled him in order to negotiate terms for selling him to St Johnstone on a permanent deal.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cammy MacPherson: St Mirren explain why midfielder has been recalled from St Johnstone - despite signing pre-contract with Perth club|url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/cammy-macpherson-st-mirren-explain-why-midfielder-has-been-recalled-from-st-johnstone-despite-signing-pre-contract-with-perth-club-3538349|access-date=2022-01-23|website=www.scotsman.com|language=en}}</ref> MacPherson joined St Johnstone permanently for an undisclosed fee on 24 January.

He also went on loan to Tampa Bay Rowdies where he made 8 appearances before getting another injury to end his time in USA
<ref>{{Cite web|title=Saints sign Cammy MacPherson|url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/|access-date=2022-01-24|website=St Johnstone Football Club|language=en}}</ref>

MacPherson signed for [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] in July 2026.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/cammy-macpherson-arrives-in-west-lothian/|title=Cammy MacPherson arrives in West Lothian|date=25 July 2026|publisher=Livingston FC}}</ref>

'''Bruce Anderson''' (born 23 September 1998) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[forward (association football)|forward]] for {{Scottish football updater|Livingst}} club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].

==Career==
===Aberdeen===
Anderson began his footballing career with Dyce Boys Club when he was five,<ref name="New contract">{{cite web |title=Bruce Anderson: Striker signs new contract |url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2018/09/04/bruce-anderson-striker-signs-new-contract/ |publisher=Aberdeen FC |date=4 September 2018 |accessdate=11 November 2018 |archive-date=30 June 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190630173420/https://www.afc.co.uk/2018/09/04/bruce-anderson-striker-signs-new-contract/ |url-status=live }}</ref> before signing with [[Aberdeen F.C. Under-20s and Academy|Aberdeen youth teams]] when he was 13.<ref name="New contract"/> His first experience of senior football came when he moved out on loan to [[Scottish League Two]] side [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]] at the beginning of the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.northern-scot.co.uk/Sport/Football/Elgin-sign-Aberdeen-striker-on-loan-30082017.htm |title=Elgin sign Aberdeen striker on loan |work=Northern Scot |publisher=Scottish Provincial Press Ltd |date=30 August 2017 |accessdate=30 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170909212310/http://www.northern-scot.co.uk/Sport/Football/Elgin-sign-Aberdeen-striker-on-loan-30082017.htm |archive-date=9 September 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In five months with the club, Anderson scored six times in fourteen appearances, before returning to his parent club in January 2018.

He made his Aberdeen debut as a substitute against [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] on 5 August 2018, scoring an equalising goal in stoppage time to secure a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{cite web |last=Law |first=Danny |title=Bruce Anderson rescues a point for Dons against 10-man Rangers with injury-time equaliser |url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/1535006/bruce-anderson-rescues-a-point-for-dons-against-10-man-rangers-with-injury-time-leveller/ |accessdate=5 August 2018 |work=Press and Journal |date=5 August 2018 |archive-date=6 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180806024347/https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/1535006/bruce-anderson-rescues-a-point-for-dons-against-10-man-rangers-with-injury-time-leveller/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On 4 September 2018, Anderson signed a new deal until summer 2021.<ref name="New contract"/> He joined [[Scottish Championship]] side Dunfermline Athletic on loan in January 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Anderson_Arrives&ID=11069|title=Anderson arrives|publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC|date=31 January 2019|accessdate=31 January 2019|archive-date=1 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190201065712/https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Anderson_Arrives&ID=11069|url-status=live}}</ref>

Anderson was one of eight Aberdeen players who received a suspended three-match ban from the [[Scottish Football Association|Scottish FA]] after they breached [[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland|coronavirus-related restrictions]] due to visiting a bar in August 2020.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53951005|title=Celtic's Boli Bolingoli gets three-game ban; 'Aberdeen eight' receive three-match suspended ban|work=BBC Sport|date=28 August 2020|archive-date=2 November 2020|access-date=29 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201102125901/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53951005|url-status=live}}</ref> On 5 October 2020, Anderson signed for [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]], on a season-long loan.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bruce departs for the Honest Men|url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2020/10/05/bruce-departs-for-the-honest-men/|website=afc.co.uk|date=5 October 2020|access-date=5 October 2020|archive-date=24 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210824045158/https://www.afc.co.uk/2020/10/05/bruce-departs-for-the-honest-men/|url-status=live}}</ref> However he was recalled by Aberdeen in January. He made 12 appearances scoring two goals against [[Albion Rovers F.C.|Albion Rovers]] in the League Cup.<ref>{{cite web|title=Derek McInnes: Bruce Anderson has to channel frustration of Ayr United loan into making impact for Aberdeen|url=https://www.eveningexpress.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/donsnews/derek-mcinnes-bruce-anderson-has-to-channel-frustration-of-ayr-united-loan-into-making-impact-for-aberdeen/|website=eveningexpress.co.uk|last=Wallace|first=Sean|date=15 January 2021|accessdate=16 January 2021|archive-date=15 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210115104432/https://www.eveningexpress.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/donsnews/derek-mcinnes-bruce-anderson-has-to-channel-frustration-of-ayr-united-loan-into-making-impact-for-aberdeen/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 1 February 2021, Anderson joined fellow Premiership side [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Nash|first=Marcus|date=1 February 2021|title=Bruce Anderson joins Accies on loan|url=https://hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/bruce-anderson-joins-accies-on-loan/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210203064238/https://hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/bruce-anderson-joins-accies-on-loan/ |archive-date=2021-02-03 |access-date=1 February 2021|website=hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Hamilton in a 4–1 win against [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] on 13 February 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55959967|title=Motherwell 1-4 Hamilton|date=13 February 2021|publisher=BBC|access-date=15 February 2021|archive-date=13 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210213183656/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55959967|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Livingston===
Anderson signed a three-year contract with [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] in May 2021, which due to take effect when his contract with Aberdeen expires.<ref name = jet>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57163573 |title=Jay Emmanuel-Thomas moves to Aberdeen from Livingston |website=BBC Sport |date=18 May 2021 |accessdate=18 May 2021 |archive-date=11 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220111162614/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57163573 |url-status=live }}</ref> He moved in the opposite direction of fellow striker [[Jay Emmanuel-Thomas]], who signed a two-year contract with Aberdeen on the same day.<ref name = jet/>

Anderson was Livingston's top scorer in the [[2021–22 Livingston F.C. season|2021-22 season]], bagging 11 league goals and 13 across all competitions in 34 appearances. The following season was less fruitful, with a return of 7 goals in the 36 appearances. His performances did, however, catch the attention of [[Erovnuli Liga|Georgian]] side [[FC Torpedo Kutaisi]] who made a six-figure transfer offer for the forward, which Livingston accepted.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/livingston-striker-bruce-anderson-talks-30391524|title=Livingston Striker Bruce Anderson in talks over Georgia move after bid accepted by Lions|date=4 July 2021|publisher=Daily Record|access-date=19 December 2023|archive-date=22 June 2026|archive-url=https://megalodon.jp/2026-0622-1328-30/https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk:443/sport/local-sport/livingston-striker-bruce-anderson-talks-30391524|url-status=live}}</ref> Anderson turned down the move without entering into discussions with the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aberdeenlive.news/sport/football/ex-aberdeen-striker-bruce-anderson-8578946|title=Ex-Aberdeen striker Bruce Anderson staying put at Livingston as he knocks back Georgia offer|date=6 July 2021|publisher=Aberdeen Live|access-date=19 December 2023|archive-date=22 June 2026|archive-url=https://megalodon.jp/2026-0622-1328-39/https://www.aberdeenlive.news:443/sport/football/ex-aberdeen-striker-bruce-anderson-8578946|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Kilmarnock===
After leaving Livingston as a free agent, Anderson signed a two-year contract with [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] in May 2024. Anderson departed from the club in July of 2026 upon expiry of his contract. 
<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cg338xw9veno |title=Bruce Anderson: Kilmarnock sign striker after Livingston exit |website=BBC Sport |date=29 May 2024 |access-date=29 May 2024 |archive-date=29 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240529164246/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cg338xw9veno |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Return to Livingston ===
After spending pre-season on trial with [[EFL League Two]] side [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]], on 1 August 2026 Anderson returned to Livingston on a one year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 August 2026 |title=Brucey's Back |url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/bruceys-back/ |access-date=3 August 2026 |website=Livingston FC}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=3 August 2026 |title=Rotherham United trialist leaves and signs for another club |url=https://www.rotherhamadvertiser.co.uk/sport/football/rotherham-united/rotherham-united-trialist-leaves-and-signs-for-another-club-8836481 |access-date=3 August 2026 |website=Rotherham Advertiser}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Anderson has spoken publicly about life as a footballer with [[type-1 diabetes]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/watch/video/sports/football/13008016/living-with-diabetes-livingstons-bruce-anderson-tells-his-story/ |title=Living with diabetes - Livingston's Bruce Anderson shares his story |publisher=Sky Sports |access-date=2 January 2024 |archive-date=2 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240102181635/https://www.skysports.com/watch/video/sports/football/13008016/living-with-diabetes-livingstons-bruce-anderson-tells-his-story |url-status=live }}</ref> Anderson first learned of his condition after being hospitalised with a football injury while playing for Aberdeen as a teenager.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aberdeenlive.news/sport/football/football-news/former-aberdeen-striker-bruce-anderson-8905675/ |title=Former Aberdeen striker Bruce Anderson opens up on struggle with diabetes |date=14 November 2023|publisher=Aberdeen Live|access-date=2 January 2024}}</ref> During a match for Livingston in 2021, Anderson collapsed having suffered a diabetic [[seizure]] on the pitch but made a full recovery.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/livingston-taking-steps-to-ensure-bruce-anderson-incident-doesnt-happen-again-1631195598000|title=Livingston taking steps to ensure Bruce Anderson incident doesn't happen again |date=9 September 2021|publisher=FourFourTwo|access-date=2 January 2024}}</ref>
