'''Ben Michael Dempsey''' (born 25 November 1999) is an English professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].

==Career==

===Charlton Athletic===
Having signed his first professional contract with [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] in May 2018,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cafc.co.uk/news/view/5afd85f9a03cc/charlton-announce-list-of-released-and-retained-players |title=Charlton announce list of released and retained players |date=18 May 2018 |publisher=Charlton Athletic F.C. |language=en |access-date=23 March 2020}}</ref> Dempsey made his debut for Charlton on 14 August 2018, playing the full 90 minutes in a 3–0 [[EFL Trophy]] defeat to [[Milton Keynes Dons F.C.|Milton Keynes Dons]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2018/08/14/england/league-cup/milton-keynes-dons-fc/charlton-athletic-football-club/2796950/|title=Milton Keynes Dons vs. Charlton Athletic - 14 August 2018 - Soccerway|website=int.soccerway.com|access-date=23 March 2020}}</ref>

====Loans====
Dempsey joined [[Kingstonian F.C.|Kingstonian]] on loan in December 2019<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.wimbledonguardian.co.uk/sport/football/17293047.kingstonian-add-right-back-and-midfielder-to-squad/ |title=K's add more players to their ranks |date=12 December 2018 |work=Wimbledon Times |access-date=23 March 2020 |language=en}}</ref> before joining [[Dulwich Hamlet F.C.|Dulwich Hamlet]] on a one-month loan on 8 November 2019,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pitchero.com/clubs/dulwichhamlet/news/dulwich-hamlet-announce-double-signing-2484384.html |title=Dulwich Hamlet announce double signing |date=8 November 2019 |publisher=Dulwich Hamlet F.C. |language=en |access-date=23 March 2020}}</ref> making his debut for Dulwich on that day in a 4–1 [[FA Cup]] defeat to [[Carlisle United F.C.|Carlisle United]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2019/11/08/england/fa-cup/dulwich-hamlet-fc/carlisle-united-fc/3180658/ |title=Dulwich Hamlet vs. Carlisle United - 8 November 2019 - Soccerway |website=uk.soccerway.com |access-date=23 March 2020}}</ref>

He then joined [[Woking F.C.|Woking]] on loan in February 2020 for the rest of the 2019-20 season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.wokingfc.co.uk/news/article/7000/dempsey-joins-on-loan/ |title=Dempsey joins on loan |date=10 February 2020 |publisher=Woking F.C. |language=en |access-date=23 March 2020}}</ref> On 12 October 2020, Dempsey returned to Woking for a second loan spell, this time running until 9 January 2021.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Ben Dempsey returns on loan |url=https://www.wokingfc.co.uk/news/article/7203/ben-dempsey-returns-on-loan/ |publisher=[[Woking F.C.]] |date=12 October 2020 |accessdate=12 October 2020}}</ref> On 13 January 2021, the loan was extended until the end of the 2020-21 season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.wokingfc.co.uk/news/article/7336/three-loans-extended/ |title=Three loans extended |publisher=Woking FC |date=13 January 2021}}</ref>

On 24 January 2022, Dempsey joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] on loan for the rest of the 2021–22 season, with an option for a permanent deal in the summer.<ref>{{cite web |title= Ben Dempsey joins Ayr United on loan|url=https://www.cafc.co.uk/news/view/61eecace044a2/ben-dempsey-joins-ayr-united-on-loan |publisher=[[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] |access-date=24 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Wilson|first=Stuart|date=2022-01-24|title=Ayr United new boy Ben Dempsey on his decision to jump at move north|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/ayrshire/charlton-athletic-ace-ben-dempsey-26034641|access-date=2022-01-24|website=Daily Record|language=en}}</ref>

===Ayr United===
On 16 May 2022, it was announced that Dempsey would join Ayr United on a permanent deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Ben Dempsey joins Ayr United on permanent deal |url=https://www.cafc.co.uk/news/view/62812e8b40c64/ben-dempsey-joins-ayr-united-on-permanent-deal |publisher=Charlton Athletic Official Site |date=16 May 2022 |access-date=16 May 2022}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle===
In June 2026 Dempsey signed with fellow [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on a two year deal.<ref>https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/jags-add-ben-dempsey-on-two-year-deal/</ref>

'''Aidan Fitzpatrick''' (born 20 March 2001) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Winger (association football)|winger]] for {{Scottish football updater|PartickT}} club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] and has previously played for [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] and [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]].

==Club career==
===Partick Thistle (first spell)===
From [[Partick]] in [[Glasgow]], Fitzpatrick started playing football at St Peters Primary School. He was recommended to [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] and progressed through the club's youth system.<ref name="primary">{{cite news |last1=Fisher |first1=Stewart |title=Aidan Fitzpatrick: My Primary 7 teacher set me on course for Partick finishing school |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/16604086.aidan-fitzpatrick-my-primary-7-teacher-set-me-on-course-for-partick-finishing-school/ |accessdate=25 January 2019 |work=The Herald |date=28 August 2018 |location=Glasgow}}</ref>

Fitzpatrick debuted for the first-team versus [[Albion Rovers F.C.|Albion Rovers]] in the [[2018–19 Scottish League Cup]] in July 2018, coming on as a substitute and scoring a goal in the 2–0 win. He was the first player born in the 21st century to play for Partick Thistle.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McGarry |first1=Graeme |title=Christie Elliott says Partick Thistle youngster Aidan Fitzpatrick 'has everything' |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/16377877.christie-elliott-says-partick-thistle-youngster-aidan-fitzpatrick-has-everything/ |accessdate=25 January 2019 |work=The Herald |date=26 July 2018 |location=Glasgow}}</ref> On his first starting appearance versus [[Stranraer F.C.|Stranraer]] in the [[2018–19 Scottish Challenge Cup]], Fitzpatrick scored two goals and had an assist in a 5–0 victory, winning an ''Irn-Bru Golden Balls'' award.<ref name="primary" /> He signed a new long-term contract in September 2018.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McDougall |first1=Mark |title=Partick Thistle secure long-term future of highly-rated teen Aidan Fitzpatrick |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/partick-thistle-secure-long-term-13234318 |accessdate=25 January 2019 |work=Daily Record |date=12 September 2018 |location=Glasgow}}</ref> 
Thistle confirmed in January 2019 that the club had received two bids for Fitzpatrick, one in the summer of 2018 and one in January 2019,<ref name="BBC Sport">{{Cite news|title=Partick earn first away win of season|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47011588|access-date=2021-08-02}}</ref> however, both bids were turned down.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/player-update-4/|title=Player Update}}</ref>

Fitzpatrick scored his first league goal for Partick Thistle in the 2–1 away win to [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] in February 2019. The following month, he scored a stoppage time winner for Thistle in a 2–1 home win over [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Thistle off bottom as United falter|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47425110|access-date=2021-08-02}}</ref> In his first season of senior football, Fitzpatrick made 28 appearances for the [[Firhill Stadium|Firhill]] club  across all competitions, scoring seven goals and having four assists.<ref name="BBC Sport"/>

===Norwich City===
On 5 July 2019, Fitzpatrick signed for [[Premier League]] club [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] for a fee reported to be in the region of £350,000.<ref>{{cite web|title=Aidan Fitzpatrick: Partick Thistle midfielder joins Norwich |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48885726 |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |accessdate=6 July 2019 |date=5 July 2019}}</ref>

===Queen of the South===
On 24 August 2020, Fitzpatrick signed for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] in a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=24 August 2020|title=Aidan Fitzpatrick|url=http://www.qosfc.com/news-5158|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=24 August 2020|website=qosfc.com}}</ref> On 8 September 2021, after securing his contract release from Norwich, he signed a one-year permanent contract with Queen of the South.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.qosfc.com/news-5526|title = QosFC: Welcome (Back) - Aidan Fitzpatrick}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle (second spell)===
On 13 July 2022, Fitzpatrick signed a two-year deal with Partick Thistle once again. Although his contract at previous club Queen of the South had expired, the ''Doonhamers'' held out for a compensation fee, due to the player still being under 23 years old.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://qosfc.com/news-5813 | title=QosFC: Aidan Fitzpatrick }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/signing-news-aidan-fitzpatrick-returns-to-firhill/ | title=SIGNING NEWS: Aidan Fitzpatrick returns to Firhill }}</ref>

In June 2023 Fitzpatrick extended his contract with Thistle, adding an extra two years on to his deal, extending it until June 2026.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/aidan-fitzpatrick-pens-contract-extension-until-2026/#:~:text=Partick%20Thistle%20are%20delighted%20to,campaign%2C%20subject%20to%20SFA%20approval. | title=Aidan Fitzpatrick pens contract extension until 2026 }}</ref>

Fitzpatrick signed a new one year contract extension with Thistle in June 2026, extending his deal until summer 2027.<ref>https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/aidan-fitzpatrick-pens-new-one-year-deal/</ref>

'''Jordan Doherty''' (born 29 August 2000) is an Irish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] or [[defender (association football)|defender]] for [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref name="Soccerway">{{Soccerway|477625|accessdate=12 March 2019}}</ref>

== Career ==
After spending the [[2019 USL Championship season|2019]] season on loan with the [[Tampa Bay Rowdies]], Doherty joined the team on a permanent basis on 24 January 2020.<ref>{{cite web |title=Back in 2020: Jordan Doherty |url=https://www.rowdiessoccer.com/news_article/show/1080222 |website=RowdiesSoccer.com |publisher=Tampa Bay Rowdies |date=24 January 2020 |accessdate=9 April 2020}} {{Dead link|date=November 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> Following the 2021 season it was announced that Doherty would leave the Rowdies.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uslchampionship.com/news_article/show/1199382-rowdies-announce-initial-roster-moves-for-2022-season|title=Rowdies Announce Initial Roster Moves for 2022 Season|author=USLChampionship com Staff|date=December 17, 2021|website=USL Championship}}</ref> Doherty signed with Irish club [[Bohemian F.C.|Bohemians]] in December 2021.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Fitzmaurice |first1=Aidan |title=Bohemians strengthen squad with signing of US-based midfielder Jordan Doherty |url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/league-of-ireland/bohemians-strengthen-squad-with-signing-of-us-based-midfielder-jordan-doherty-41172351.html |website=Independent.ie |date=21 December 2021 |publisher=[[Irish Independent]] |access-date=12 January 2023}}</ref>

Doherty returned to the Rowdies on 12 January 2023.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rowdies Welcome Jordan Doherty Back to Squad |url=https://www.rowdiessoccer.com/news/2023/01/12/rowdies-jordan-doherty-back-to-squad/ |website=RowdiesSoccer.com |publisher=[[Tampa Bay Rowdies]] |access-date=12 January 2023}}</ref> He left Tampa Bay following their 2024 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rowdiessoccer.com/news/2024/11/25/rowdies-announce-2024-end-of-year-roster-updates/|title=Rowdies Announce 2024 End of Year Roster Updates}}</ref>

He signed for [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] in May 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/5499360/jordan-doherty-raith-rovers-fc-championship-livingston/|title=Jordan Doherty reacts to Raith Rovers exit as he joins Championship rivals|date=26 May 2026|publisher=The Courier}}</ref>

'''Matthew Todd''' (born 14 June 2001), commonly known as '''Matty Todd''', is a Scottish professional [[footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].

==Career==
Todd was one of six players to join [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] in May 2018 after graduating from Fife Elite Football Academy.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Reserve_squad_takes_shape&ID=10626 |title=Reserve squad takes shape |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=24 May 2018 |accessdate=6 April 2019}}</ref> He had previously taken part in a number of Dunfermline matches, and scored in a [[Fife Cup]] match against [[Burntisland Shipyard F.C.|Burntisland Shipyard]], which was abandoned after 50 minutes due to a serious injury to Pars player [[Aaron Splaine]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Matty_Todd_signs_for_Dunfermline&ID=10627 |title=Matty Todd signs |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=25 May 2018 |accessdate=6 April 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Fife_Cup_v_Burntisland_Shipyard&ID=10323 |title=Fife Cup v Burntisland Shipyard |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=22 November 2017 |accessdate=6 April 2019}}</ref>

Todd made his first appearance after signing with the club in a [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] victory over [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]], playing the full 90 minutes.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/fixture.php?SID=First%20Team&D=2018-08-14&ID=1150 |title=Inverness Caley Thistle 1 Dunfermline Athletic 2 |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=14 August 2018 |accessdate=6 April 2019}}</ref> His first [[Scottish Championship|league]] appearance came in a 3–0 win over [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]], where he replaced [[Kallum Higginbotham]] in the final minutes of the match.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/fixture.php?SID=First%20Team&D=2019-02-26&ID=1138 |title=Dunfermline 3 Partick Thistle 0 |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=26 February 2019 |accessdate=6 April 2019}}</ref>

In September 2020, Todd moved on season-long loan to [[Scottish League Two]] side [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Matty_Todd_goes_out_on_loan&ID=12572 |title=Matty Todd goes out on loan |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=25 September 2020 |accessdate=25 September 2020}}</ref> Following the postponement of football in the Scottish lower leagues in January 2021, Todd was recalled by his parent club.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=One_signing_in_and_two_recalls&ID=12797 |title=One signing in and two recalls |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=14 January 2021 |accessdate=14 January 2021}}</ref>

Following Dunfermline's relegation to [[Scottish League One|League One]], Todd became a first team regular making 40 appearances and scoring 10 goals in the [[2022–23 Dunfermline Athletic F.C. season|2022-23 Season]]. Todd won numerous end of season awards including Goal of the Season and Young Player of the Season,<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Player_of_the_Year_Awards_2022-2023&ID=14359 | title=Player of the Year Awards 2022-2023 | website=dafc.co.uk}}</ref> as well as being inducted in to the [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year]].

In June 2026, Todd moved to [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on a two year contract until summer 2028.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Matty Todd signs for Saints! {{!}} ST JOHNSTONE FC |url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/matty-todd-signs-for-saints/ |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk |language=en-GB}}</ref>

'''Cameron Palmer''' (born 15 May 2000) is a [[Northern Ireland|Northern Irish]] professional footballer who plays for [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Livingston F.C. | Livingston]]

A product of the [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] youth academy, Palmer has previously had loan spells with [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]], [[Orange County SC|Orange County]] and [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]].

==Club career==
===Early career===
Palmer was born in [[York|York, England]] and raised in [[Toronto]], [[Ontario]], Canada. He is the son of Don Palmer, a church pastor, author, and speaker, currently residing in Edinburgh, but originally from [[Belfast]]. Cammy (Cameron) moved with his family to Canada when he was only 8 months old. He started playing competitive soccer at age 5, playing for [[Pickering FC|Pickering SC]], Ajax SC and eventually [[Darby FC#Whitby FC|Whitby Iroquois SC]]. Whilst playing for Whitby in [[Ontario]], former Rangers player [[Andy Kennedy (footballer, born 1964)|Andy Kennedy]] came across the young footballer. Kennedy contacted Rangers and told them about the youngster. His family moved back to Scotland in 2011 and Palmer went on trial and very soon joined the youth ranks of the [[Glasgow]] giants.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Jack |first1=Christopher |title=From Canada to Copland Road: Cammy Palmer has a former Rangers striker to thank for starting his Ibrox journey |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/16977178.from-canada-to-copland-road-cammy-palmer-has-a-former-rangers-striker-to-thank-for-starting-his-ibrox-journey/ |website=www.heraldscotland.com |date=12 October 2018 |publisher=The Herald |access-date=18 July 2019}}</ref> After impressing at numerous levels at the club, Palmer was named as the reserve side's team captain in 2018.

===Professional career===
After a solid progression at youth level for Rangers, Palmer signed a contract extension with the [[Ibrox Stadium|Ibrox]] side until 2021 in June 2019.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Shaw |first1=Louise |title=Palmer Signs Contract Extension |url=https://rangers.co.uk/news/academy-news/palmer-signs-contract-extension/ |website=www.rangers.co.uk |publisher=Rangers Football Club |access-date=18 July 2019}}</ref>

On 10 July 2019, Palmer joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on loan until January 2020. Three days later Palmer made his professional footballing debut in a 1-0 win in the [[Scottish League Cup]] against [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] at [[Firhill Stadium|Firhill]].<ref>{{cite web |title=LOAN NEWS: Cammy Palmer joins on loan |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/loan-news-cammy-palmer-joins-on-loan/ |website=www.ptfc.co.uk |publisher=Partick Thistle FC |access-date=18 July 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Labellarte |first1=Giuseppe |title=Rangers fans react on Twitter as Ibrox academy ace Cammy Palmer seals loan move to Partick Thistle |url=https://www.hitc.com/rangers-fans-cammy-palmer-loan-partick-thistle/ |website=www.hitc.com |date=10 July 2019 |publisher=HITC |access-date=18 July 2019}}</ref> Palmer scored his first professional goal scoring for Thistle in a 3-1 away win over Inverness.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-fixture/inverness-caledonian-thistle-v-partick-thistle-28th-september-2019/|title=Inverness Caledonian Thistle v Partick Thistle – 28th September 2019}}</ref>

On 3 February 2020, Palmer joined [[USL Championship]] club [[Orange County SC]] on loan for the 2020 season.<ref>{{cite web  |title= Rangers Players Head to Orange County SC|url=https://www.orangecountysoccer.com/news_article/show/1083100 |website=orangecountysoccer.com |date=3 February 2020 |access-date=3 February 2020}}</ref>

Palmer was loaned to [[Scottish League One]] club [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]] in October 2020.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/rangers-northern-ireland-youth-star-22935962 |title=Rangers and Northern Ireland youth star makes Clyde switch |first=Paul |last=Thomson |newspaper=Daily Record |date=31 October 2020 |access-date=22 November 2020}}</ref>

On 27 January 2021, Palmer joined [[NIFL Premiership]] side [[Linfield F.C.]] on an 18-month contract.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hendry |first1=Mark |title=Rangers youngster Cammy Palmer joins Linfield on permanent deal |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/19042014.rangers-youngster-cammy-palmer-joins-linfield-permanent-deal/ |website=www.heraldscotland.com |date=27 January 2021 |publisher=Herald Scotland |access-date=27 January 2021}}</ref>

'''Daniel O'Reilly''' (born 11 April 1995) is an Irish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays for {{Scottish football updater|PartickT}} club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] as a [[centre back]].<ref>{{soccerway|daniel-oreilly/213966}}</ref><ref name="eurosport">{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurosport.co.uk/football/daniel-o-reilly_prs420679/person.shtml|title=Daniel O'Reilly - Player Profile - Football|website=Eurosport UK}}</ref>

==Early life==
O'Reilly was born in [[Dublin]].<ref name="eurosport"/> He grew up in [[Celbridge]] and attended [[Salesian College Celbridge]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/daniel.oreilly.330|title=Daniel O'Reilly|website=www.facebook.com}}</ref>

== Club career ==

===Early career===
O'Reilly started his youth career with [[Cherry Orchard F.C.|Cherry Orchard]] before being signed by [[Fulham F.C. Academy|Fulham Academy]] in November 2010 aged 15.<ref name="auto"/> On 30 January 2014, O'Reilly was sent to [[Walton Casuals F.C.|Walton Casuals]] on a one-month loan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fulhamfc.com/|title=Fulham FC|first=Fulham|last=FC|website=Fulham FC}}</ref> He stayed at Fulham in four years before being released, then had a brief stay at [[Southern Football League|Southern Premier League]] [[Hereford United F.C.|Hereford United]] in 2014 before the club collapsed.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.extratime.com/player/11119282/player/|title=Extratime.com - Extratime.ie - Daniel O'Reilly|website=www.extratime.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TEUwBwAAQBAJ&q=%22Daniel+O%27Reilly%22&pg=PT24|title=The Blizzard - The Football Quarterly: Issue Sixteen|first1=Jonathan|last1=Wilson|first2=Dileep|last2=Premachandran|first3=James|last3=Corbett|first4=Stuart Roy|last4=Clarke|first5=Ben|last5=Lyttleton|first6=Scott|last6=Murray|date=11 March 2015|publisher=Blizzard Media Ltd|via=Google Books}}</ref> He subsequently moved to [[Bishop's Stortford F.C.|Bishop's Stortford]].

===Return to Ireland===
O'Reilly then returned to Ireland to play with [[Bray Wanderers F.C.|Bray Wanderers]]. After a brief period at [[Eastbourne Borough F.C.|Eastbourne Borough]], O'Reilly returned in 2016 to the [[League of Ireland]], playing with [[Longford Town F.C.|Longford Town]] and [[Finn Harps F.C.|Finn Harps]].<ref name="ltfc">{{cite web|url=http://ltfc.ie/player/daniel-oreilly/|title=Daniel O'Reilly – Longford Town FC • Official Website|website=ltfc.ie|accessdate=29 November 2019|archive-date=19 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201019161350/http://ltfc.ie/player/daniel-oreilly/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.extratime.ie/player/11119282/daniel_oreilly/|title=Extratime.ie - Daniel O'Reilly|website=www.extratime.ie}}</ref>

At the end of the 2019 season he was voted Supporter's Player of the Year at Finn Harps. In November 2019 O'Reilly signed for [[Shelbourne F.C.|Shelbourne]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://shelbournefc.ie/player_profile/daniel-oreilly/|title=Daniel O'Reilly|access-date=29 November 2019|archive-date=24 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200924234301/https://shelbournefc.ie/player_profile/daniel-oreilly/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In December 2020 he moved to [[2020 League of Ireland First Division]] Winners [[Drogheda United F.C.|Drogheda United]] ahead of their first season back in the [[League of Ireland Premier Division]], where he was voted Club Player of the Year in his only season at the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://droghedaunited.ie/daniel-oreilly-signs-for-drogheda-united/|title=Daniel O'Reilly Signs For Drogheda United|date=19 December 2020}}</ref>

===Hamilton Academical===
On 1 January 2022, O'Reilly's agency (Stephen Hunt Management) announced that he had signed for [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]], after rejecting several offers from Ireland.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/dans-the-man-for-accies/|title=Dan's the man for Accies|date=1 January 2022|access-date=1 January 2022|archive-date=1 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220101130342/https://hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/dans-the-man-for-accies/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Raith Rovers===
In November 2023 O'Reilly signed a deal until January 2024 with [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] after remaining a free agent since he left Hamilton in June 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.raithrovers.net/65387/daniel-oreilly-signs.htm|title=O'Reilly Signs|website=Raith Rovers press release|date=20 November 2023|access-date=23 January 2024}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle===
O'Reilly signed for fellow [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] in January 2024 on an 18-month contract.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/signing-news-daniel-oreilly-is-a-jag/ | title=Signing News: Daniel O'Reilly is a Jag! }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/24041409.oreilly-transfer-coup-real-partick-thistle-statement-intent/ | title=Daniel O'Reilly transfer coup real Partick Thistle statement of intent | date=11 January 2024 }}</ref>

O'Reilly signed a one-year contract extension with Thistle in October 2024.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Dan O’Reilly signs one-year contract extension  {{!}}  Partick Thistle FC | url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/dan-oreilly-signs-one-year-contract-extension/ | access-date=2025-07-26 | website=ptfc.co.uk}}</ref>

O'Reilly scored his first goal for Thistle with a header from a corner, in a 2–0 away win over Airdrie.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Airdrieonians vs Partick Thistle: Scottish Championship stats & head-to-head - BBC Sport | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c5ywl9p44kwt | access-date=2025-07-26 | website=www.bbc.co.uk}}</ref>

O’Reilly won the Partick Thistle player of the year award for 2024–25, as voted for by Thistle supporters.<ref>{{Cite tweet | user=partickthistle| number=1911169448125358322 | title=The winner of the 2024/25 @McCreaFS Player of the Year Award is Dan O'Reilly}}</ref>

In October 2025, O’Reilly signed a further contract extension with Thistle, signing an extension until summer 2027, with the option of a further extension.<ref>https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/dan-oreilly-signs-contract-extension/</ref>

==International career==
O'Reilly was selected as an unused sub for the [[Republic of Ireland national under-17 football team|Republic of Ireland U17]] team in 2012, in a qualifying game against [[Kazakhstan national under-17 football team|Kazakhstan]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fai.ie/ireland/match/23/2012/2004890|title=Kazakhstan 1 - 1 Republic of Ireland {{pipe}} 2012 - Under 17 {{pipe}} 2004890 {{pipe}} Football Association of Ireland|website=www.fai.ie}}</ref>

'''Bradly van Hoeven''' (born 17 April 2000) is a Dutch professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Winger (association football)|winger]] for {{Scottish football updater|Livingst}} club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].

==Club career==
Born in [[Maassluis]], Van Hoeven played in the youth departments of [[Excelsior Maassluis]] and [[Sparta Rotterdam]]. In 2018, he was moved to the Sparta reserve team, Jong Sparta, competing in the [[Tweede Divisie]]. He made his professional football debut for Sparta on 1 April 2019, in a 2–0 win over [[MVV Maastricht]], coming on as a substitute for [[Ragnar Ache]] in the 89th minute.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sparta wint op verjaardag van MVV |url=https://www.sparta-rotterdam.nl/sparta-wint-op-verjaardag-mvv/ |publisher=[[Sparta Rotterdam]] |accessdate=15 October 2020 |language=Dutch |date=1 April 2019 |quote=In de slotfase maakte Bradly van Hoeven nog zijn eerste minuten in Sparta 1. De jongeling, die vele jaren in de opleiding doorbracht, verving Ache.}}</ref> In June 2020, he joined [[Go Ahead Eagles]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bradly van Hoeven: 'Nieuwe stap in mij ontwikkeling' |url=https://www.ga-eagles.nl/bradly-hoeven-nieuwe-stap-ontwikkeling/ |publisher=[[Go Ahead Eagles]] |accessdate=15 October 2020 |language=Dutch |date=12 June 2020}}</ref>

On 27 June 2021, van Hoeven moved to [[Eerste Divisie]] club [[Almere City FC]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Perry|date=27 June 2021|title=Bradly van Hoeven vanaf zondag bij selectie|url=https://almerecity.nl/almere-city-1/bradly-van-hoeven-vanaf-zondag-bij-selectie/|access-date=24 August 2021|website=Almere City FC|language=nl}}</ref> On 12 January 2023, he was sent on loan to [[TOP Oss]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=TOP Oss|url=https://toposs.nl/bradly-van-hoeven-naar-oss/|title=De voorhoede van TOP Oss versterkt zich met Bradly van Hoeven|date=12 January 2023|access-date=23 January 2023|language=nl}}</ref> On 1 February 2024, van Hoeven was loaned by [[FC Emmen|Emmen]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Emmen|url=https://fcemmen.nl/fc-emmen-huurt-bradly-van-hoeven/|title=FC EMMEN HUURT BRADLY VAN HOEVEN|trans-title=FC EMMEN LOANS BRADLY VAN HOEVEN|date=1 February 2024|access-date=3 February 2024|language=nl}}</ref>

On 24 September 2024, van Hoeven joined Polish [[Ekstraklasa]] club [[Motor Lublin]] for the remainder of the season, with an option for a further year.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Galiński |first1=Tomasz |title=Motor Lublin pozyskał nowego skrzydłowego. Prosto z Holandii |url=https://sportowefakty.wp.pl/pilka-nozna/1147568/motor-lublin-pozyskal-nowego-skrzydlowego-prosto-z-holandii |website=sportowefakty.wp.pl |access-date=27 September 2024 |language=pl |date=24 September 2024}}</ref> He made his debut the following day as a second-half substitute in a 0–2 home loss to [[Jagiellonia Białystok]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Sezon 2024/25 |url=http://www.90minut.pl/wystepy.php?id=49594&id_sezon=105 |website=90minut.pl |access-date=27 September 2024 |language=pl}}</ref> After van Hoeven became a regular starter following the winter break, Motor exercised their option on his contract in April 2025.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bradly van Hoeven też zostaje w Motorze |url=https://www.dziennikwschodni.pl/sport/pilka-nozna/ekstraklasa/bradly-van-hoeven-tez-zostaje-w-motorze,n,1000359536.html |website=dziennikwschodni.pl |access-date=6 April 2025 |language=pl |date=2 April 2025}}</ref> On 10 June 2026, Motor announced they would not be extending van Hoeven's contract for the following season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Oficjalnie! Holenderski skrzydłowy odchodzi z Motoru |url=https://przegladsportowy.onet.pl/pilka-nozna/ekstraklasa/oficjalnie-holenderski-skrzydlowy-odchodzi-z-motoru/xh5ek5h |website=przegladsportowy.onet.pl |access-date=3 July 2026 |language=pl |date=10 June 2026}}</ref>

'''Patrick James Reading''' (born 29 May 1999) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|left-back]] for club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].

==Club career==

===Stevenage===
Reading spent his youth career at [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]], before he joined [[Stevenage F.C.|Stevenage]] on 31 January 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51332475|title=Stevenage: Ben Folami, Canice Carroll & Patrick Reading join League Two strugglers|work=BBC Sport |date=31 January 2020}}</ref> Reading made his Stevenage debut, playing the full 90 minutes in a 2–1 loss to Exeter City in League Two.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/545323/stevenage-exeter-city|title=Exeter 2-1 Stevenage (8 Feb, 2020) Final Score - ESPN (UK)|website=ESPN}}</ref>

He was released by Stevenage at the end of the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stevenagefc.com/news/2020/june/stevenage-football-club-retained-released-list-202021-sky-bet-league-two-efl-english-football-league-thursday-18th-june-2020/|title=Stevenage 2020/21 Retained & Released List|website=www.stevenagefc.com}}</ref>

===Ayr United===
In July 2020 he signed a two-year deal with [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ayrunitedfc.co.uk/patrick-reading-signs-for-united/|title=Patrick Reading signs for United|publisher=Ayr United F.C.|accessdate=21 July 2020|archive-date=9 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200809180906/https://ayrunitedfc.co.uk/patrick-reading-signs-for-united/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
Reading scored his first goal for Ayr United in January 2021, in a 3–2 away defeat to Queen of the South.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/55450497|title=Queen of the South 3-2 Ayr United: Dramatic finish as home side earn back-to-back wins|work=BBC Sport |date=2 January 2021}}</ref>

In May 2022 Reading signed a two year extension to his deal with Ayr United.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/ayrshire/paddy-reading-ayr-uniteds-long-27011830|title=Paddy Reading: Ayr United's vision sold me on new deal|first=Stuart|last=Wilson|date=19 May 2022|website=Daily Record}}</ref>

On 24 May 2024, Reading signed a further two year extension to his Ayr United contract, extending his deal until 2026.<ref>{{Cite tweet | user=ayrunitedfc | number=1793945040215331303 | title=The Club are delighted to announce that Paddy Reading has signed a 2-year contract extension and continues his stay at Somerset Park until June 2026...}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle===
After five years with Ayr United, Reading joined fellow [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on a free transfer in June 2025, signing a two year deal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/partick-thistle-sign-paddy-reading-from-ayr-united/|title=Partick Thistle sign Paddy Reading from Ayr United.|website=Partick Thistle FC}}</ref> Reading made his Thistle debut  in a 4–1 away victory over Edinburgh City in the Scottish League Cup group stages.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cx24yx2krgnt|title=Edinburgh City vs Partick Thistle: League Cup stats & head-to-head|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

Reading scored his first Thistle goal on the opening day of the 2025–26 Scottish Championship season, in an away defeat to St Johnstone.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c3r4l08jjl7t|title=St Johnstone vs Partick Thistle: Scottish Championship updates & match report, BBC Sport|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

==International career==
He has represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] level.<ref>{{SFA Profile|id=530106}}</ref>

'''Reece McAlear''' (born 12 February 2002) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|StJohnst}} club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].

==Career==
He joined [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] from [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] for an undisclosed fee in summer 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Fraser |date=26 July 2019 |title=Reece McAlear leaves Motherwell for Norwich City |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-transfer-news/reece-mcalear-leaves-motherwell-norwich-18780957 |access-date=1 December 2020 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref>

He made his debut on 28 November 2020 as a substitute in a league match against Coventry City.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55025707|title=Late Coventry goal pegs back Norwich|work=BBC Sport |date=28 November 2020 |accessdate=1 December 2020}}</ref><ref name="sb">{{soccerbase|125105}}</ref>

On 17 June 2021, McAlear joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ictfc.com/reece-mcalear-signs-for-ictfc-on-loan|title=Reece McAlear Signs For ICTFC On Loan|publisher=[[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.]]|date=17 June 2021|accessdate=17 June 2021}}</ref>

On 21 May 2022, it was announced that McAlear would be released by Norwich City at the end of the season when his contract expired.<ref>{{cite news |title=Rupp to depart as club confirm released players |url=https://www.canaries.co.uk/content/norwich-city-retained-list-lukas-rupp-to-depart-at-the-end-of-the-season |access-date=20 May 2022 |publisher=Norwich City FC |date=20 May 2022}}</ref>

On 9 June 2022, it was announced that McAlear had signed for [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]] on a two-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 June 2022 |title=Reece McAlear: Tranmere Rovers sign former Norwich midfielder |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/61752223 |access-date=2 July 2022 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 31 January 2023, McAlear joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Midfielder Reece McAlear leaves Tranmere for Ayr United loan spell |url=https://www.wirralglobe.co.uk/sport/23288748.midfielder-reece-mcalear-leaves-tranmere-ayr-united-loan-spell/ |access-date=2023-01-31 |website=Wirral Globe |date=31 January 2023 |language=en}}</ref> He was released by Tranmere at the end of the [[2023–24 Tranmere Rovers F.C. season|2023–24 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tranmererovers.co.uk/news/2024/april/202324-retained-and-released-list/|title=2023/24 retained and released list|website=www.tranmererovers.co.uk|date=30 April 2024|accessdate=30 April 2024}}</ref>

In May 2024, McAlear signed a pre-contract with [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on an initial one-year deal, with an automatic one-year extension triggered by promotion.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/reece-the-next-piece-in-the-lions-squad/|title=Reece the next piece in the Lions squad|date=29 May 2024|publisher=Livingston FC}}</ref>

In July 2025, McAlear signed for [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] for an undisclosed amount.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/reece-mcalear-signs-for-saints|title=Reece McAlear signs for Saints!|date=18 July 2025|publisher=St Johnstone FC}}</ref>

==International career==
McAlear has represented Scotland at youth international level.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/players/?pid=259862&lid=11|title=Reece McAlear at Scottish FA|publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]]|accessdate=17 June 2021}}</ref>

'''Adam Montgomery''' (born 18 July 2002) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[left-back]] or a [[left winger]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], on loan from [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].

==Career==
Montgomery signed his first professional contract with [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in July 2019, and he extended his contract to 2025 in February 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.67hailhail.com/news/celtic-secure-youngster-on-new-long-term-contract/|title=Celtic secure youngster on new long-term contract|website=67hailhail.com|date=27 February 2021|accessdate=13 May 2021}}</ref> After making the bench for the first team on four occasions, he made his professional debut for Celtic on 12 May 2021, starting in a 4–0 win over [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56990118|title=Celtic 4-0 St Johnstone|publisher=BBC|date=12 May 2021|accessdate=13 May 2021}}</ref>

On 31 January 2022, he joined [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] on loan until the end of the [[2021–22 Aberdeen F.C. season|2021–22 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2022/01/31/adam-montgomery-joins-the-dons-on-loan/|title=Adam Montgomery Joins The Dons On Loan|website=www.afc.co.uk|date=31 January 2022}}</ref>

On 3 July 2023, he signed for [[EFL League One|League One]] club [[Fleetwood Town F.C.|Fleetwood Town]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fleetwoodtownfc.com/news/2023/july/montgomery-signing/|title=Town sign Adam Montgomery on loan from Celtic for the season|website=www.fleetwoodtownfc.com|date=3 July 2023|accessdate=3 July 2023}}</ref>

On 15 January 2024, Montgomery joined [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] on loan until the end of the [[2023–24 Motherwell F.C. season|2023–24 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2024/01/15/adam-montgomery-joins-on-loan-from-celtic/|title=Adam Montgomery Joins On Loan From Celtic|website=www.motherwellfc.com|date=15 January 2024}}</ref> On 1 February 2024, he returned to [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] after suffering a serious injury during a training session.<ref>{{cite web |title=ADAM MONTGOMERY INJURY UPDATE |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2024/02/01/adam-montgomery-injury-update/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=1 February 2024 |date=1 February 2024}}</ref>

In July 2025, Montgomery signed for [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on loan.<ref>{{cite web |title=ADAM MONTGOMERY|url=https://x.com/LiviFCOfficial/status/1948714903528685946?t=RxEun0JVF95Evixl1CTlqg&s=19 |publisher=X|date=25 July 2025}}</ref> His loan agreement ended early in January 2026 due to another injury setback.<ref>{{cite web |title='Livi to buy Robertson' as Montgomery returns to Celtic - gossip|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c62r7119rn9o |publisher=BBC Sport|date=16 January 2026}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Montgomery started out as a forward at the club before being moved into defence by coach Darren O'Dea, and that paid off in February 2021 when the youngster extended his contract to 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.celticfc.com/players/celtic-b/Adam-Montgomery |title=Celtic secure youngster on new long-term contract|website=celticfc.com|date=18 June 2023|accessdate=18 June 2023}}</ref>

'''Ethan John Ingram''' (born 16 April 2003) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]]. Ingram came through the [[West Bromwich Albion F.C. Under-21s and Academy|West Bromwich Albion youth academy]], and has previously played for [[Salford City F.C.|Salford City]] and [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].

==Club career==
===West Bromwich Albion===
Born in [[Gloucester]], Ingram was scouted by one of [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]]'s development centre's aged 12, before joining their academy, signing his first scholarship deal aged 16.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ethan Ingram |url=https://www.wba.co.uk/player/83 |access-date=25 August 2021 |website=wba.co.uk |publisher=West Bromwich Albion F.C. |language=en}}</ref> He made his debut for the club on 25 August 2021, starting in a 6–0 [[EFL Cup]] second round defeat to [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58252911 |title=West Brom 0–6 Arsenal |website=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=25 August 2021 |access-date=27 April 2024}}</ref> Ingram scored the winning penalty in the final of the [[2021–22 Premier League Cup]] as West Brom beat [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C. Development Squad and Academy|Wolverhampton Wanderers U23]] 5–4 on penalties after a 2–2 draw.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.shropshirestar.com/sport/football/2022/05/16/penalty-hero-ethan-ingram-eyeing-west-brom-first-team-spot/ |title=Penalty hero Ethan Ingram eyeing West Brom first team spot |website=Shropshire Star |date=16 May 2022 |access-date=27 April 2024}}</ref>

====Salford City (loan)====
On 1 September 2023, Ingram joined [[EFL League Two]] club [[Salford City F.C.|Salford City]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.salfordcityfc.co.uk/news/2023/september/01/salford-sign-west-brom-defender-on-loan/ |title=Salford Sign West Brom Defender On Loan |website=Salford City |date=1 September 2023 |access-date=27 April 2024}}</ref> He made his debut for the club on 5 September 2023, in a 3–0 defeat away to [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] in the [[EFL Trophy]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/bolton-wanderers-vs-salford-city/teams/495029 |title=Bolton Wanderers vs Salford City |website=Sky Sports |date=5 September 2023 |access-date=27 April 2024}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club on 21 October 2023, in a 2–2 draw with [[Swindon Town F.C.|Swindon Town]] in a [[EFL League Two|League Two]] match.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c3gxpx0llpzt |title=Salford City 2–2 Swindon Town |website=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=21 October 2023 |access-date=27 April 2024}}</ref>

===Dundee===
On 4 July 2024, Ingram joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-07-04 |title=Ingram arrives |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/ingram-arrives/ |access-date=2024-07-04 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> Ingram made his debut for the ''Dark Blues'' in a 1–7 away victory over [[Bonnyrigg Rose F.C.|Bonnyrigg Rose]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bonnyrigg Rose vs. Dundee - 13 July 2024 - Soccerway |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2024/07/13/scotland/league-cup/bonnyrigg-rose-athletic-fc/dundee-fc/4360410/ |access-date=2024-07-13 |website=uk.soccerway.com}}</ref> Ingram scored his first goal for the club three days later in an away win over [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arbroath vs Dundee: League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4ngzrxwpxzt |access-date=2024-07-16 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

=== Partick Thistle ===
In February 2026, Ingram joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ethan Ingram arrives on loan from Dundee |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/ethan-ingram-arrives-on-loan-from-dundee/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Partick Thistle FC |language=en}}</ref> Ingram made ten appearances for the club, avoiding defeat in all ten games.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=9 July 2026 |title=Ethan Ingram returns on permanent deal|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/ethan-ingram-returns-on-permanent-deal/ |access-date=9 July 2026 |website=Partick Thistle F.C.}}</ref> At the end of the season Ingram departed Dundee.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-01 |title=Retained List 2026 |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/retained-list-2026/ |access-date=2026-06-01 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref>

Following his loan spell, Ingram signed permanently for [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] in July 2026, agreeing a two-year deal with the club.<ref name=":0" />

==International career==
He has represented England at [[England national under-17 football team|under-17]] and [[England national under-18 football team|under-18]] international levels.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ethan Ingram » Internationals |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/person/pe637440/ethan-ingram/international-matches/ |access-date=25 August 2021 |website=worldfootball.net |language=en}}</ref>

On 21 September 2022, Ingram made his [[England national under-20 football team|England U20]] debut as a substitute during a 3–0 victory over [[Chile national under-20 football team|Chile]] at the [[Pinatar Arena]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.englandfootball.com/articles/2022/Sep/21/england-mu20s-chile-pinatar-match-report-20222109|title=Report: England MU20s 3–0 Chile|first=Liam|last=Crane|date=21 September 2022|accessdate=25 September 2022|website=EnglandFootball.com}}</ref>

'''Jack Wilkie''' (born 20 December 2003)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jack Wilkie |url=https://www.arbroathfc.co.uk/players/jack-wilkie/ |access-date=2024-07-16 |website=Arbroath FC |language=en}}</ref> is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|Livingst}} club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{soccerbase|135704|accessdate=18 October 2021}}</ref> He has previously played for [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] and [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]], as well as in loan spells for [[East Craigie F.C.|East Craigie]], [[Peterhead F.C.|Peterhead]], [[Edinburgh City F.C.|Edinburgh City]] and [[Broughty Athletic F.C.|Broughty Athletic]].

== Career ==
In October 2020, Wilkie made his debut for [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] in a [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage match against [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]], coming off the bench late on in a 3–0 win.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Dundee v Cove Rangers|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54889403|access-date=2021-10-18}}</ref>

In June 2021, Wilkie signed his first professional contract with Dundee.<ref>{{Cite web|title=@jackwilkie15 on Instagram|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/CQBIqDuMJwo/|access-date=2021-10-19|website=www.instagram.com}}</ref> In August, Wilkie joined [[Midlands Football League|Midlands League]] side [[East Craigie F.C.|East Craigie]] on loan. He scored his first goal for the ''Shipbuilders'' in a [[Scottish Junior Cup]] match against [[Banchory St Ternan F.C.|Banchory St Ternan]], and would be named Man of the Match in the 7–2 win.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Brave fight as Banchory St Ternan exit Scottish Junior Cup|url=https://www.deesidepiper.co.uk/sport/football/brave-fight-as-banchory-st-ternan-exit-scottish-junior-cup-3401882|access-date=2021-10-18|website=www.deesidepiper.co.uk|language=en}}</ref> In May 2022, Wilkie signed an extension with Dundee which would keep him there for another season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-05-25 |title=Development squad sign up |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/development-squad-sign-up/ |access-date=2022-06-04 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref>

In Dundee's opening competitive fixture of the [[2022–23 Dundee F.C. season|2022–23 season]], Wilkie would appear as a substitute in a [[Scottish League Cup]] win over [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Dundee v Hamilton Academical |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62107679 |access-date=2022-07-09}}</ref> On 13 August 2022, Wilkie would join [[Scottish League One]] side [[Peterhead F.C.|Peterhead]] on loan.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Loan Deals in place! {{!}} Peterhead FC |url=https://www.peterheadfc.org/2022/08/13/loan-deals-in-place/ |access-date=2022-08-13 |language=en}}</ref> Wilkie made his debut the same day away to [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Falkirk v Peterhead |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62445851 |access-date=2022-08-13}}</ref> Wilkie would grab his first goal for the ''Blue Toon'' on 25 February 2023, equalising to help Peterhead clinch a point against [[Kelty Hearts F.C.|Kelty Hearts]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Peterhead v Kelty Hearts |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64686481 |access-date=2023-02-25}}</ref> Despite Peterhead being relegated at season's end, Wilkie was named as the club's Young Player of the Year Award winner.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=8 May 2023 |title=@pfcofficial on Twitter |url=https://twitter.com/pfcofficial/status/1655487202057412608 |access-date=2023-05-09 |website=Twitter |language=en}}</ref>

On 4 August 2023, Wilkie joined [[Scottish League One]] club [[Edinburgh City F.C.|Edinburgh City]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web |last=petermceleny |date=2023-08-04 |title=Wilkie goes out on loan |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/wilkie-goes-out-on-loan/ |access-date=2023-08-04 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> The following day, Wilkie made his debut for the ''Citizens'' as an early substitution in a league game away to [[Stirling Albion F.C.|Stirling Albion]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Stirling Albion v Edinburgh City |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66194592 |access-date=2023-08-05}}</ref> Wilkie scored his first Edinburgh City goal on 7 October against [[Kelty Hearts F.C.|Kelty Hearts]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Edinburgh City v Kelty Hearts |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66969318 |access-date=2023-10-07}}</ref> After struggling with injury during his loan stint, Wilkie was recalled by Dundee on 18 January 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-18 |title=Sharp and Wilkie back from loans |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/sharp-wilkie-back/ |access-date=2024-01-18 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref>

On 9 February 2024, having played for two senior [[Scottish FA|SFA]] clubs already in the season, Wilkie joined [[Midlands Football League|Midlands League]] club and [[Scottish Junior Football Association|SJFA]] member [[Broughty Athletic F.C.|Broughty Athletic]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-09 |title=Wilkie joins Broughty Athletic on loan |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/wilkie-joins-broughty/ |access-date=2024-02-09 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=9 February 2024 |title=Broughty Athletic JFC on Facebook |url=https://www.facebook.com/Broughtyathletic/posts/pfbid0u4CTuvPfayKHpzWj1esrpMrRiAYQQizAy2kCjqQdNo93xtR9h7CpYwL71dLg1ixul |access-date=2024-02-09 |website=www.facebook.com}}</ref> Wilkie made his debut the following day, starting in a 10–0 league win away to [[Brechin Victoria F.C.|Brechin Victoria]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 February 2024 |title=Brechin Victoria F.C. v Broughty Athletic F.C. |url=https://www.scottishjuniorfa.com/result/ |access-date=2024-02-10 |website=Scottish Junior FA |language=en}}</ref> On 20 May, Dundee confirmed that Wilkie would leave at the expiry of his contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-20 |title=Squad Update 2024 |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/squad-update-2024/ |access-date=2024-05-20 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref>

On 28 May 2024, Wilkie joined [[Scottish League One]] club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cran |first=George |date=2024-05-28 |title=Former Dundee defender Jack Wilkie finds new club |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/4994162/exclusive-former-dundee-defender-jack-wilkie-finds-new-club/ |access-date=2024-05-28 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref> He made his competitive debut on 16 July in a defeat against his former club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arbroath vs Dundee: League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4ngzrxwpxzt |access-date=2024-07-16 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 28 September, Wilkie scored his first goal for the ''Red Lichties'' in an away league victory over [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cove Rangers vs Arbroath: Scottish League 1 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cr54dl32gn4t |access-date=2024-09-29 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 12 April, Wilkie won the league with Arbroath after a 4–0 home victory over [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Arbroath vs Stenhousemuir: Scottish League 1 stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/ce3v4jqxjjqt |access-date=2025-04-12 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In May 2026 following another successful season with Arbroath where the part-time side reached the [[Scottish Premiership]] play-offs, Wilkie signed with soon-to-be [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Black |first=Dave |date=2026-05-11 |title=Jack Wilkie joins the Lions |url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/jack-wilkie-joins-the-lions/ |access-date=2026-05-18 |website=Livingston FC |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Wilkie is the son of former [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] and [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] footballer [[Lee Wilkie]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hamilton |first=Sean |date=2023-08-04 |title=Dundee send starlet Jack Wilkie on loan to League One side |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/4612903/dundee-send-starlet-jack-wilkie-on-loan-to-league-one-side/ |access-date=2023-09-16 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref>

'''Oisin Smyth''' (born 5 May 2000) is a Northern Irish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://uk.soccerway.com/players/oisin-smyth/559436/|title=O. Smyth |publisher=Soccerway |access-date=2 January 2024}}</ref>

==Early and personal life==
Smyth is from [[Derrytrasna]].<ref name="auto1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.colerainechronicle.co.uk/football/2022/01/31/news/derrymacash-s-smyth-set-for-oxford-switch-21514/|title=Derrytrasna's Smyth set for Oxford switch |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220131190622/https://www.colerainechronicle.co.uk/football/2022/01/31/news/derrymacash-s-smyth-set-for-oxford-switch-21514/ |archive-date=31 January 2022 |newspaper=Coleraine Chronicle |date=31 January 2022 |access-date=2 January 2024}}</ref> His father Liam was also a footballer, active in the Irish League.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/irish-league/dungannon-swifts/dungannon-swifts-wont-let-oisin-smyth-go-on-cheap-warns-chairman-keith-boyd-41190228.html|title=Dungannon Swifts won't let Oisin Smyth go on cheap, warns chairman Keith Boyd |first=Graham |last=Luney |newspaper=Belfast Telegraph |date=29 December 2021 |access-date=2 January 2024}}</ref> His uncle [[Pat McGibbon]] was a Northern Ireland international.<ref name="auto"/>

==Club career==
Smyth began his career with [[Dungannon Swifts F.C.|Dungannon Swifts]] at the age of 12, making his senior debut in October 2018.<ref name="auto"/> He became club captain for the 2021–22 season.<ref name="auto"/>

===Oxford United===
In January 2022, Smyth signed for [[EFL League One|League One]] club [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60197373|title=Oxford United: Ciaron Brown signs on loan, Oisin Smyth and Marcus Browne make permanent moves |date=1 February 2022 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=2 January 2024}}</ref><ref name="auto1"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/irish-league/transfer-deadline-day-oisin-smyth-set-to-complete-league-one-switch-as-ronan-hale-sparks-late-battle-41295486.html|title=Transfer deadline day: Oisin Smyth set to complete League One switch as Ronan Hale sparks late battle |first=Gareth |last=Hanna |newspaper=Belfast Telegraph |date= 31 January 2022 |access-date=2 January 2024}}</ref> having been linked with a move away from Dungannon Swifts the previous month.<ref name="auto"/> On 5 January 2023, Smyth joined [[National League (division)|National League]] club [[Solihull Moors F.C.|Solihull Moors]] on an initial one-month loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.solihullmoorsfc.co.uk/news/posts/oisin-smyth-joins-on-loan/|title=Oisin Smyth Joins on Loan|publisher=Solihull Moors F.C.|date=5 January 2023|accessdate=5 January 2023}}</ref> He played three times for Solihull Moors before returning to his parent club.<ref>{{cite news |url= https://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/sport/23289870.oxford-united-boss-karl-robinson-future-midfielder-oisin-smyth/|title=Oxford United boss Karl Robinson on future of midfielder Oisin Smyth |first=Liam |last=Rice |date=31 January 2023 |newspaper=Oxford Mail |access-date=1 February 2023}}</ref>

His first goal for Oxford United, and his first in English football, was a 30-yard winner in a 2–1 away victory over [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] on 1 January 2024.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/sport/24021244.oxford-united-midfielder-oisin-smyth-winner-charlton-athletic/ |title=Oxford United midfielder Oisin Smyth on winner at Charlton Athletic |first=Liam |last=Rice |date=1 January 2024 |newspaper=Oxford Mail |access-date=2 January 2024}}</ref>

===St Mirren===
On 14 June 2024, he signed for [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/sport/24387756.oisin-smyth-signs-st-mirren-oxford-united/ |title=Oisin Smyth signs for St Mirren from Oxford United |first=Liam |last=Rice |newspaper=Oxford Mail |date=14 June 2024 |access-date=14 June 2024}}</ref> Smyth made his St Mirren debut in a [[Europa Conference League]] qualifier against Icelandic side Valur.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newsletter.co.uk/sport/football/northern-ireland/it-was-perfect-former-irish-league-ace-makes-immediate-scottish-premiership-mark-with-debut-brace-4729402|title='That's what I wanted to do when I came on...this is exactly what you want on a home league debut - it was perfect.'|date=5 August 2024|website=Belfast News Letter}}</ref> Smyth scored his first and second goal for St Mirren on his league debut for the club, in a 3–0 home win over [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on the opening day of the Scottish Premiership season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cxw2vpvmmg9t|title=St. Mirren vs Hibernian: Scottish Premiership|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle===
On [[transfer deadline day]] in September 2025, Smyth joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on a season long loan.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oisin Smyth joins Partick Thistle on loan from St Mirren |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/oisin-smyth-joins-partick-thistle-on-loan-from-st-mirren/ |access-date=1 September 2025 |website=Partick Thistle FC |language=en}}</ref> He was recalled in January 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cm2y6040r1jo|title=St Mirren recall Smyth from Partick Thistle loan|date=12 January 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> After playing two games with St Mirren in January, Smyth rejoined Thistle on loan later that month until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/oisin-smyth-returns-on-loan/|title=Oisin Smyth returns on loan|website=Partick Thistle FC}}</ref> Just five games into his return to Thistle, Smyth suffered a partial tear of the posterior cruciate ligament, which ruled him out for a significant period.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/injury-update-smyth-chalmers-and-watt/|title=Injury Update: Smyth, Chalmers and Watt|website=Partick Thistle FC}}</ref>

Smyth joined Partick Thistle permanently in June 2026, signing a two year deal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/oisin-smyth-returns-to-maryhill-on-a-two-year-deal/|title=Oisin Smyth returns to Maryhill on a two-year deal|website=Partick Thistle FC}}</ref> After returning to the club permanently, Smyth scored on his second debut, in a 6–0 home win over Brechin City in a [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage tie.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cn0vv0zzk78t|title=Partick Thistle vs Brechin City: Scottish League Cup score updates & stats|first=Live|last=Text|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

==International career==
Smyth is a [[Northern Ireland national under-21 football team|Northern Ireland under-21]] youth international.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/teams/players/250151077--oisin-smyth/|title=Oisin Smyth - Northern Ireland - U21 EURO|publisher=UEFA |access-date=2 January 2024}}</ref>
