'''Ruari Michael Paton''' (born 9 August 2000) is an Irish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)#Striker|striker]] for {{Scottish football updater|StJohnst}} club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]]. He has represented the Republic of Ireland at under-16 level.

Paton, a talented [[dance]]r, spent his youth with [[Shelbourne F.C.|Shelbourne]], [[St. Kevin's Boys F.C.|St Kevin's Boys]] and [[Belvedere F.C.|Belvedere]], before he left Ireland to join the development squad at Scottish club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]]. He spent time on loan at [[Gala Fairydean Rovers F.C.|Gala Fairydean Rovers]], before joining [[East Kilbride F.C.|East Kilbride]] in July 2019 after being released from Hibernian. His goal record in the [[Lowland Football League|Lowland League]] earned him a move to [[Stranraer F.C.|Stranraer]] in [[Scottish League Two]]. He was signed by [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] in July 2021 and played on the losing side in the [[2022 Scottish Challenge Cup final|2022 final]] of the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]]. He was named to the [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year]] following 22 [[Scottish League One]] goals in the 2022–23 season. He was sold to [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] in June 2023 and was again named on the PFA Scotland Team of the Year after scoring 17 [[Scottish Championship]] goals in the 2023–24 campaign. He was signed by English club [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]] for an undisclosed fee in July 2024 and returned to Scotland on loan at [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] in January 2025 and at St Johnstone in February 2026. He helped St Johnstone to win the [[Scottish Championship]] title at the end of the 2025–26 campaign and joined the club permanently in the summer.

==Early life==
Ruari Paton was born in [[Dublin]] on 9 August 2000.<ref name=soccerway/> He grew up in [[Carpenterstown (townland, Castleknock)|Carpenterstown]].<ref name="noodle">{{cite news |last1=McDermott |first1=Scott |title=Ruari Paton charts his Queen's Park rise via Pot Noodle dinners and dancing |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/ruari-paton-charts-queens-park-31010745 |access-date=14 July 2024 |work=Daily Record |date=24 September 2023 |language=en}}</ref> His mother came from [[Bristol]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Substack |first1=Valiant's |title=The FA Cup, celebrating fans and plans revealed |url=https://portvalethevaliant.substack.com/p/the-fa-cup-celebrating-fans-and-plans |access-date=6 December 2025 |work=Valiant's Substack |date=4 December 2025}}</ref> He was a talented [[dance]]r in his youth.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stranraerfc.org/plenty-to-celebrate-for-paton/|work=Stranraer FC|accessdate=26 July 2023|title= Plenty to celebrate for Paton|date=17 April 2021}}</ref> He gained a Higher in PE and a Sports Leadership Award from [[Ross High School, Tranent|Ross High School]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hislop |first1=John |title=Hibs' youngster Ruari Paton overcomes hurdles to gain qualifications |url=https://theedinburghreporter.co.uk/2017/08/hibs-youngster-ruari-paton-overcomes-hurdles-to-gain-qualifications/ |access-date=15 July 2024 |work=The Edinburgh Reporter |date=10 August 2017}}</ref>

==Career==
===Early career===
Paton played for [[Belvedere F.C.|Belvedere]] in Dublin before signing for [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] as a 16-year-old on a pro-youth contract.<ref>{{cite web|first=Cameron|last=Ritchie|date=2 June 2023|accessdate=26 July 2023|title=Football: Team of the Year honour for striker Ruari Paton|url=https://www.eastlothiancourier.com/sport/23560633.football-team-year-honour-striker-ruari-paton/|website=East Lothian Courier}}</ref> On 19 September 2018, he joined [[Gala Fairydean Rovers F.C.|Gala Fairydean Rovers]] of the [[Lowland Football League|Lowland League]] on [[Loan (sports)|loan]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hislop |first1=John |title=Hibs duo Patrick Martin and Ruari Paton join Gala Fairydean Rovers on loan |url=https://theedinburghreporter.co.uk/2018/09/hibs-duo-patrick-martin-and-ruari-paton-join-gala-fairydean-rovers-on-loan/ |access-date=15 July 2024 |work=The Edinburgh Reporter |date=19 September 2018}}</ref> On 22 September, he scored a hat-trick in a 6–0 win over [[Lossiemouth F.C.|Lossiemouth]] in a [[Scottish Cup]] qualification match at [[Netherdale]].<ref name=hat>{{cite news |last1=Knox |first1=David |title=Paton pounces on Scottish Cup opportunity |url=https://www.bordertelegraph.com/sport/16898388.paton-pounces-scottish-cup-opportunity/ |access-date=14 July 2024 |work=Border Telegraph |date=24 September 2018 }}</ref> He scored 13 league goals in the [[2018–19 Lowland Football League|2018–19]] season.<ref>{{cite web |title=2018/19 Lowland League Season |url=https://slfl.co.uk/archive/2018-19-lowland-league-season/ |website=Scottish Lowland League |access-date=15 July 2024}}</ref> He did not play a first-team game at [[Easter Road]] and was one of 17 players released from Hibernian in May 2019.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pilcher |first1=Ross |title=The 17 players that have left Hibs after loans and contracts ended |url=https://www.edinburghlive.co.uk/sport/football/hibs-announce-departure-17-players-16304353 |access-date=15 July 2024 |work=Edinburgh Live |date=20 May 2019 |language=en}}</ref> He later said "I went there thinking I was the man and had it all sorted out and would go to the first team. It did not work out that way and life comes around and hits you in the face."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ritchie |first1=Cameron |title=Ruari Paton out to make history in the Scottish Cup |url=https://www.eastlothiancourier.com/sport/19238232.paton-relishing-chance-face-off-ex-hibs-team-mates/ |access-date=15 July 2024 |work=East Lothian Courier |date=17 April 2021 |language=en}}</ref>

Paton failed a trial with [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] as manager [[Ian Murray (footballer)|Ian Murray]] felt he was not good enough for professional football.<ref name="noodle"/> On 3 July 2019, he signed with Lowland League champions [[East Kilbride F.C.|East Kilbride]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=McPartlin |first1=Patrick |title=Former Hibs pair snapped up by East Kilbride ahead of 2019/20 Lowland League season |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/latest-hibs-news/former-hibs-pair-snapped-up-by-east-kilbride-ahead-of-201920-lowland-league-season-544667 |access-date=14 July 2024 |work=Edinburgh News |date=3 July 2019}}</ref> Paton said that "[[Stuart Malcolm]] [East Kilbride manager] gave me a chance there when no one else would".<ref name="noodle"/> He supplemented his income playing for East Kilbride by working as a labourer on a building site.<ref name="noodle"/> He later said that "I was eating [[Pot Noodle]]s every day for dinner" due to lack of finances, but that he refused to accept returning to Ireland without having made a success of his footballing career in Scotland.<ref name="noodle"/> He scored 12 goals by November, helping the Lowland League side to reach the third round of the Scottish Cup.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Thomson |first1=Paul |title=East Kilbride striker Paton targets memorable Scottish Cup run |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/east-kilbride-striker-paton-targets-20915938 |access-date=15 July 2024 |work=Daily Record |date=20 November 2019 |language=en}}</ref> He scored 12 league goals in the [[2019–20 Lowland Football League|2019–20]] season.<ref>{{cite web |title=2019/20 Lowland League Season |url=https://slfl.co.uk/archive/2019-20-lowland-league-season/ |website=Scottish Lowland League |access-date=15 July 2024}}</ref>

===Stranraer===
Paton agreed a two-year contract with [[Stranraer F.C.|Stranraer]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/queen-south-boss-delighted-capture-24421037.amp|website=Daily Record|accessdate=26 July 2023|date=29 June 2021|first=Stephen|last=Temlett|title= Queen of the South boss delighted at capture of two attacking recruits}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eastlothiancourier.com/news/19205217.former-ross-high-pupil-ruari-paton-aiming-scottish-cup-glory/|website=East Lothian Courier|accessdate=26 July 2023|title=Former Ross High pupil Ruari Paton aiming for Scottish Cup glory|date=3 April 2021|first=Cameron|last=Ritchie}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eastlothiancourier.com/sport/19238232.paton-relishing-chance-face-off-ex-hibs-team-mates/#|website=East Lothian Courier|accessdate=26 July 2023|title= Former Hibs striker Ruari Paton keen to make Scottish Cup history|date=17 April 2021|first=Cameron|last=Ritchie}}</ref> He had caught the eye of manager [[Stephen Farrell (footballer)|Stephen Farrell]] with his goalscoring record the previous season, which had been cut short due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Paton is a Blue |url=https://stranraerfc.org/paton-is-a-blue/ |access-date=14 July 2024 |work=Stranraer FC |date=5 May 2020}}</ref> He was signed to compete with Thomas Orr for a place alongside veteran forward [[Darryl Duffy]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Darryl praises young strike duo - Stranraer FC |url=https://stranraerfc.org/darryl-praises-young-strike-duo/ |access-date=15 July 2024 |work=Stranraer FC |date=7 October 2020}}</ref> The three players ended up playing as an attacking trio.<ref>{{cite news |title=Orr praises strike partners - Stranraer FC |url=https://stranraerfc.org/orr-praises-strike-partners/ |access-date=15 July 2024 |work=Stranraer FC |date=17 December 2020}}</ref> The Blues qualified for the [[Scottish League Two]] play-offs at the end of the [[2020–21 Scottish League Two|2020–21]] season, losing to [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] at the semi-final stage. Paton scored nine goals in 30 matches at [[Stair Park]].<ref name="2020–21"/>

===Queen of the South===
On 2 July 2021, Paton signed a two-year contract with [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] in [[Dumfries]], following an undisclosed transfer fee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/new-queen-south-signing-ruari-24434844|website=Daily Record|accessdate=26 July 2023|title= New Queen of the South signing Ruari Paton "over the moon" with Palmerston move|first=Stephen|last=Temlett|date=2 July 2021}}</ref> Manager [[Allan Johnston]] said he was "a great young prospect that we all have high hopes for".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Temlett |first1=Stephen |title=Queens boss delighted at new attackers |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/queen-south-boss-delighted-capture-24421037 |access-date=14 July 2024 |work=Daily Record |date=29 June 2021 |language=en}}</ref> Paton scored his first goals for the [[Palmerston Park]] club later that month in his first two games versus [[Annan Athletic F.C.|Annan Athletic]] and [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/queen-south-new-boy-ruari-24575335|website=Daily Record|title= Queen of the South new boy Ruari Paton enjoying proving doubters wrong with two goals in two games|first=Kenny|last=McDonald|date=20 July 2021|accessdate=26 July 2023}}</ref> He scored the winning goal in the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite news |title=Scottish Challenge Cup: Queen of the South complete semi-final line-up |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/59499070 |access-date=14 July 2024 |work=BBC Sport |date=1 December 2021}}</ref> Queen of the South reached the final of the Challenge Cup at [[Excelsior Stadium]], where they [[2022 Scottish Challenge Cup final|were beaten 3–1]] by [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]].<ref name=scc>{{cite news |last1=Herrall |first1=Jack |title=SPFL Trust Trophy final: Raith Rovers 3-1 Queen of the South |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/60902630 |access-date=14 July 2024 |work=BBC Sport |date=3 April 2022}}</ref> Paton ended the [[2021–22 Queen of the South F.C. season|2021–22]] campaign with eight goals in 45 games, with three goals coming in the league.<ref name="2021–22"/> Queens were relegated from the [[Scottish Championship]] in last place.<ref>{{cite web |title=Queen of the South Standings 2021/2022 & Table |url=https://tribuna.com/en/clubs/queen-of-the-south/table/2021-2022/ |website=Tribuna.com |access-date=15 July 2024}}</ref>

Paton finished the [[2022–23 Queen of the South F.C. season|2022–23]] season with 25 goals for the Doonhamers.<ref>{{cite web|date=23 June 2023|accessdate=26 July 2023|first=Joel|last=Sked|url= https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/celtic/scottish-transfers-rangers-ace-wanted-celtic-eye-trio-plus-12-goal-midfielder-hearts-make-right-back-move-4194141|title= Scottish transfers: Rangers ace wanted, Celtic eye trio plus 12-goal midfielder, Hearts make right-back move|website=The Scotsman}}</ref> Paton finished as joint-top scorer in [[Scottish League One]], alongside [[Calum Gallagher]] of [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]], and was also named on the [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/cinch-league-1-team-of-the-season-2223|work= SPFL|accessdate=26 July 2023|title= Cinch League 1 Team Of The Season 22/23|date=15 June 2023}}</ref> Speaking in March, manager [[Marvin Bartley]] told his players to be less reliant on Paton's goalscoring ability to win games for them.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Temlett |first1=Stephen |title=Queens boss gets what he wants against Airdrie |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/queen-south-boss-gets-exactly-29386064 |access-date=14 July 2024 |work=Daily Record |date=8 March 2023 |language=en}}</ref> The team finished in fifth place, missing out on the play-offs by three points.<ref>{{cite web |title=Scottish League One Table 2022/2023 & Standings |url=https://tribuna.com/en/league/scottish-league-one/table/2022-2023/ |website=Tribuna.com |access-date=15 July 2024}}</ref>

===Queen's Park===
On 22 June 2023, Paton returned to the Scottish Championship after signing a three-year contract with [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/queen-to-queens-for-ruari-paton/#:~:text=Queen's%20Park%20have%20secured%20the,an%20indication%20of%20his%20potential.|work=Queen's Park FC|accessdate=26 July 2023|title= Queen To Queen's For Ruari Paton|date=22 June 2023}}</ref> On 25 July, Paton scored four goals in a 5–0 win over [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]] in the Scottish League Cup at [[Hampden Park]], his first professional hat-trick and four-goal haul in his career.<ref>{{cite web|title=Viaplay Cup: St Johnstone drop out while Livi & St Mirren win; Paton hits four for Queen's|date=25 July 2023|accessdate=26 July 2023|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66308564|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He was named [[List of Scottish Professional Football League monthly award winners|Scottish Championship Player of the Month]] after scoring three league goals to send [[Robin Veldman]]'s Spiders top of the table in August.<ref>{{cite news |title=Championship award for Paton {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/championship-award-for-paton |access-date=14 July 2024 |work=spfl.co.uk |date=1 September 2023}}</ref> Paton scored 25 goals in the [[2023–24 Queen's Park F.C. season|2023–24]] season and was named on the PFA Scotland Team of the Year, and was also nominated for the Player of the Year award.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Davenport |first1=Sean |title=Ruari Nominated for PFA Scotland Championship Player of the Year |url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/ruari-nominated-for-pfa-scotland-championship-player-of-the-year/ |access-date=14 July 2024 |work=Queen's Park Football Club |date=25 April 2024}}</ref> In the expectation that Paton would leave the club, manager [[Callum Davidson]] signed [[Zak Rudden]] as his replacement in July 2024.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ouakli |first1=Adam |title=NEXT UP: QUEEN'S PARK (H) |url=https://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/2024/07/30/next-up-queens-park-h/ |access-date=3 March 2025 |work=Falkirk FC |date=30 July 2024}}</ref>

===Port Vale===
On 15 July 2024, Paton signed a three-year deal with English [[EFL League Two|League Two]] club [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]] for an undisclosed "six-figure" transfer fee.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 July 2024 |title=Ruari Paton: Port Vale sign Queen's Park striker for undisclosed fee |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c9x8e8l6x6do |access-date=15 July 2024 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Ruari Paton is a Valiant |url=https://www.port-vale.co.uk/news/ruari-paton-valiant |access-date=15 July 2024 |work=Port Vale FC |date=15 July 2024 |language=en}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the Valiants in his second appearance for the club, converting a {{convert|25|yd}} [[Free kick (association football)|free kick]] in a 3–2 defeat at [[Barrow A.F.C.|Barrow]] in an [[EFL Cup]] fixture on 13 August; he was also named as [[Player of the match|man of the match]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Baggaley |first1=Mike |title=Vale in talks about player deal |url=https://portvalethevaliant.substack.com/p/vale-in-talks-about-player-deal |access-date=19 August 2024 |work=Valiant's Substack |date=14 August 2024}}</ref> Paton lost his first-team place, but marked his return to the starting eleven with the only goal of the game at [[Harrogate Town A.F.C.|Harrogate Town]] on 22 October.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Baggaley |first1=Mike |title=Vale make it four in a row |url=https://portvalethevaliant.substack.com/p/vale-make-it-four-in-a-row |access-date=23 October 2024 |work=Valiant's Substack |date=23 October 2024}}</ref> He struggled for league starts for the Valiants under [[Darren Moore]], however, and returned to Scotland on loan at [[Scottish Premiership|Premiership]] club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] on 20 January 2025 after manager [[Jim Goodwin]] looked to bolster his attacking line.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Temple |first1=Alan |title=Ruari Paton set for Dundee United as Jim Goodwin moves to strengthen attack |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/5164521/ruari-paton-dundee-united-january-transfer-window/ |access-date=19 January 2025 |work=The Courier |date=18 January 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Ruari Paton joins Dundee United on loan |url=https://www.port-vale.co.uk/news/ruari-paton-joins-dundee-united-loan |access-date=20 January 2025 |work=Port Vale FC |date=20 January 2025 |language=en}}</ref> He made his debut for the "Tangerines" later that day in the [[Dundee derby]] and "was denied a debut goal by an outstanding [[Ethan Ingram]] block" as United lost 1–0 at [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=O'Neill |first1=George |title=Dundee end wait for derby win to knock Dundee United out of Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cjdenj593znt#Report |access-date=20 January 2025 |work=BBC Sport |date=20 January 2025}}</ref> He played a total of 13 games for Dundee United.<ref name=2024-25/>

On 22 July 2025, Paton became the first player to score against [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] at the new [[Everton Stadium]] in a pre-season friendly defeat.<ref>{{cite news |title=Match Report {{!}} Everton 2-1 Port Vale |url=https://www.port-vale.co.uk/news/match-report-everton-2-1-port-vale |access-date=22 July 2025 |work=Port Vale FC |date=22 July 2025 |language=en}}</ref> He missed the first month of the [[2025–26 Port Vale F.C. season|2025–26]] season, however, after tweaking a hip muscle.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Baggaley |first1=Mike |title=Vale impress in home opener |url=https://portvalethevaliant.substack.com/p/vale-impress-in-home-opener |access-date=8 August 2025 |work=Valiant's Substack |date=8 August 2025}}</ref> His goal at [[Exeter City F.C.|Exeter City]] on 13 September was his first in the EFL since October, and he said after the match he was aiming to give the manager no choice but to play him.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Harby |first1=Chris |last2=Bowers |first2=Phil |title=Ruari Paton: Port Vale striker wants to become undroppable |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/crkj24d4m1ro |access-date=15 September 2025 |work=BBC Sport |date=15 September 2025}}</ref> Paton was named on that week's League One Team of the Week.<ref>{{Cite tweet |user=SkyBetLeagueOne |number=1967599801379545322 |title=✨ It's time for your @WhoScored #SkyBetLeagueOne Team of the Week #EFL}}</ref>

===St Johnstone===
On 2 February 2026, Paton joined Scottish Championship leaders [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on loan until the end of the [[2025–26 St Johnstone F.C. season|2025–26]] season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ruari Paton loaned to St. Johnstone |url=https://www.port-vale.co.uk/news/ruari-paton-loaned-st-johnstone |access-date=3 February 2026 |work=Port Vale FC |date=2 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref> He said he felt "pure excitement" at joining the promotion push at [[McDiarmid Park]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nicolson |first1=Eric |title=Ruari Paton: St Johnstone deadline day signing has 'pure excitement' for Perth move |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/5424234/ruari-paton-st-johnstone-port-vale-confirmed/ |access-date=3 February 2026 |work=The Courier |date=2 February 2026}}</ref> He scored on his debut at [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] 11 days later to extend the Saints lead at the top of the table.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ruari Paton fires St Johnstone to victory at Airdrieonians with debut goal |url=https://www.irishnews.com/sport/soccer/ruari-paton-fires-st-johnstone-to-victory-at-airdrieonians-with-debut-goal-M54DO5JU6RKWLHJC3ZDMWRY6TM/ |access-date=14 February 2026 |work=The Irish News |date=13 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref> On 21 April, he scored the second goal of a 2–0 victory at [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] that confirmed St Johnstone as champions of the Championship.<ref name="c26">{{cite news |title=St Johnstone win Scottish Championship title with win at Dunfermline |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cwyk22wd9y0t |access-date=22 April 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref> He returned to [[Vale Park]] to find himself transfer listed,<ref>{{cite news |title=Port Vale FC Retained List 2026 confirmed |url=https://www.port-vale.co.uk/news/port-vale-fc-retained-list-2026-confirmed |access-date=5 May 2026| date=5 May 2026 |work=Port Vale FC |language=en}}</ref> and joined St Johnstone for an undisclosed fee on 25 June.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ruari Paton signs for Saints! |url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/ruari-paton-signs-for-saints/ |access-date=25 June 2026 |work=St Johnstone FC |date=25 June 2026}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Paton is a hard-working [[Forward (association football)#Striker|striker]] with an excellent goalscoring record.<ref>{{cite news |title=Boss evaluates new recruits - Stranraer FC |url=https://stranraerfc.org/boss-evaluates-new-recruits/ |access-date=15 July 2024 |work=Stranraer FC |date=5 July 2020}}</ref> He often celebrates goals by dancing.<ref>{{cite news |title=Plenty to celebrate for Paton - Stranraer FC |url=https://stranraerfc.org/plenty-to-celebrate-for-paton/ |access-date=15 July 2024 |work=Stranraer FC |date=31 December 2020}}</ref>

'''Joel Leigh Cotterill''' (born 10 October 2004) is a Welsh [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as an [[attacking midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|StJohnst}} club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]]. He is a [[Wales national under-21 football team|Wales under-21]] international.

==Career==
===Swansea City===

Cotterill is a product of the Swansea City academy which he joined aged 7 and he signed his first professional contract in June 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Joel Cotterill {{!}} Swansea |url=https://www.swanseacity.com/player/246 |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=www.swanseacity.com |language=en}}</ref>  On 9 August 2022, Cotterill made his senior debut for [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] as a second-half substitute in 2–2 loss on penalties to [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]] in the [[EFL Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carabao Cup (Sky Sports) |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/oxford-united-vs-swansea-city/teams/469507 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230829165348/https://www.skysports.com/football/oxford-united-vs-swansea-city/teams/469507 |archive-date=2023-08-29 |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=Sky Sports |language=en-GB |url-status=live }}</ref>

In August 2023, Cotterill joined [[EFL League Two]] club Stockport County for the duration of the 2023–24 season.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-08-28 |title=Joel Cotterill: Swansea City midfielder joins Stockport on season-long loan |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66640428 |access-date=2025-05-25 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Cotterill made a number of substitute appearances for Stockport, notably featuring in an 8–0 win over [[Sutton United F.C.|Sutton United]] where he scored his first senior goal,<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-12-16 |title=Stockport County 8-0 Sutton United - Leaders put eight past bottom club |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67667635 |access-date=2025-05-25 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> before being recalled in January 2024.

On 30 July 2024, Cotterill returned to League Two, joining [[Swindon Town F.C.|Swindon Town]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.swindontownfc.co.uk/news/2024/july/30/town-sign-joel-cotterill/|title=Town sign Joel Cotterill|website=www.swindontownfc.co.uk|date=30 July 2024|accessdate=31 July 2024}}</ref>

On 1 September 2025, Cotterill signed a new two-year contract with Swansea City,<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.swanseacity.com/news/joel-cotterill-signs-new-contract-and-makes-bristol-rovers-loan-move|title=Joel Cotterill signs new contract and makes Bristol Rovers loan move|website=www.swanseacity.com|date=1 September 2025|accessdate=1 September 2025}}</ref> before joining League Two club [[Bristol Rovers F.C.|Bristol Rovers]] on loan until the end of the [[2025–26 Bristol Rovers F.C. season|2025–26 season]].<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.bristolrovers.co.uk/news/bristol-rovers-secure-loan-signing-joel-cotterill|title=Bristol Rovers secure loan signing of Joel Cotterill|website=www.bristolrovers.co.uk|date=1 September 2025|accessdate=1 September 2025}}</ref> On 6 January 2026 he was recalled from his loan by Swansea City.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c5y5egqkxz7o Cotterill loan ended]</ref> 

On 14 January 2026, he joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/cotterilljoinsthedee/|title=Cotterill Joins The Dee|website=dundeefc.co.uk|date=14 January 2026|accessdate=14 January 2026}}</ref> On 25 January, Cotterill made his debut for the ''Dee'' as a substitute in a league game away to [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rangers vs Dundee: Scottish Premiership radio commentary & text updates |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cgqezldx58wt |access-date=2026-01-25 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 21 February, Cotterill scored his first Dundee goal in an away win over [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aberdeen vs Dundee: Scottish Premiership updates & match report |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c9q54w07vxlt |access-date=2026-02-22 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

=== St Johnstone ===
On 1 September 2026 Cotterill joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on a one year contract.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c2e0wgw73wlo Cotterill joins St Jognstone]</ref>

==International career==
Cotterill is a Wales international at [[Wales national under-18 football team|Under-18]],[[Wales national under-19 football team|Under-19]] and [[Wales national under-21 football team|Under-21]] level.

'''Aidan Tomas Denholm''' (born 9 November 2003) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Central Midfielder|central midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Livingst}} club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].

He has previously played on loan for clubs [[Berwick Rangers F.C.|Berwick Rangers]], [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]], and [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] while at Hearts.

== Career ==

=== Heart of Midlothian ===
Denholm was born in [[East Calder]], [[West Lothian]]<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date= |title=Birth registers |url=https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/record-results/191392730069a78f5d192f9 |website=Scotland's People |location=Edinburgh, Scotland |publisher= |access-date=25 April 2026}}</ref> and joined [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] aged eight.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 August 2023 |title=Denholm in dreamland after going from Hearts scrapheap to Euro stage |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c5143dqe2pjo |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230908154538/https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c5143dqe2pjo |archive-date=8 September 2023 |access-date=8 September 2023 |website=BBC}}</ref> Coming on as a 77th minute sub, Denholm made his professional debut in a 3–0 victory over [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]] in the [[Scottish League Cup|League Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 July 2021 |title=Hearts 3-0 Cove Rangers |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2021/07/13/scotland/league-cup/heart-of-midlothian-fc/cove-rangers-football-club/3510571/ |access-date=8 September 2023 |website=Soccerway}}</ref>

joins the Dream Team |url=https://berwickrangers.com/denholm-joins-the-dream-team/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321113616/https://berwickrangers.com/denholm-joins-the-dream-team/ |archive-date=21 March 2023 |access-date=8 September 2023 |website=Berwick Rangers}}</ref> Denholm scored his first goal for Berwick in a [[Scottish Cup]] 2–1 loss against [[Stirling Albion F.C.|Stirling Albion]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 October 2021 |title=Berwick Rangers 1-2 Stirling Albion |url=https://www.stirlingalbionfc.co.uk/berwick-rangers-1-2-stirling-albion/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220527223511/https://www.stirlingalbionfc.co.uk/berwick-rangers-1-2-stirling-albion/ |archive-date=27 May 2022 |access-date=8 September 2023 |website=Stirling Albion FC}}</ref> His loan was extended in December 2021, seeing him stay with Berwick until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 December 2021 |title=Gaffer 'delighted' as Hearts after end of loan to Berwick Rangers |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/teenage-midfielder-back-at-hearts-after-end-of-loan-to-berwick-rangers-3708706 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220813220912/https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/teenage-midfielder-back-at-hearts-after-end-of-loan-to-berwick-rangers-3708706 ====2022–23: East Fife loan====
Following a successful first half of the season with [[Heart of Midlothian F.C. Reserves and Academy|Hearts B]], Denholm joined [[Scottish League Two|League Two]] side, [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]] for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aidan Denholm Signs On Loan |url=https://eastfifefc.info/latest-news/1310-aidan-denholm-signs-on-loan |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230327062103/https://eastfifefc.info/latest-news/1310-aidan-denholm-signs-on-loan |archive-date=27 March 2023 |access-date=8 September 2023 |website=East Fife FC}}</ref> Denholm made his debut a day later in a 1–1 draw to Stirling Albion.<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 February 2023 |title=EAST FIFE VS. STIRLING ALBION 1 - 1 |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2023/02/04/scotland/third-division/east-fife-fc/stirling-albion-fc/3801421/ |access-date=8 September 2023 |website=Soccerway}}</ref> Becoming a regular feature during the second half of the season, Denholm played 15 times for East Fife in the league, who finished inside the [[2022–23 Scottish League One#League One play-offs|play-offs]]. They lost in the semi-finals to [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 May 2023 |title=Clyde 1 1 East Fife |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65514571 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230810043224/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65514571 |archive-date=10 August 2023 |access-date=8 September 2023 |website=BBC}}</ref>

====2023–24: Release and return to Hearts ====
Denholm was one of five youngsters who were released at the end of his contract after the [[2022–23 Heart of Midlothian F.C. season|2022–23 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 June 2023 |title=QUINTET TO LEAVE HEARTS |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/quintet-to-leave-hearts |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230908154731/https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/quintet-to-leave-hearts |archive-date=8 September 2023 |access-date=8 September 2023 |website=Hearts FC}}</ref> Denholm was told of his release by then Hearts manager, [[Robbie Neilson]] and began looking elsewhere. Denholm was ready to work in a bank, with his mum,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Story of Aidan Denholm and Hearts: Being released, looking for bank jobs to starring in memorable European night |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/story-of-aidan-denholm-and-hearts-being-released-looking-for-bank-jobs-to-starring-in-memorable-european-night-4261273 |access-date=8 September 2023 |website=The Scotsman |date=18 August 2023 }}</ref> before going on trial to [[English League One]] side, [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Barry |date=17 August 2023 |title=Exclusive: Aidan Denholm reveals the inside story on his Hearts exit, trial in England, call to return and European debut |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/exclusive-aidan-denholm-reveals-the-inside-story-on-his-hearts-exit-trial-in-england-call-to-return-and-european-debut-4258213 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230824081600/https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/exclusive-aidan-denholm-reveals-the-inside-story-on-his-hearts-exit-trial-in-england-call-to-return-and-european-debut-4258213 |archive-date=24 August 2023 |access-date=8 September 2023 |website=Edinburgh News}}</ref> Driving back from his trial, his old B-team manager and new Hearts [[Technical director (sports)|Technical Director]], [[Steven Naismith]], called Denholm and offered him a second chance at Hearts.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 August 2023 |title=Hearts ace Aidan Denholm on job search and what Cammy Devlin told him |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/23733010.hearts-ace-aidan-denholm-job-search-cammy-devlin-told/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230821191346/https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/23733010.hearts-ace-aidan-denholm-job-search-cammy-devlin-told/ |archive-date=21 August 2023 |access-date=8 September 2023 |website=The Herald}}</ref>

On 10 August 2023, Denholm made his [[UEFA Europa Conference League]] debut in a 2–1 loss to [[Rosenborg BK]], coming on as a 71st minute substitute for [[Cameron Devlin]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 August 2023 |title=MATCH REPORT: ROSENBORG 2-1 HEARTS |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/match-report-rosenborg-2-1-hearts |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230811051845/https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/match-report-rosenborg-2-1-hearts |archive-date=11 August 2023 |access-date=8 September 2023 |website=Hearts FC}}</ref> Three days later, Denholm made his [[Scottish Premiership]] debut for Hearts in a 0–0 draw to [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], also coming on as a substitute for Devlin.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Petrie |first=Andrew |date=13 August 2023 |title=Heart of Midlothian 0 0 Kilmarnock |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66419887 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230815032314/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66419887 |archive-date=15 August 2023 |access-date=8 September 2023 |website=BBC}}</ref>

==== 2024–25: Ross County loan ====
On 26 July 2024, Denholm would join fellow [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] on loan for the 2024–25 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Denholm joins Ross County on loan – Hearts |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/denholm-joins-ross-county-on-loan |access-date=2024-07-27 |website=www.heartsfc.co.uk |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Aidan Denholm joins on loan from Hearts |url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/aidan-denholm-joins-on-loan-from-hearts |access-date=2024-07-27 |website=RCFC |language=en}}</ref> On 4 January 2025, he was recalled by Hearts after suffering an injury in a Ross County game against [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 January 2025 |title=Aidan Denholm has returned to Hearts from his loan spell at Ross County. |url=https://bsky.app/profile/thejamtarts.bsky.social/post/3levy2bx3jc25 |access-date=4 January 2025 |website=Bluesky}}</ref>

===Livingston===
On 26 July 2025, Denholm signed for fellow Scottish Premiership club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on a three-year deal.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/squad-update-aidan-denholm/|title=Squad Update {{!}} Aidan Denholm|website=livingstonfc.co.uk|date=26 July 2025|accessdate=28 July 2025}}</ref> He picked up a hamstring injury during his debut the following day and missed most of the 2025-26 season.<ref> {{cite web|url= https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/premiership-boss-responsibility-star-signed-hearts-suffers-gutting-debut-injury-blow-5243806 |title= Premiership boss takes responsibility after star signed from Hearts suffers gutting debut injury blow |website=Edinburgh Evening News|date=27 July 2025|accessdate=2 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Livingston v St Mirren: Team news |url=https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/livingston-v-st-mirren-team-185515034.html |website=AOL |access-date=27 February 2026}}</ref>

'''Emmanuel Danso''' (born 10 November 2000) is a Ghanaian professional footballer who plays as a central midfielder for [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].

==Career==
In February 2019, Danso joined French club [[Olympique Lyonnais]] from Ghanaian lower-tier side SC Accra.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 February 2019 |title=Ghanaian youngster Emmanuel Danso completes Olympique Lyon move |url=https://www.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/SportsArchive/Ghanaian-youngster-Emmanuel-Danso-completes-Olympique-Lyon-move-719891 |access-date=7 October 2023 |website=GhanaWeb}}</ref> In August 2022, he joined Norwegian club [[Strømsgodset Toppfotball|Stromsgodset]] signing a two-and-a-half-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nilsen |first=Jostein |date=2022-08-03 |title= Klar for Godset: – Ser veldig spennende ut |url=https://www.dt.no/5-57-1955535 |url-access=subscription |access-date=2023-10-07 |website=Drammens Tidende |language=no}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=4 August 2022 |title=Ghanaian midfielder Emmanuel Danso joins Norwegian club Stromsgodset |url=https://ghanasoccernet.com/ghanaian-midfielder-emmanuel-danso-joins-norwegian-club-stromsgodset |access-date=7 October 2023 |website=Ghanasoccernet}}</ref> He made his professional debut with [[Strømsgodset Toppfotball|Strømsgodset]] in a 6–0 Eliteserien win over Jerv on 21 August 2022, as a second-half substitute for [[Johan Hove]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nilsen |first=Jostein |date=21 August 2022 |title=SIF avslutter Elvefestivalen mot bunnlag |url=https://www.dt.no/5-57-1965426 |access-date=7 October 2023 |website=Drammens Tidende |language=no}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-09-18 |title=Hove-dobbel stoppet Godsets tapsrekke: – Godt etter en tøff periode |url=https://www.dagsavisen.no/sport/2022/09/18/hove-dobbel-stoppet-godsets-tapsrekke/ |access-date=2023-10-07 |website=Dagsavisen |language=no}}</ref>

Having fulfilled a one-year contract with [[Stabæk Fotball|Stabæk]], Danso was linked with a move to Scottish side [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] in December 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 December 2025 |title=EXCLUSIVE: Emmanuel Danso set to join Scottish Premiership side Livingston FC |url=https://www.flashscore.com/news/soccer-premiership-exclusive-emmanuel-danso-set-to-join-scottish-premiership-side-livingston-fc/8pMSnLOh/|website=flashscore.com}}</ref> The move was finalized on 24 December, effective from 1 January 2026, on a contract lasting until June 2029.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/squad-update-welcome-emmanuel-danso/|title=Squad Update : Welcome Emmanuel Danso|date=24 December 2025|publisher=Livingston F.C.|access-date=24 December 2025}}</ref>

'''Macaulay John Tait''' (born 27 August 2005) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|StJohnst}} club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date=17 July 2026 |title=Macaulay Tait signs for Saints!
 |url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/macaulay-tait-signs-for-saints/ |website=St Johnstone F.C. |location=Perth, Scotland |publisher= |access-date=17 July 2026}}</ref>

==Career==
Tait began his career with Arniston Rangers YFC before moving on to Lochend Boys Club, where he was scouted and joined [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] aged eight; before joining [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]]'s academy.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/inside-story-on-hearts-macaulay-tait-the-scout-who-discovered-him-celtic-link-and-the-billy-gilmour-quality-4472412| title=Inside story on Hearts' Macaulay Tait| work=[[Edinburgh Evening News]] | date=10 January 2024 | accessdate=11 March 2024}}</ref> He signed a two-year deal with the club in April 2023 having impressed for the reserve side in the [[Lowland Football League]], whom he captained.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.edinburghlive.co.uk/sport/hearts-tie-down-macaulay-tait-26791873| title=Hearts tie down Macaulay Tait as he makes 'next level' admission over Lowland League challenge| work=Edinburgh Live | date=27 April 2023 | accessdate=11 March 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/23484614.steven-naismith-bigs-peter-harings-midfield-role-hearts-squad/| title=Steven Naismith bigs up Peter Haring's midfield role in Hearts squad| work=[[The Herald (Glasgow)|The Herald]] | date=27 April 2023 | accessdate=11 March 2024}}</ref>

Having made his debut in December 2023,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/5-scottish-premiership-teenage-talents-32228690| title=5 Scottish Premiership teenage talents everyone will want| work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]] | date=28 February 2024 | accessdate=11 March 2024}}</ref> he signed a new four-year deal in February 2024.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/tait-pens-long-term-deal| title=Tait Pens Long Term Deal| work=[[Heart of Midlothian F.C.]] | date=9 February 2024 | accessdate=11 March 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/macaulay-tait-signs-a-new-long-term-deal-at-hearts-with-the-promise-of-more-to-come-4512690| title=Macaulay Tait signs a new long-term deal at Hearts with the promise of more to come| work=[[Edinburgh Evening News]] | date=9 February 2024 | accessdate=11 March 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c72gzn77z57o| title=Tait signs long-term Hearts deal| work=[[BBC Sport]] | date=9 February 2024 | accessdate=11 March 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/pages/macaulay-tait| title=MACAULAY TAIT| work=[[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] | accessdate=11 March 2024}}</ref>

On 24 January 2025, Tait joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/welcome-macaulay-tait/|title=Welcome, Macaulay Tait!|website=livingstonfc.co.uk|date=24 January 2025|accessdate=24 January 2025}}</ref> Tait featured 23 times for Livingston, helping them to a second-placed finish in the [[2024–25 Scottish Championship|Championship]].<ref name=Loanmove /> Livingston would go on to play-off success, with Tait playing in both the semi-final and final victories, which secured promotion back to the Premiership.<ref name=Loanmove />

On 27 June 2025, Hearts announced that Tait had re-joined Livingston on a season-long loan.<ref name=Loanmove>{{cite web |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/taits-livi-loan-1|title=Taits Livi Loan|work=heartsfc.co.uk|publisher=[[Heart of Midlothian F.C.]] |date=27 June 2025 |accessdate=27 June 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/livingston-deal-for-hearts-midfielder-macaulay-tait-including-a-key-clause-5199256|title=Livingston deal for Hearts midfielder Macaulay Tait - including a key clause|work=.edinburghnews.scotsman.com|publisher=[[Edinburgh Evening News]] |date=27 June 2025 |accessdate=27 June 2025}}</ref>

'''Babacar Fati''' (born 1 February 2000) is a professional [[association football|football]] player who plays as a [[left-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|Livingst}} club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]]. Born in Portugal, he represents the [[Guinea-Bissau national football team|Guinea-Bissau national team]].

==Club career==
Fati started football in the youth sector of [[C.F. Os Unidos|Unidos de Lisboa]], and later joined the youth academy of [[Sporting CP]], and made his senior debut with the reserve team [[Sporting CP B]] in 2020.<ref>[https://maisfutebol.iol.pt/sub-19/lesao/sporting-terminou-a-epoca-para-babacar-fati Júnior do Sporting operado a fratura de uma vértebra cervical], maisfutebol, 5 May 2019</ref><ref>[https://www.record.pt/futebol/futebol-nacional/liga-betclic/sporting/detalhe/20191029-1521-silas-chama-babacar-fati-e-loide-augusto Silas chama Babacar Fati e Loide Augusto], record.pt, 27 October 2019</ref>

On 16 August 2022, Fati moved to Finland after signing with [[SJK Seinäjoki]] in [[Veikkausliiga]].<ref>[https://sjk.fi/uutiset/tervetuloa-babacar-fati/ Tervetuloa Babacar Fati!], sjk.fi, 16 August 2022</ref><ref>[https://www.record.pt/futebol/futebol-nacional/liga-betclic/sporting/detalhe/babacar-fati-ruma-ao-sjk-da-finlandia Babacar Fati ruma ao SJK da Finlândia], record.pt, 16 August 2022</ref><ref>[https://ilkkapohjalainen.fi/urheilu/sjk-akatemian-huippukausi-johti-erikoiseen-tilanteeseen-säännöt-muuttumassa-ensi-kaudeksi SJK Akatemian huippukausi johti erikoiseen tilanteeseen – Säännöt muuttumassa ensi kaudeksi], Ilkka-Pohjalainen, 12 October 2023</ref> Initially, he featured for both the first team and the reserve team [[SJK Akatemia]]. On 26 March 2024, his deal with SJK was extended until the end of 2025, with an option for 2026.<ref>[https://sjk.fi/uutiset/babacar-fatille-pitka-jatkosopimus/ Babacar Fatille pitkä jatkosopimus], sjk.fi, 26 March 2024</ref>

On 19 January 2026, Fati moved to Scotland, joining [[Scottish Premiership|Premiership]] club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on a contract until June 2029 for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=19 January 2026 |title=Babacar Fati joins the Lions |url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/squad-update-babacar-fati-joins-the-lions/ |access-date=20 January 2026 |publisher=[[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==
On 13 March 2025, Fati received his first call-up to the [[Guinea-Bissau national football team|Guinea-Bissau national team]], for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification – CAF Group A|2026 FIFA World Cup qualification]] matches against [[Sierra Leone national football team|Sierra Leone]] and [[Burkina Faso national football team|Burkina Faso]].<ref>[https://www.cafonline.com/news/guinea-bissau-name-four-new-players-in-squad-for-fifa-world-cup-qualifiers/ Guinea Bissau name four new players in squad for FIFA World Cup qualifiers], cafonline.com, 13 March 2025</ref> He made his international debut on 20 March, in a match against Sierra Leone.

==Personal life==
Fati is of [[Afro-Portuguese people|Bissau-Guinean]] descent. His cousin Vítor Fati plays football for [[A.D. Camacha|Camacha]].

'''Lewis Budinauckas''' (born 19 June 2002) is a Scottish [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].

==Career==

===Rangers===
Budinauckas signed a professional deal with [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] after coming through the clubs youth ranks. Initially joining up with the Rangers B side. <ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/rangers-mcgregor-butland-budinauckas-scotland-33882799.amp | title=Rising Rangers star plots route to being next Allan McGregor | date=14 October 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.rangersreview.co.uk/news/23435376.lewis-budinauckas-rangers-b-red-card-celtic-overturned/ | title=Lewis Budinauckas Rangers B red card against Celtic overturned after appeal | date=4 April 2023 }}</ref>

====Loan spells====
Bundinauckas has had numerous loan spells away from Rangers. Initially joining Civil Service Strollers, before joining Scottish Championship side Raith Rovers on an emergency loan in 2022.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.raithrovers.net/goalkeeper-signs/ | title=Goalkeeper signs | date=24 March 2022 }}</ref>

In 2024 Bundinauckas joined Scottish Championship side Greenock Morton on an emergency loan.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://gmfc.net/lewis-budinauckas-joins-on-an-emergency-loan/ | title=Lewis Budinauckas joins on an emergency loan - Greenock Morton FC | date=26 October 2024 }}</ref>

In February 2025 Bundinauckas followed in his father [[Kevin Budinauckas|Kevin’s]] footsteps as he joined Scottish Championship club Partick Thistle on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/lewis-budinauckas-joins-on-loans-from-rangers/ | title=Lewis Budinauckas joins on loans from Rangers }}</ref>

===Partick Thistle===
Following his loan spell with the club, Budinauckas joined [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] permanently in June 2025, on a one year deal, with an option for a further year.<ref>https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/bud-is-back/</ref>

'''Brooklyn Lukongola Kabongolo''' (born 16 October 2002) is a French professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|Livingst}} club  [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].

==Club career==
Kabongolo came through the youth academy at [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]], but left the club without making a single first team appearance. After his exit from [[Portman Road]], Kabongolo signed for [[Billericay Town F.C.|Billericay Town]] in 2023.<ref>https://www.billericaytownfc.co.uk/latest-signings/</ref> Some impressive performances led to the opportunity to sign for [[Southend United F.C.|Southend United]].<ref>{{ cite web| url=https://www.echo-news.co.uk/sport/23828470.billericay-town-boss-brooklyn-kabongolos-move-southend-united/| title=Billericay Town boss on Brooklyn Kabongolo's move to Southend United| date=2 October 2023| publisher=Echo News}}</ref>

He signed for [[Southend United F.C.|Southend United]] for the second half of the 2023-2024 season.  The defender made 13 league appearances for the Shrimpers before deciding to leave the club in February 2024 after failing to agree a new deal.<ref>{{ cite web| url=https://www.phoenixfm.com/2024/02/07/kabongolo-leaves-southend/| title=Brooklyn Kabongolo leaves Southend United| date=7 February 2024| publisher=Phoenix FM}}</ref><ref>{{ cite web| url=https://www.echo-news.co.uk/sport/24106624.southend-united-boss-kevin-maher-explains-brooklyn-kabongolos-exit/| title=Southend United boss Kevin Maher explains Brooklyn Kabongolo's exit| date=8 February 2024| publisher=Echo News}}</ref>

He signed for [[Oxford City F.C.|Oxford City]] in July 2024.  After making 9 first team appearances for the club, he was on the move again when he signed for [[Aveley F.C.|Aveley]] in October 2024.<ref>{{ cite web| url=https://thurrock.nub.news/sports/football/aveley-sign-brooklyn-kabongolo-5017| title=Aveley sign Brooklyn Kabongolo| date=4 October 2024| publisher=Thurrock Nub News}}</ref>

Kabongolo's good form earned him a move to Scottish side [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] in July 2025, signing a two year deal with the [[West Lothian]] club.<ref>{{ cite web| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cn9yex1zjrpo| title=Defender Kabongolo joins Livi on two-year deal| date=10 July 2025| publisher=BBC}}</ref>

In October 2025, he joined [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] on loan until the end of the [[2025–26 Livingston F.C. season|2025–26]] season.<ref>{{ cite web| url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/squad-update-kabongolo-joins-arbroath-on-loan/| title=Kabongolo joins Arbroath| date=1 October 2025| publisher=Livingston F.C.}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Kabongolo is of French and Congolese heritage.<ref>{{ cite web| url=https://africasoccer.com/french-congolese-defender-brooklyn-lukongolo-kabongolo-makes-major-career-move-to-livingston/| title=French-Congolese defender Brooklyn Lukongolo Kabongolo makes major career move to Livingston| date=17 July 2025| publisher=Africa Soccer}}</ref>

'''Unax Álvarez de Eulate Oyanguren''' (born 26 February 2002) is a Spanish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] for [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]]. 

==Early life==
Álvarez was born on 26 February 2002 and raised in [[Vitoria-Gasteiz]], Spain.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.elcorreo.com/deportes/futbol/tercera-rfef/unax-alvarez-portugalete-20230207104312-nt.html|title=Unax: "En los entrenamientos se nota mejoría, ahora tenemos que trasladarlo al campo"|trans-title=Unax: "We've noticed improvement in training, now we have to translate that to the pitch"|language=es|publisher=[[El Correo]]|date=7 February 2023|access-date=20 June 2026}}</ref> He spent time in the youth academy of [[Deportivo Alavés]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/5519629/st-johnstone-who-is-unax-alvarez/|title=Who is Unax Alvarez and have St Johnstone signed a Spanish Josh McPake?|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[The Courier (Dundee)|The Courier]]|date=18 June 2026|access-date=20 June 2026|last=Nicolson|first=Eric}}</ref>

== Career ==
Álvarez played for [[Tercera Federación]] team [[Club San Ignacio|San Ignacio]] in his hometown of Vitoria-Gasteiz, scoring eight goals in 33 appearances during the [[2021–22 Tercera División RFEF|2021–22 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Olazabal |first=Peru |date=20 January 2023 |title=Unax Álvarez llega cedido al Portugalete |url=https://www.elcorreo.com/deportes/futbol/tercera-rfef/unax-alvarez-llega-20230120132333-nt.html |access-date=20 June 2026 |publisher=[[El Correo]] |language=es}}</ref> 

During the summer of 2022, Álvarez signed for [[Deportivo Alavés B]], the reserve team for [[La Liga]] side Deportivo Alavés, where he played in the [[Segunda Federación]] and scored one goal. In early 2023, he was loaned to [[Club Portugalete|Portugalete]] as he felt he was not getting enough minutes with Alavés B.<ref name=":0" /> 

In 2023, he signed for [[CD Toledo]] in the [[CD Toledo|Tercera Federación]].<ref name=":1" /> 

In 2024, Álvarez signed for [[CD Guadalajara (Spain)|CD Guadalajara]] of the [[Primera Federación]]. After two seasons, it was announced that he would depart the club.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nicolson |first=Eric |date=17 June 2026 |title=St Johnstone sign goalscoring Spanish winger Unax Alvarez |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/5519185/st-johnstone-unax-alvarez-spian-sign/ |access-date=20 June 2026 |publisher=[[The Courier (Dundee)|The Courier]] |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In June 2026, Álvarez signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on a two year deal, subject to work permit.<ref>{{Cite web |date=17 June 2026 |title=Unax Álvarez de Eulate signs for Saints! |url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/unax-alvarez-de-eulate-signs-for-saints/ |access-date=20 June 2026 |website=www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk |language=en-GB}}</ref>
